a_rows_sample.anchor: The Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) extends First-Degree Entailment (FDE / Belnap-Dunn 4-valued logic) to eliminate the structural distinction collapses identified in prior kernel evaluations ... ABK-1 resolves these deficiencies by embedding the standard 4-valued truth space BF_4 into an Annotated Bilattice Frame B_ABK. Each proposition is represented as an annotated truth tuple that pairs an FDE valuation with a justification graph, a temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ABK-1: an architecture that embeds standard 4-valued FDE (BF_4) into an Annotated Bilattice Frame, pairing each proposition's FDE valuation with a justification graph, temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata, explicitly targeting the lineage/temporal/underdetermined collapses previously measured against bare FDE (this batch's r-req-fde-kernel-test-vectors-result).

a_rows_sample.anchor: State(phi) = <nu(phi), J(phi), tau(phi), mu(phi)> ... FDE Truth Valuation nu in BF_4 ... Justification Graph J = <V_J, E_J, m> ... Temporal Validity Window tau = <t_start, t_end, v_D, TTL> ... Modal and Boundary Metadata mu = <Type, Modality, ScopeMask>
a_rows_sample.statement: Formal definition of the ABK-1 state 4-tuple State(phi)=<nu,J,tau,mu>: nu is the FDE truth valuation in the powerset of {T,F}; J=<V_J,E_J,m> is a justification DAG (premise nodes, derivation edges, justification mode in {Evidenced,Inferred,Reported,Assumed}); tau=<t_start,t_end,v_D,TTL> is a temporal validity window with a dependency version vector; mu=<Type,Modality,ScopeMask> carries Analytic/Synthetic, Necessary/Contingent, and a scope bitmask.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Order (<=_k): S1 <=_k S2 iff (nu1 subseteq nu2) and (J1 sqsubseteq_DAG J2) ... Truth Order (<=_t): S1 <=_t S2 iff (T in nu1 implies T in nu2) and (F in nu2 implies F in nu1) ... Conjunction (x_t) ... Disjunction (+_t) ... combining FDE valuation, justification-DAG union, temporal intersection, and metadata AND (mu1 (dot) mu2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ABK-1's algebraic lattice structure over B_ABK = BF_4 x J x T x M: a Knowledge Order (<=_k, comparing valuation-subset and DAG-substructure) and a Truth Order (<=_t, standard FDE truth ordering), plus lattice conjunction and disjunction operators that combine FDE valuations via standard FDE meet/join, union justification DAGs, intersect temporal validity windows, and combine modal metadata via a metadata-AND operator.

type_signature.codomain: boolean order relations, or a combined ABK-1 state

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suite 1.2 Underdetermined vs. Unknown | FAIL | PASS (via J.nodes.length > 0) | PASS ... Suite 2.1 Inferred vs. Assumed | FAIL | PASS (via J.mode) | PASS ... Suite 3.1 Stale vs. Expired | FAIL | PASS (via tau.tEnd and v_D) | PASS ... The Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) achieves a 100% Pass Rate across all Tier P1 and Tier P2 distinction verification suites, qualifying it for ratification as a fully R_req-compliant KnowledgeOS kernel engine.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that ABK-1, re-run against the SPEC-RREQ-TEST-2026-V1 suite, converts all three of the bare-FDE test failures found earlier in this batch (Underdetermined-vs-Unknown via presence of justification-graph nodes; Inferred-vs-Assumed via J.mode; Stale-vs-Expired via temporal window and dependency-version comparison) into PASSes, alongside the two bare-FDE PASSes it retains (Contradiction-vs-Unknown; Absence-vs-Evidence-of-Absence), yielding a claimed 100% pass rate across Tier P1/P2 and a recommendation to ratify ABK-1 as R_req-compliant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: export class ABKState { public val: FDEValue; public justification: JustificationGraph; public temporal: TemporalWindow; public metadata: ModalMetadata; ... resolveKnowledgeStatus(currentTime, upstreamVersions): KnowledgeStatus { if (this.resolveCurrency(...) === 'Expired') return 'NotAssessed'; switch(this.val) { case 'B': return 'Contradictory'; ... case 'N': { if (this.justification.nodes.length > 0) return 'Underdetermined'; return 'Unknown'; } } }
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a full TypeScript reference implementation of ABK-1: an ABKState class carrying val/justification/temporal/metadata fields with resolveKnowledgeStatus (currency-checks first, then value-switches, distinguishing Underdetermined from Unknown by non-empty justification nodes), resolveCurrency (Expired if past tEnd, Stale if any dependency version has advanced, else Current), and resolveJustificationMode methods; and an ABKAlgebra class with a hard-coded FDE conjunction truth table and a meet() operation merging justification DAGs (node/edge union), temporal windows (intersection), and metadata (conjunctive AND, scope-mask bitwise AND).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architectural Specification: ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Interface (ABK-CONTR-INT-v1) ... The Contr Isolation Module operates directly on top of the Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) to handle non-explosion, contradiction trap frames, and resolution state tracking for paraconsistent evaluations. ... When an inbound assertion or lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu(phi)=B), the ABK-1 engine delegates contradiction containment to ABKContrBridge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a bridge architecture (SPEC-ABK-CONTR-2026-V1) between ABK-1 and a Contr contradiction-isolation engine: whenever an ABK-1 lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu=B), the engine delegates containment to an ABKContrBridge that traps the state in a local frame, sets ResolutionStatus=Unresolved, and initializes an evidential polarity edge graph, ensuring downstream inference cannot propagate the contradiction beyond a bounded contextual scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: export interface IABKContrBridge { shouldIsolate(state): boolean; isolateContradiction(...): ContrIsolationPayload; updateResolutionStatus(...): ContradictionTrapFrame; evaluateResolution(frameId): ABKState; } ... evaluateResolution ... if (totalWeight > 0.5) { resolvedVal='T'; resolution='Resolved'; } else if (totalWeight < -0.5) { resolvedVal='F'; resolution='Resolved'; } else { resolvedVal='B'; resolution='Irresolvable'; }
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the IABKContrBridge TypeScript interface (shouldIsolate, isolateContradiction, updateResolutionStatus, evaluateResolution) and its ABKContrBridge implementation: contradiction resolution sums signed evidential-polarity weights across conflicting sources and resolves to True (Resolved) if the sum exceeds +0.5, False (Resolved) if below -0.5, or remains contradictory (Irresolvable) if the weights are near-balanced -- a simple threshold-based weighted-voting resolution rule for the contradiction lifecycle.

type_signature.domain: a contradiction trap frame with polarity-weighted evidence edges
type_signature.codomain: a resolved (or still-contradictory) ABKState plus a ResolutionStatus

a_rows_sample.anchor: describe('ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Integration Suite' ... it('should detect contradictory valuations (B) and trigger isolation' ... it('should mark frame as Irresolvable when evidence weights cancel out' ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a runnable Jest end-to-end integration test suite (abk-contr-integration.test.ts) covering contradiction detection and trap-frame creation, non-explosion verification (an isolated contradictory proposition does not pollute an unrelated proposition's algebra), and resolution-lifecycle management (transition through InProgress/Resolved, resolving to True when positive evidence dominates, and remaining Irresolvable when weights cancel).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Documents: RREQ-SPEC-v1.0, ABK-1-SPEC-v1.0, ABK-CONTR-v1.0 ... The Governing Insight: R_req is the semantic contract. ABK-1 is the implementation vehicle. ABK-1 achieves 100% compliance across all Tier P1 and P2 distinctions. The Contr Bridge provides non-explosive contradiction isolation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executive summary frames the package's governing insight: R_req is the semantic contract, ABK-1 is the implementation vehicle achieving claimed 100% compliance across Tier P1/P2, and the Contr Bridge provides non-explosive contradiction isolation -- packaging three previously-separate documents (R_req, ABK-1, ABK-Contr) plus a test-verification document for joint ratification.

a_rows_sample.statement: Grades each component of the proposed EVal=<nu,J,tau,mu> tuple by separate epistemic status: nu (strong candidate), J (strong candidate), tau (candidate), mu (candidate), with the product tuple itself as the canonical EVal rated OPEN; states EVal is not merely a tuple of everything useful -- each component must be shown semantically necessary for the declared evaluation questions, or the exercise degenerates into constructing a database schema rather than deriving a kernel.

So: ABK-1 representation: CLOSED as a validated candidate. ABK-1 kernel: NOT CLOSED. This distinction is extremely important.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the scope of ABK-1's six-test PASS result: it proves ABK-1 is adequate for the TESTED R_req distinctions, not that 'ABK-1 is the KnowledgeOS kernel' -- ABK-1-as-representation is CLOSED as a validated candidate, but ABK-1-as-kernel remains NOT CLOSED, a distinction judged extremely important.

a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Executable Adequacy EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) as a proposed missing formal relation between representation-adequacy theory and kernel theory: the representation K and operations O together must be able to answer the required questions Q while preserving every required distinction AND producing an auditable transition; without EA, a representation (e.g. ABK-1) could be perfectly Adequate(R,Q,Gamma) while still being insufficient as a kernel.

C2 Representation Adequacy: CLOSED ... C3 ABK-1 as Representation Candidate: CLOSED (as candidate, not kernel) ... C4 Non-Explosion Principle: CLOSED (principle only).

Proposes the defensible replacement Adequacy_tested(ABK1,R_test)=1, explicitly scoped to the tested distinction set R_test rather than claiming universal Adequacy=1.0.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVal(p,R,C) -> <Standing, Boundary, Reason, Context, Provenance> ... Standing (S): dual-dimensional support pair (S+,S-) ... Constraint: S+ and S- are strictly independent (S+ != 1-S-) ... Boundary (B): {EXPLICIT, DERIVED, HYPOTHETICAL} ... Reason (Re): justification DAG/proof ... Context (C): <t,d,theta> ... Provenance (P): DAG of source attributions.
b_rows_sample.statement: SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 defines EVal(p,R,C) as a 5-tuple <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance>: Standing=(S+,S-) in R+xR+ with the explicit constraint S+ != 1-S- (ruling out scalar-complement collapse); Boundary in {EXPLICIT,DERIVED,HYPOTHETICAL} (adding a third value, HYPOTHETICAL, beyond this batch's earlier two-value Explicit/Derived); Reason as a justification DAG; Context as <timestamp,domain,threshold-parameters>; Provenance as a DAG of source attributions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: State(p) piecewise: ACCEPTED if S+(p)>=tau+ and S-(p)<tau- ; REFUTED if S+(p)<tau+ and S-(p)>=tau- ; CONTRADICTION if S+(p)>=tau+ and S-(p)>=tau- ; UNDERDETERMINED if S+(p)<tau+ and S-(p)<tau- ... Property 1 Non-Destructive Composition: EVal(p,R1 union R2,C).Standing = (S+_R1+S+_R2, S-_R1+S-_R2). No evidence combination operation is permitted to subtract or cancel out opposing support dimensions directly. Property 2 Non-Monotonicity of Standing ... Property 3 Scope Isolation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives a four-way EpistemicState (ACCEPTED, REFUTED, CONTRADICTION, UNDERDETERMINED) from Standing via context-defined thresholds tau+/tau-, and states three operational laws: Non-Destructive Composition (standings from unioned state graphs ADD rather than cancel: no combination operation may subtract opposing support dimensions), Non-Monotonicity of Standing (new evidence updates Standing without invalidating prior evaluation history), and Scope Isolation (a CONTRADICTION state in one context does not force CONTRADICTION in an orthogonal context).

b_rows_sample.anchor: SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 Compliance if it passes two core verification constraints: 1. Tuple Completeness: Querying any claim p returns all 5 fields of the evaluation tuple without null/empty dropouts on valid data. 2. Standing Independence: Injecting S- does not alter S+, proving no scalar subtraction or net collapse occurred. SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 is hereby RATIFIED as the formal Evaluation Semantics for KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues a self-contained ratification sign-off for SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 conditioned on two compliance checks (Tuple Completeness -- all 5 EVal fields always returned; Standing Independence -- injecting S- does not alter S+), declaring it 'hereby RATIFIED as the formal Evaluation Semantics for KnowledgeOS' -- the fourth self-contained ratification act in this single file, none tied to an external governance-ledger record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: tau = <tau_accept+, tau_refute-, tau_margin, omega_prov> ... d_state(E,tau) piecewise: DETERMINED_TRUE if S+>=tau_accept+ and S-<tau_refute- and (S+-S-)>=tau_margin ; DETERMINED_FALSE symmetric; DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION if S+>=tau_accept+ and S->=tau_refute- ; UNDERDETERMINED if both below threshold ; AMBIGUOUS otherwise.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the decision threshold vector tau=<tau_accept+,tau_refute-,tau_margin,omega_prov> and the piecewise d_state mapping from Standing (S+,S-) and tau into five discrete determination states (DETERMINED_TRUE, DETERMINED_FALSE, DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION, UNDERDETERMINED, AMBIGUOUS), requiring a margin of dominance |S+-S-|>=tau_margin to resolve TRUE/FALSE ambiguity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVal is NOT yet closed ... Problem 1 -- EVal has collapsed evaluation into standing ... insufficient evidence, theory incomplete, unobservable, underdetermined, epistemically inaccessible can all yield the same low-standing result. We already demonstrated that a flat value domain cannot preserve these distinctions. So: EVal != Standing -> FourState must remain a constitutional distinction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that SPEC-EVAL's threshold-based four-state derivation (ACCEPTED/REFUTED/CONTRADICTION/UNDERDETERMINED from S+/S- alone) repeats the exact kind of collapse the programme already rejected: insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness, unobservability, underdetermination, and epistemic inaccessibility can all produce the same low-standing result under this mapping. States as a constitutional distinction that EVal must not be identified with a simple Standing-to-four-state function.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document incorrectly says EVal is total ... Our previous Sat/EVal experiments found exactly the opposite problem: some evaluator classes were theory-blocked. Therefore the honest formulation is: EVal: (K,R,Q,Gamma) -> EValResult where the result may contain a typed evaluation boundary/reason explaining why evaluation cannot determine the requested property. evaluation totality is not yet established.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects SPEC-EVAL's claim that 'EVal guarantees that evaluation results are total, deterministic', citing prior Sat/EVal experiments that found some evaluator classes are theory-blocked (cannot always return a result); proposes the honest formulation EVal:(K,R,Q,Gamma)->EValResult where the result may itself be a typed evaluation boundary/reason explaining why evaluation cannot determine the requested property; states 'evaluation totality is not yet established' as the corrected status.

type_signature.codomain: EValResult, possibly itself a typed boundary/reason for non-determination

b_rows_sample.anchor: The S+, S- numerical semantics are still unjustified ... we previously rejected introducing arbitrary scalar evidence weighting into the kernel. Why? source reliability != evidence standing; evidence quality != process reliability; positive/negative support != probability; scalar weighting requires an aggregation theory; cross-frame aggregation remains unresolved ... (S+,S-) is a valid candidate representation, but the numeric semantics must remain PROP / OPEN, not constitutional fact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms a standing rejection of arbitrary scalar evidence weighting in the kernel, citing five reasons (source reliability != evidence standing; evidence quality != process reliability; positive/negative support != probability; scalar weighting requires an aggregation theory; cross-frame aggregation remains unresolved, per the composition experiments' finding that aggregation rule and frame semantics are coupled); concludes (S+,S-) is a valid candidate representation but its numeric semantics must remain PROP/OPEN, not constitutional fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: My recommendation: do NOT write Theory v1.3 yet ... the text itself has not earned those ratifications. This is exactly the kind of premature closure we have been trying to prevent. I would therefore change their status to: [RATIFICATION CANDIDATE] or [PROPOSED -- VALIDATED IN TESTED SCOPE] until the unresolved semantic issues are closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly rejects writing Theory v1.3 given the current state, and directly quotes the reviewed document's 'hereby RATIFIED' language for SPEC-CONTR and SPEC-EVAL as premature closure the programme has been trying to prevent; recommends downgrading their declared status to [RATIFICATION CANDIDATE] or [PROPOSED -- VALIDATED IN TESTED SCOPE] until the unresolved semantic issues identified in this review are closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P1 Contr: Contradiction != False/Unknown/Underdetermined CLOSED; FDE S+ and S- as representation CLOSED; five contradiction types identified CLOSED; Numeric threshold semantics OPEN -- Unjustified; Universal isolation theorem OPEN -- Overclaimed ... P2 EVal: the 5-tuple structure CLOSED, flat-value-domain-insufficiency CLOSED, typed boundary/Reason required CLOSED; Totality/Determinism/Non-destructive claims OPEN -- Overclaimed ... P3 Standing Semantics: (S+,S-) representation and the positive/negative distinction CLOSED; numeric semantics in [0,infinity) and scalar weighting theory OPEN -- Unjustified/Unresolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally records three items as PARTIALLY CLOSED, splitting each into a closed sub-part and an open sub-part: Contr (non-identity with False/Unknown/Underdetermined, the FDE S+/S- representation, and the five-type typology are CLOSED; the specific numeric threshold semantics and any 'universal isolation theorem' remain OPEN as unjustified/overclaimed); EVal (the 5-tuple structure, the insufficiency of a flat value domain, and the requirement for a typed boundary/Reason are CLOSED; totality, determinism, and non-destructiveness claims remain OPEN as overclaimed); Standing (the (S+,S-) representation and positive/negative distinction are CLOSED; the numeric range and any scalar-weighting/aggregation theory remain OPEN).

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVal is the biggest remaining mathematical problem ... the EVal tuple <S,B,Reason,C,P> does not actually contain its own evaluation outcome. Yet later the specification defines: State(p) = {Accepted,Refuted,Contradiction,Underdetermined}. So there is a type inconsistency: EVal -> 5-tuple, but: EvaluationResult -> 5-tuple + EpistemicState. Which one is EVal?
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a genuine type inconsistency across the EVal specification: EVal is defined once as a bare 5-tuple <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance>, which does not itself contain an evaluation outcome, but the same specification separately defines a State(p) mapping into a four-value EpistemicState and an EvaluationResult data class that bundles the 5-tuple with that EpistemicState -- leaving it unresolved which of the two ('EVal' or 'EvaluationResult') is actually the object the theory means by EVal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I recommend: Eval_c(K,r,Gamma) -> EVal where: EVal = <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance,EvaluationStatus> but EvaluationStatus must not be the old four-state epistemic collapse. It needs typed boundary/reason information.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes resolving the EVal type inconsistency by extending EVal to a 6-tuple <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance,EvaluationStatus>, with the explicit constraint that EvaluationStatus must not be the old flat four-state epistemic collapse but must carry typed boundary/reason information for non-determination causes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The document's 'non-monotonicity' law is mathematically false ... EVal(p,delta(R,e),C).Standing != EVal(p,R,C).Standing ... It says adding new evidence always changes standing. Counterexample: S+(p)=5 then add irrelevant evidence about another proposition q. Standing for p should remain: S+(p)=5. Therefore the law should not be 'non-monotonicity.' The correct statement is: Evidence addition may change evaluation; it need not.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refutes the EVal specification's stated 'Non-Monotonicity of Standing' property (evidence addition to R always changes EVal's Standing for a given proposition p) with a direct counterexample: adding irrelevant evidence about an unrelated proposition q should leave p's standing S+(p) unchanged, contradicting the universal-inequality form of the stated law. Replaces it with the weaker, correct statement: evidence addition MAY change evaluation; it need not -- with the specific behavior (monotone/non-monotone/revisionary/retracting/context-sensitive) to be investigated per evidence-operator rather than asserted as a universal law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The additive Standing law is also not closed ... S+_{R1 union R2} = S+_{R1} + S+_{R2} ... That is a specific aggregation model. It assumes independent additive contribution. But we already established that: evidence may be dependent, sources may duplicate each other, frame semantics matter, aggregation rule remains underdetermined. Therefore: Standing aggregation rule = OPEN. Do not put addition into the constitutional kernel yet.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies that SPEC-EVAL's 'Non-Destructive Composition' property (Standing of a union of state graphs equals the SUM of the parts' Standings) silently assumes an independent-additive aggregation model, which conflicts with prior findings that evidence may be dependent, sources may duplicate each other, and frame semantics matter to composition; concludes the Standing aggregation rule remains OPEN and must not be hard-coded as addition in the constitutional kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would immediately downgrade: SPEC-CONTR ratification, SPEC-EVAL ratification, universal six-invariant claim, ABK-1 '100% adequacy' claim, numerical Standing semantics, additive evidence aggregation, EVal totality, universal non-monotonicity. ... We cannot close KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3 yet. But we can close the discovery phase and reduce the remaining work to five coupled closure problems.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final senior-review recommendation: immediately downgrade eight specific claims (SPEC-CONTR ratification, SPEC-EVAL ratification, the universal six-invariant claim, ABK-1's 100%-adequacy claim, numerical Standing semantics, additive evidence aggregation, EVal totality, universal non-monotonicity); concludes KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3 cannot yet be closed, but the discovery phase can be closed and the remaining work reduced to five coupled closure problems, with another broad research/literature phase judged counterproductive at this point.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Effective immediately, the KnowledgeOS status registry is revised according to the following Formal Downgrades & Corrections: 1. Downgrade Contr = FDE-B ... 2. Downgrade Universal Invariants ... 3. Correction of Circular R_req Definition ... 4. Correction of Non-Monotonicity Law ... 5. Abolition of Additive Standing Law ... 6. Isolation of Determination (Det): Added explicit bridge layer.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally enacts six corrections as immediate status-registry revisions, restating and accepting every mathematical objection raised by the preceding review: Contr-FDE identity downgraded to symptom, universal six-invariant preservation downgraded to task-bounded, R_req's circular definition corrected, the Non-Monotonicity law corrected to permissive, the additive Standing law abolished, and an explicit Det bridge layer added.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'spec-eval-2026-v1-five-tuple-standing-boundary-reason-context-provenance' POSSIBLY relates to 'abk-1-annotated-bilattice-kernel-candidate' (batch B0062). Note: A self-declared [RATIFIED] Evaluation Semantics spec defining EVal as a 5-tuple <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance>: Standing=(S+,S-) in R+xR+ with S+ != 1-S- (no scalar collapse); Boundary in {EXPLICIT,DERIVED,HYPOTHETICAL}; Reason as a justification DAG/proof; Context=<t,d,theta>; Provenance a DAG of source attributions. Derives a four-way EpistemicState (ACCEPTED/REFUTED/CONTRADICTION/UNDERDETERMINED) via threshold comparison of S+ and S- against context-defined tau+/tau-, and states three operational-law properties: Non-Destructive Composition (standings add rather than cancel across unioned state graphs), Non-Monotonicity of Standing (new evidence need not preserve prior evaluation), and Scope Isolation (contradiction in one context does not force contradiction in an orthogonal context); includes a full Python reference implementation (Standing, EvaluationResult, EvaluationEngine).

a_rows_sample.anchor: State_{Arjuna} = (K,U,N,D,E)
a_rows_sample.statement: Arjuna's problem is not purely epistemic: KnowledgeGap+UnderstandingGap+NormativeGap+ActionConflict can occur simultaneously, giving State_Arjuna=(K,U,N,D,E) where E is emotional/psychological state, modeled as a separate AffectiveState rather than folded into the Knowledge State. Suggests a DDD separation of concerns: Inquiry, Knowledge, Understanding, NormativeReasoning, Decision, Action, AffectiveContext as different concerns.

a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Actor State (Role, Capabilities, KnowledgeAccess, Authority, Purpose, Commitments, AffectiveContext), making Arjuna formally representable and establishing KnowledgeState ≠ ActorState: Action = f(Knowledge, Actor, Role, Purpose, Norms, Authority) — the same Knowledge State can produce different actions for different actors.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Actor \neq Role \neq Duty
a_rows_sample.statement: Strengthens Role's centrality (verse 35, own duty vs another's): Duty=f(Role,Context,NormativeFramework) rather than Duty=f(Actor) — a person has duties in a role under a normative context, not directly. Models Actor--holds-->Role--activates-->Duty--constrained by-->Norm as a value-object chain, giving Actor ≠ Role ≠ Duty. Warns against generalizing sva-dharma (embedded in varṇa/āśrama) carelessly into 'every software actor has a role and therefore a duty' — the valid abstraction is narrower: when a normative system assigns responsibilities by role, role-context must participate in determining applicable duties.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sense Objects \rightarrow Attachment/Desire \rightarrow Distortion \rightarrow Impaired Knowledge \rightarrow Action
a_rows_sample.statement: Retains a causal chain (Sense Objects->Attachment/Desire->Distortion->Impaired Knowledge->Action, verse 40's lust-covers-knowledge claim) showing AgentState can affect InterpretationOfKnowledge, but corrects S0807's 'AffectiveState' as too narrow, replacing it with a broader AgentCondition (cognitive condition, motivational condition, affective condition, capability, role, authority, commitments), giving Interpretation=f(Knowledge,AgentCondition,Context).

a_rows_sample.anchor: we can distinguish two Ātma concepts
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two Ātma concepts that must be given different names so they are never confused: Human/Knower Ātma 𝒜_H — the human Knower (e.g. Arjuna) who has intent, asks questions, observes, experiences uncertainty, evaluates meaning, decides, and acts, with changing knowledge state K^H_t but persistent subject; and KnowledgeOS Ātma 𝒜_K — the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS epistemic system/kernel that maintains and operates on its own knowledge states K^K_t via observation representation, evidence/provenance, dimension discovery, epistemic evaluation, Zero, coherence, state transition, investigation support.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...)
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the Knower itself as the biggest missing formally-completed piece despite 𝒜_H (Knower Ātma) being named: proposes N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...) as the needed model, motivated by the principle that two Knowers can observe the same reality and produce different Ideal States — 'not an error, a fundamental property of the system'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action = (Actor, Role, Operation, Duty, Intention, Orientation, Context, Outcome) ... ObservedAction != ActionMeaning; CanAct != ShouldAct != WillAct
a_rows_sample.statement: Expands the Action formalization from (Actor, Operation, Result) into an eight-field structure (Actor, Role, Operation, Duty, Intention, Orientation, Context, Outcome), with new invariants ObservedAction != ActionMeaning (the same observable action can carry different semantic status depending on orientation/intention/duty) and CanAct != ShouldAct != WillAct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across successive knowledge states, while its knowledge, understanding, observations, and forms may change over time.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Knowledge Ātma A_K as the persistent identity of a knowledge-bearing system across a sequence of knowledge states K_0,K_1,...,K_t, satisfying A_K(t1)=A_K(t2) while K_t1≠K_t2 in general — 'the Ātma remains invariant while the knowledge state evolves'. Explicitly NOT defined as 'all knowledge' or as the Ideal State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Knowledge Ātma}\neq K_t\neq I_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes three distinct concepts that must not collapse: Knowledge Ātma (who/what persists through knowledge-state changes), Knowledge State K_t (what is currently known/represented), Ideal State I_t (what should be known/understood/achieved for the current purpose) — Knowledge Ātma ≠ K_t ≠ I_t, called 'a very strong architectural separation'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t\subseteq\mathcal K
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a potentially unbounded Knowledge Space 𝒦 of which the current Knowledge State is only a finite/partial representation, K_t⊆𝒦; Knowledge Ātma is not 𝒦 itself but the persistent identity undertaking an 'epistemic journey' A_K --epistemic journey--> K_t⊆𝒦 across K_0->K_1->K_2->... indefinitely. Layered architecture diagram: Ātma=persistence/identity, Knowledge State=current manifestation, Zero=reveals the boundary of what is currently known, Lord=expands the possible knowledge horizon, Sārathi=navigates the transition, Knower=experiences/evaluates/decides.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural and mathematical abstraction inspired by the philosophical concept of Ātman. It is not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman described in the Bhagavad Gītā.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues an explicit disclaimer required before using the term in formal theory: Knowledge Ātma is an architectural/mathematical abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a computational representation or proof of the metaphysical Ātman — protecting the model from a category error. Notes that introducing Knowledge Ātma changes the ontology of the complete KnowledgeOS model, requiring formal distinction of identity, state, knowledge, understanding, ideal, and evolution, and recommends exploring this before Question 20.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is the persistent Knower whose identity remains invariant while its knowledge, understanding, observations, experiences, and represented states change over time.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reconciles 'Ātma = invariant identity underlying changing states' with 'Ātma = the Knower' into one definition: Ātma = the persistent Knower, invariant (A_t1=A_t2) while its knowledge state K_t changes (K_t1≠K_t2). 'Knower' names its role, 'invariant/persistent' names its mathematical property.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \underbrace{\text{Ātma}}_{\text{Who knows}} \quad \underbrace{K_t}_{\text{What is known}} \quad \underbrace{I_t}_{\text{What should be known}}
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a clean three-way separation Ātma ('who knows') / K_t ('what is known') / I_t ('what should be known'), judged much cleaner than identifying Ātma with the Knowledge State itself; repeats the caution that this is a KnowledgeOS mathematical/architectural abstraction inspired by Ātman, not a claim of having mathematically captured the metaphysical Ātman of the Gītā.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ātma is not the entire KnowledgeOS kernel implementation. Rather, “Knowledge Ātma” can be the conceptual identity/principle of the kernel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge Ātma ≡(conceptual) the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS Kernel, while 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = the executable realization of that principle' — preserving the concept/implementation distinction. The kernel is what remains structurally stable while Knowledge State K_t, Epistemic State Σ_t and Investigation State Q_t evolve.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_K = \operatorname{Invariant}(S_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives Ātma a formal manifestation: A_K = Invariant(S_t) where S_{t+1}=δ(S_t,o_t) — the system state evolves (S_0->S_1->S_2->...) while A_K remains invariant, giving architectural form to 'Ātma is the persistent Knower while the state changes'. Composes the full architecture: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Ātma Kernel + Knowledge Space + Epistemic Capabilities + Domain Knowledge, with the Kernel managing/evolving K_t and K_t⊆𝒦.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we can distinguish two Ātma concepts
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two Ātma concepts that must be given different names so they are never confused: Human/Knower Ātma 𝒜_H — the human Knower (e.g. Arjuna) who has intent, asks questions, observes, experiences uncertainty, evaluates meaning, decides, and acts, with changing knowledge state K^H_t but persistent subject; and KnowledgeOS Ātma 𝒜_K — the persistent identity/principle of the KnowledgeOS epistemic system/kernel that maintains and operates on its own knowledge states K^K_t via observation representation, evidence/provenance, dimension discovery, epistemic evaluation, Zero, coherence, state transition, investigation support.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet say that KnowledgeOS Ātma is literally a second Ātman
b_rows_sample.statement: Cautions against treating KnowledgeOS Ātma as literally a second metaphysical Ātman — that would move from architectural analogy to metaphysical claim. Defines 𝒜_H := Human Knower abstraction and 𝒜_K := KnowledgeOS persistent system identity; the shared word 'Ātma' expresses the analogy of persistence/invariant identity, not metaphysical identity between the two.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal A_H \neq \mathcal A_K \neq K_t \subseteq \mathcal K
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the four-way separation Knower Ātma ≠ Knowledge Ātma, Knowledge Ātma ≠ Knowledge State, Knowledge State ≠ Knowledge Space, giving 𝒜_H ≠ 𝒜_K ≠ K_t ⊆ 𝒦. Models the Arjuna-Sārathi interaction as 𝒜_H --Intent--> 𝒜_K --Investigation--> K_t --Zero--> Δ_t --Sārathi--> next inquiry, worked through 'show me whom I have to fight' discovering new dimensions {Kinship, Teacher, Elder,...} via parsing/semantic reconstruction rather than the Knower pre-specifying them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames the architecture as Human Knower <-> KnowledgeOS Ātma <-> Knowledge Space, with Zero/Lord/Sārathi operating between the current state and the expanding knowledge horizon, and proposes that the next formal question should be 'what is the exact relationship between the Human Knower Ātma and the KnowledgeOS Ātma?' rather than continuing with an isolated mathematical object — called 'a significant conceptual milestone'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...)
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the Knower itself as the biggest missing formally-completed piece despite 𝒜_H (Knower Ātma) being named: proposes N=(Identity,Intent,Perspective,Context,Goals,Capabilities,Constraints,...) as the needed model, motivated by the principle that two Knowers can observe the same reality and produce different Ideal States — 'not an error, a fundamental property of the system'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \widehat K_t = \text{best available reconstruction from }O_{\le t}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes 'we try our best but never reach the best' as K̂_t = best available reconstruction from O_≤t, with K̂_t ≠ K_t possibly persisting even as observations accumulate (O_≤t1 ⊆ O_≤t2 may give a better but still imperfect K̂_t2). Draws a careful analogy to least-squares/Gaussian estimation (x̂=argmin_x‖Ax-b‖²): 'best approximation under a criterion' does not guarantee x̂=x_true, giving 'Best reconstruction under regime R ≠ complete underlying Knowledge'. Places measure/probability theory specifically at the Observations->probabilistic reconstruction step (P(K_t|F_t), E[X_t|F_t]), with K_t itself 'conceptually prior' to the probabilistic extraction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ātman should not be modeled as an "Ideal State" itself. It is better modeled as the invariant identity underlying changing states.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed equation of Ātman with the Ideal State, offering instead 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' ℐ with ℐ_{t+1}=ℐ_t while K_{t+1}≠K_t and I_{t+1}≠I_t in general, giving Identity ≠ Current State ≠ Ideal State — 'a very important refinement'. K_t = State(ℐ,t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_0 \subseteq? K_1 \subseteq? K_2
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge evolution K_0->K_1->K_2->... within K_t⊆𝒦 is NOT necessarily monotonic — an assertion can be accepted, then questioned, then rejected, so K_{t+1} may contain less information than K_t in one sense while being epistemically better, reinforcing the earlier distinction between knowledge quantity and knowledge quality/coherence. Also cautions against assuming lim_{t->∞} K_t = 𝒦 as a mathematical fact rather than an assumption.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Ātman doctrine} \rightarrow \text{philosophical inspiration} \rightarrow \text{Invariant Identity abstraction}
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit philosophy/mathematics firewall: 'The Gītā teaches that Ātman is not destroyed' does NOT mathematically imply 'our model proves an invariant identity exists' — Ātman doctrine -> philosophical inspiration -> Invariant Identity abstraction, never Ātman doctrine ⇒ mathematical theorem. Recommends adding 'Persistent Identity / Invariant Subject' as a new theoretical concept (not folding Ātman into Ideal State), with a suggested documentation sentence: 'The concept of Ātman provides a philosophical analogue for the architectural concept of persistent identity... KnowledgeOS may use this as a conceptual inspiration, but does not claim to computationally model Ātman or establish its metaphysical truth.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: atman-in-the-conceptual-model -> atman-within-our-knowledgeos-theory -> atma-and-kernel-are-the-same-underlying-idea -> atma-can-be-the-knowledgeos-kernel -- fourth turning point -- a four-document escalation ending in Atma can be the Kernel ... The corpus also issues its own guard against over-literal mapping (correction-don-t-map-chakra-knowledge-layer).
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies R3's fourth turning point: a four-document escalation across 14 minutes (08-27 08:51-09:05) moving from 'Atma usable in the conceptual model' to 'Atma can be the Kernel', while also noting the corpus issued its own guard against over-literal mapping (a correction document refusing to map chakras directly onto knowledge layers) and flags that whether Atma-as-Kernel was ever tested is NOT ESTABLISHED at inventory depth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OQ-01 What is the Kernel object, if not Knowledge? ... never answered in-corpus; R5's answer (8 primitives) is a kernel, but the R1 question was about the object of protection | OQ-03 Is Determination ... now covered by step-008 acceptance/commitment -- or still missing? R1->R5 mapping absent | OQ-05 Did Atma-as-Kernel survive? (025s mentions Knowledge Atma) R3->R5, unmapped
b_rows_sample.statement: Records three unresolved substantive questions the corpus itself never answers: OQ-01 what the Kernel object actually is if not Knowledge (R1's original object-of-protection question, distinct from R5's 8-primitive kernel answer); OQ-03 whether R1's 'Determination is the missing mathematical object' is now covered by step-008's acceptance/commitment machinery or still missing (no R1->R5 mapping exists); OQ-05 whether Atma-as-Kernel survived into R5 (a 025s document mentions 'Knowledge Atma' but the R3->R5 mapping is unestablished).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4 ATMAN -- UNKNOWN (hypothesis without descendants) ... never tested, never withdrawn; C-012 remains OPEN. The 025s trace needs one read in Phase 2B to classify as refined or abandoned
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces Atman/Atma's lineage from R3's 14-minute escalation to 'Atma can be the KnowledgeOS Kernel' through a later trace ('Knowledge Atma' in step-025s) to absence from the final 8-primitive kernel and Steps 100-158 vocabulary -- final verdict UNKNOWN: the hypothesis was never tested nor formally withdrawn, C-012 remains OPEN, and the 025s trace needs a dedicated read to classify it as refined or abandoned.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: AAG=(V,E) ... V=V_C∪V_K∪V_I∪V_E∪V_T∪V_F
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Architecture Assurance Graph AAG=(V,E) with node types V_C (components/bounded contexts), V_K (contracts), V_I (invariants), V_E (enforcement mechanisms), V_T (verification tests), V_F (evidence/artifacts), and typed edges Component-owns->Invariant, Contract-carries->SemanticProperty, Mechanism-enforces->Invariant, Test-verifies->Invariant, Evidence-supports->Test/Claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I -> Owner -> Mechanism -> Test -> Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: For a critical property I, the complete assurance chain is I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence; a missing edge is potentially an assurance gap. Worked example: I_Authority->Governance->AuthorizationPolicy->NegativeTest->TestEvidence is a complete chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A — Defined and enforced ... D — Claimed but unverifiable
a_rows_sample.statement: Every invariant is classified into one of four situations: (A) defined and enforced and verified; (B) defined but not enforced (M=empty); (C) implemented but not architecturally declared (a mechanism exists but nobody established which invariant it protects); (D) claimed but unverifiable (documentation asserts I=True but no evidence exists). D is flagged as particularly dangerous.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I) ... Gap(I) in {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines assurance gap conceptually as Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I), explicitly refusing to assign arbitrary numerical values and instead classifying into {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} 'until we establish a justified scoring model'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Component correctness =/=> System correctness
a_rows_sample.statement: An architecture may have every individual bounded context (Evidence, Assessment, Governance) correct while still having a critical global assurance gap, e.g. if the contract Assessment->Governance silently drops uncertainty; boxed conclusion: component correctness does not imply system correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(I_global) <= min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}
a_rows_sample.statement: States a weakest-link property: for a critical end-to-end property I_global, assurance is bounded by the minimum assurance of its constituent links, explicitly qualified as 'not a universal mathematical law; it is a useful conservative assurance model' — if one indispensable boundary lacks a provenance guarantee, end-to-end provenance cannot be honestly claimed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Traceability_syntactic=True but Traceability_historical=False
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision traceability example D->A->E: traceability is only True if each reference (Decision->Assessment ID->Evidence ID) remains resolvable and semantically versioned; if the Assessment ID resolves only to the latest Assessment, syntactic traceability can hold while historical traceability fails — 'this distinction is crucial'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SyntacticCorrectness =/= SemanticCorrectness ... HTTP 200 ... JSON schema valid
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness: an HTTP 200 proves transport success but not BusinessMeaningCorrect; a valid JSON schema does not prove SemanticContractValid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate six-dimension KnowledgeOS assurance vector A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g): A_s structural (component exists, boundary explicit, dependencies controlled, contracts defined), A_m semantic (meaning preserved, no overloaded concept, no Boolean replacing a richer state), A_e epistemic/statistical (evidence, inference, assumptions, uncertainty, correlation vs causation, model version), A_t temporal (which version/policy/model applied when, historical reconstructability), A_p provenance (claim origin, traversable chain), A_g governance (who was authorized, under which valid policy, permission vs execution).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues a single global assurance score is dangerous: if A_s=1 but A_p=0, a scalar like 0.83 could falsely imply reasonable assurance, whereas for critical systems one missing indispensable property may be enough to block certification; boxed principle: vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization — an explicit statistical-design principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C0 — Informational ... C4 — Critical assurance
a_rows_sample.statement: Provisionally classifies invariant criticality into five levels: C0 Informational (documentation/style), C1 Functional (normal business behavior), C2 Semantic (meaning/context preservation), C3 Governance (authority/policy/compliance), C4 Critical assurance (safety, irreversible action, high-impact decision, legally significant state); flagged as needing later validation against real KnowledgeOS use cases.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mechanism(I)=f(Criticality(I))
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes assurance-mechanism selection as a function of criticality: low-risk -> Documentation+UnitTest; medium -> IntegrationTest+ContractTest; high -> PropertyBasedTest+Replay+AuditEvidence; critical -> FormalModel/Proof where practical — self-labeled 'a proposed framework, not yet a frozen standard'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an AI-generated-artifact metadata schema A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance), stating the schema must be derived from the actual KnowledgeOS implementation but conceptually AI output should not be treated as an unexplained opaque fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI -> CandidateResult -> DeterministicValidation -> AcceptedArtifact. Not: AI -> ProductionTruth
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architecture must route AI output through AI->CandidateResult->DeterministicValidation->AcceptedArtifact, never directly AI->ProductionTruth, calling this distinction 'central to our KnowledgeOS design'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TrustedFor(x,p,t) ... Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose)
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against another bare Boolean (`trusted = true`); trust/assurance must be contextual, TrustedFor(x,p,t) — an artifact trustworthy for Task_1 need not be trustworthy for Task_2. Generalizes to Valid(x) being usually incomplete; the better form is Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose), called 'a major insight for KnowledgeOS': validity is not absolute but ValidForPurpose(P).

a_rows_sample.anchor: StructuralValid ... SemanticValid ... EpistemicallyValid ... TemporallyValid ... GovernanceValid
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five validity types (Structural/Semantic/Epistemic/Temporal/Governance Valid), concluding Valid(x) should be treated as shorthand only when the intended dimension is explicitly known.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Different missing edges represent different classes of architectural weakness
a_rows_sample.statement: States the missing-node principle: Invariant->Owner with no Enforcement is a design gap; Enforcement->Test missing is an assurance gap; Test->Evidence missing is an auditability gap — different missing edges are different classes of architectural weakness, letting the architecture 'diagnose itself' via forall I_i: Complete(AAG(I_i))? producing a reproducible gap report.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System -> Output + EvidenceOfCorrectness
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the architecture's strongest form as System->Output+EvidenceOfCorrectness rather than merely System->Output, stated as precisely what deterministic assurance is trying to accomplish.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not claim: 'The architecture is mathematically proven.' ... FormalizableArchitecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit self-warning: the architecture must not be claimed as mathematically proven; what exists is a FormalizableArchitecture, and the next task is determining which portions can actually be Formalized->Specified->Verified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### DDD ... VERY STRONG ... Gītā 1–4 ... DEEP CONSISTENCY
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 verdict: DDD, Mathematics, Statistics, Governance, and AI are each rated VERY STRONG, and Gita chapters 1-4 rated DEEP CONSISTENCY, citing continued distinctions Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Action, Capability!=Authority, PastState!=CurrentState, Decision!=Outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. Step 212 Section 212.6 defines E_0=No evidence, E_1=Claim/documentation, E_2=Static implementation evidence, E_3=Executable test evidence, E_4=Runtime/production evidence, E_5=Formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #4 — E_1 bound twice inside Step 210 itself
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P (evidence items entailing propositions); Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (an ordinal assurance rung). Same symbol, same document, incompatible types, undisambiguated. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #5 — Evidence/Test ordering reversed between Step 210's own boxed conclusion and Step 211's boxed conclusion
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 Section 210.40 boxes Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance; Step 211 Section 211.2 boxes I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence -- directly conflicting orderings, both boxed as conclusions in consecutive files. Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple and Step 209's tail agenda both side with Step 211's ordering, so Step 210's boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own boxed tuple. Severity MEDIUM; the direction matters since Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test while Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #6 — min over assurance vs. the prohibition on scalarization, both boxed in Step 211
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 Section 211.6 states Assurance(I_global)<=min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}; Step 211 Section 211.17 boxes 'Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization.' min over a set requires a total order on the codomain, but Section 211.9 makes assurance a 6-vector (only partially ordered), so evaluating min requires exactly the scalarization Section 211.17 forbids -- the two boxed positions of one file are mutually exclusive. Aggravated by Section 211.4's ordinal-only assurance-adjacent quantities and by Section 211.17's own use of cardinal values A_s=1, A_p=0, 0.83. Severity HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #7 — Step 212 builds ownership diagnostics and deletes the ownership data needed to run them
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 boxes 'Ownerless Invariants' as a finding to explicitly search for (I exists but Owner(I)=empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4's register reprints all fifteen invariants with the Owner column removed (columns reduced to ID|Property|Target), and no search for ownerless invariants is performed anywhere in the file. Step 210's deleted Owner column contained exactly the data Sections 212.15/212.16 are designed to interrogate: 7 of 15 rows owned by a layer or pattern (effectively ownerless), 5 of 15 slash-shared. Severity HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #8 — F/D/P/U mandated in Step 213, applied zero times across Steps 213-215
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 213 Section 213.26 mandates that every important statement during reconstruction carry an [F]/[D]/[P]/[U] label ('our editorial control system'). A machine count of applied labels in Steps 213, 214, and 215 finds 4, 0, 0 respectively, and all four occurrences in 213 are the legend itself. Zero of the hundreds of statements in the three files that mandate the labels carry one, even though Section 213.26 explicitly scopes the requirement to these reconstruction documents themselves. Severity HIGH; this is a performative contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #9 — Step 214's self-assessment table violates Step 214's own boxed evidentiary rule eight lines later
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.32 boxes 'no architectural claim should be stronger than the evidence supporting it.' Step 214 Section 214.33's final row states 'Risk of overclaiming | Explicitly controlled' -- a claim about the corpus's own overclaiming risk with zero supporting evidence, in a table that also self-awards 'Very strong' on five dimensions in a file containing no evidence at all. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #10 — Three incompatible ledger arities inside Step 214
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 214 Section 214.1 boxes a 10-tuple EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status); Section 214.6 gives a 15-field schema table; the Section 214 tail (line 1095) gives an 8-column matrix header whose columns barely overlap the 10-tuple's. b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #12 — Step 215 exempts itself and its seven predecessors from its own discipline
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 215 Section 215.31 (Phase 1) targets S_1...S_182 -> EvidenceLedger, goal 'understand what actually happened'; the same file's closing paragraph defers 'what we previously called Step 183 onward' to a later decision about renaming or absorption. Steps 183-215 include all eight in-scope files of this verification, so the reconstruction discipline is scoped to exclude the very documents that mandate it -- compounded by Contradiction #8 (zero labels applied). Severity HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #13 — The scope of the derivation phase disagrees between Step 212 and Step 215
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 Section 212.5 states 'Steps 1-211 have largely been derivation'; Step 215 Section 215.31 and five other occurrences scope the reconstruction to S_1...S_182. The corpus states the derivation ran to 211 while scoping reconstruction to 182; the 29-step remainder is never reconciled, and 182 is never justified anywhere. Severity MEDIUM.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #14 — Subtraction on an undefined information measure, forbidden in Step 208 and performed anyway in Step 212
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.10 writes L(C)=I_required-I_preserved and immediately cautions 'we should not treat this as a literal numeric quantity until we define an information measure.' Step 212 Section 212.19 writes L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) without that caveat and without citing 208.10 -- no information measure is defined anywhere in the intervening four files. This is the fourth occurrence of the pattern in the band (208.3's I(A)<I(E), 208.10, 212.19, and 214.7's SemanticLoss(A)>0). Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #16 — Invariants modeled as a dependency graph and as a flat conjunction, consecutively, within Step 209
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.31 states that some invariants depend on others (HistoricalTraceability depends on Identity+Versioning+Provenance), illustrated with a 24-line ASCII dependency graph. Step 209 Section 209.32 then composes all invariants as a flat, order-free conjunction I_global=AND_{i=1}^n I_i. A conjunction cannot express dependency; the two sections model the same invariant set with incompatible structures, consecutively. Severity MEDIUM.

a_rows_sample.statement: Notes directory structure suggests architectural intent but naming alone is not proof of actual conformance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Steps 101-105 established the conformance model for architecture, semantics, governance, agents. Step 106 asks: does that architecture survive contact with the actual running system? A_I->A_C->A_D->A_R. Crucial requirement: A_R approx A_I subject to explicitly documented runtime differences.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 106's central test: whether the architecture survives contact with the running system, via A_I(intended)->A_C(implementation)->A_D(deployed)->A_R(runtime), requiring approximate conformance A_R≈A_I subject to documented differences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.1 — Why runtime is the final authority for runtime facts ... Documentation ≠ RuntimeEvidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Documentation ≠ RuntimeEvidence: runtime is the final authority for runtime facts, illustrated by a documented ServiceA→ServiceB call diverging from actual production topology.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.2 — Four representations ... Architecture model A_I, Source model A_C, Deployment model A_D, Runtime model A_R. The goal is not necessarily literal equality. It is Conformance(A_I,A_C,A_D,A_R).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the four representations (Architecture/Source/Deployment/Runtime models) and states the goal is Conformance(A_I,A_C,A_D,A_R), not literal equality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.3 — Experiment 1: deployed version mismatch ... Architecture says KnowledgeOS=2.1. Deployment runs KnowledgeOS=2.0. Expected: DeploymentDrift. Result: PASS. The system must report the mismatch rather than silently assuming the latest code is running.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a deployed version (2.0) lagging the architecture-declared version (2.1) is DeploymentDrift, which must be reported not silently assumed away; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.4 — Experiment 2: configuration mismatch ... Repository defines FeatureX=True. Production configuration FeatureX=False. Expected: runtime behavior must be evaluated using the actual configuration. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: runtime behavior must be evaluated using the actual production configuration (FeatureX=False), not the repository default; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.5 — Configuration is architecture ... Architecture is not only SourceCode. It includes relevant Configuration. A_R=Code+Configuration+Infrastructure+Dependencies+RuntimeState.
b_rows_sample.statement: States configuration is part of architecture: A_R=Code+Configuration+Infrastructure+Dependencies+RuntimeState.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.6 — Experiment 3: environment-specific architecture ... Development: PostgreSQL. Production: ManagedDatabase. Expected: not automatically a violation if the architecture explicitly allows environment-specific infrastructure (ArchitectureRule=EnvironmentAware). Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: environment-specific infrastructure (dev PostgreSQL vs prod ManagedDatabase) is not automatically a violation if declared EnvironmentAware; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.7 — Runtime topology ... Component→Instance→Environment→Host/Platform. e.g. AgentGateway→Container→Production→Cluster.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the runtime topology model Component→Instance→Environment→Host/Platform.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.8 — Experiment 4 ... Architecture identifies AgentGateway. Runtime has AgentGateway_1 and AgentGateway_2. Expected: both instances map to the same logical component. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: multiple runtime instances (AgentGateway_1, _2) must map to the same logical component; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.9 — Logical versus physical identity ... LogicalComponent ≠ RuntimeInstance. A component may have n instances.
b_rows_sample.statement: States LogicalComponent ≠ RuntimeInstance: one component may have many runtime instances.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.10 — Experiment 5 ... A deployment scales ServiceA: 2→8 instances. Expected: architecture does not become eight separate logical components. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: scaling ServiceA from 2 to 8 instances does not create eight logical components; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.11 — Runtime dependency discovery ... evidence may come from network connections, service discovery, traces, logs, configuration, deployment manifests.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists evidence sources for runtime dependency discovery: network connections, service discovery, traces, logs, configuration, deployment manifests.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.12 — Experiment 6 ... Architecture says A ↛ C. Runtime trace shows A→C. Expected: RuntimeArchitectureViolation. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: an observed A→C dependency violating the architecture's A↛C rule is RuntimeArchitectureViolation; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.13 — Runtime architecture graph ... G_R(t)=(V_R,E_R) where V_R=RuntimeComponents, E_R=ObservedDependencies. Then compare with G_I.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the runtime architecture graph G_R(t)=(V_R,E_R), compared against the intended graph G_I.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.14 — Architecture drift ... Drift(t)=Difference(G_I,G_R(t)). This is one of the most valuable KnowledgeOS capabilities.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Drift(t)=Difference(G_I,G_R(t)), called one of the most valuable KnowledgeOS capabilities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.15 — Experiment 7 ... A new external API appears in production. No architecture record exists. Expected: DriftCandidate. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: an undocumented new external API appearing in production is a DriftCandidate; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.16 — But drift is not automatically violation ... A runtime difference may be ApprovedException or ExpectedDynamicBehavior. Drift ≠ Violation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Drift ≠ Violation: a runtime difference may be an ApprovedException or ExpectedDynamicBehavior.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.17 — Experiment 8 ... A temporary scaling mechanism creates additional runtime instances. Architecture does not enumerate every instance. Expected: no architecture violation. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: temporary scaling instances not enumerated in architecture is not itself a violation; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.18 — Dynamic architecture ... Instances(t), Load(t), Connections(t), ResourceAllocation(t). KnowledgeOS must model which dimensions are Static versus Dynamic.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires KnowledgeOS to model which architectural dimensions are intentionally dynamic (Instances(t), Load(t), Connections(t), ResourceAllocation(t)) versus static.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 106.19 — Experiment 9 ... Agent workers scale automatically from 2→20. Expected: scaling itself is not drift if permitted by architecture. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 9: architecturally-permitted auto-scaling (2→20) is not drift; result PASS.
