a_rows_sample.anchor: 31 distinct definitional statements, 347 files, 148 numbered steps.
a_rows_sample.statement: A full corpus scan (347 files, 148 numbered steps) locates 31 distinct definitional statements of 'Assurance', tabulated by source step/date with meaning, formal type, inputs, outputs, lifecycle, pairwise compatibility, and evidence provenance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Not one concept. Not merely overloaded terminology. Four different KINDS of thing plus one ill-formed definition: A property of a claim's justification ... A property of the ARTIFACT's form ... A risk quantity ... A structural/organisational unit ... Ill-formed
a_rows_sample.statement: The 31 statements resolve into four incompatible KINDS of thing (a property of a claim's justification — steps 140/168/211 plus the executable-vs-prose meta-claim, genuinely the same concept at different abstraction levels; a property of the artifact's FORM, a measure of the above rather than the thing itself; a risk quantity, step 092, a different concept about consequences not justification; a structural/organisational unit, steps 127 and 071, an architectural placement rather than a semantic definition) plus one ill-formed self-referential definition (step 230).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every neighbour has a distinct, well-typed signature. Assurance has none that is not already one of them. That is the decisive test: a term with no signature of its own is not a formal term.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decisive test applied: Verification (Artifact x Spec -> Bool), Validation (K x Standard -> Assessment), Assessment (P x Evidence x Context x Policy -> Sigma), Evidence (QualifiedObservation), Backward traceability (claim -> ancestors, reachability in R_der union R_ref), and Governance compliance (Policy x Transformation -> Admissible) each already have a distinct, well-typed signature; Assurance has no signature that is not already one of these — a term with no signature of its own is judged not a formal term.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 230: Assurance = DeterministicAssurance. Step 2026-08-23 imports: "Assurance does not recursively certify itself." The corpus asserts a prohibition and then violates it 100+ steps later.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 230's self-referential definition Assurance=DeterministicAssurance is REFUTED as ill-formed and shown to directly contradict the corpus's own later-imported Williamson prohibition ('Assurance does not recursively certify itself', 2026-08-23) — the corpus states a prohibition and then violates it 100+ steps earlier in its own numbering; JustificationStrength avoids the defect because it is a property OF a claim assigned by an EXTERNAL procedure and never certifies itself, turning the prohibition into a type constraint rather than a warning.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance ⟶ REMOVED from the canonical vocabulary as a formal term ... JustificationStrength(claim): Claim → OrdinalScale ... Traceability(claim): Claim → ℘(Claim) ... Risk(action): Action → OrdinalScale ... GovernanceValid(K, Γ): already defined
a_rows_sample.statement: Resolution (CB-1, closed by splitting rather than choosing): Assurance is removed from the canonical vocabulary as a formal term, retained only as an informal umbrella word never used in a type signature; its legitimate content redistributes with no residue into four independently defined functions: JustificationStrength(claim):Claim->OrdinalScale (ordinal scale {prose,reviewed,tested,executable,proven}, subsuming steps 140/168/211), Traceability(claim):Claim->P(Claim) (reachability in R_der union R_ref, = step 170), Risk(action):Action->OrdinalScale (= step 092), and GovernanceValid(K,Gamma) (already defined elsewhere); the word is dropped because it is prominent, not retained because it is correct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The most-repeated statement (≥5 independent files) is: "Assurance is strong exactly where it is executable and weak exactly where it is prose." Applied reflexively: the 1468-file corpus is prose, therefore JustificationStrength(corpus) = prose, the weakest level.
a_rows_sample.statement: The corpus's own most-repeated claim about Assurance (>=5 independent files: strong where executable, weak where prose) is applied reflexively to the corpus itself: since the 1468-file corpus is prose, JustificationStrength(corpus)=prose, the weakest ordinal level; only the executable fragments (the EKP's 18 lint rules, 47 lineage tests, and this verification programme's own executed counterexamples) score above it — used as the argument for why triangulation against a running implementation was necessary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four-way split loses nothing | FORMALLY DERIVED — not proven exhaustive over all 31 ... JustificationStrength is ordinal | FORMALLY DERIVED — no arithmetic admissible
a_rows_sample.statement: Self-limiting classification of the split's own result: the claim that the four-way split (JustificationStrength/Traceability/Risk/GovernanceValid) loses nothing is FORMALLY DERIVED but explicitly not proven exhaustive over all 31 source statements; JustificationStrength is FORMALLY DERIVED to be ordinal only, meaning no arithmetic (e.g. averaging or summation) is admissible on it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CB-1 Assurance contradictory -> CLOSED — split into JustificationStrength / Traceability / Risk / GovernanceValid (artifact B) ... CB-2 P=(E,D,V) undefined -> CLOSED — Entity/Dimension/Value, Q14 ... CB-4 theory disconnected from EKP -> CLOSED — triangulated; 7 predicates engineeringally verified ..
a_rows_sample.statement: Four previously-open corpus gaps (CB-series) are recorded CLOSED as of this phase: CB-1 (Assurance's internal contradiction, closed by the four-way split), CB-2 (P=(E,D,V) undefined, closed by the Entity/Dimension/Value resolution), CB-4 (theory disconnected from the EKP, closed by triangulation with 7 engineeringally verified predicates), and CB-7 (the state/history boundary, closed as SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance | REMOVED from the formal vocabulary — split four ways ... JustificationStrength · Traceability · Risk | NEW — the split's products ... Entity · Dimension · Value | NEW as first-class terms — previously hidden inside an opaque P ... Conflict | SEPARATED from Contradiction ... ℛ_rel (relate
a_rows_sample.statement: Terms whose status changed in this verification phase: Assurance REMOVED (split four ways); JustificationStrength/Traceability/Risk added as NEW terms (the split's products); Entity/Dimension/Value promoted to first-class NEW terms (previously hidden inside opaque P); Conflict SEPARATED from Contradiction as a distinct concept; R_rel (related_to) added as a NEW symmetric relation family learned from the implementation; and Epistemic Status DEMOTED from FROZEN back to PROPOSED because its three-state model was refuted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 42.10: There must be no averaging. Executed: Pre=T, Assurance=T, Authorization=T, Invariant=F → False. A 95%-admissible decision is inadmissible. ... the gates are nominal/boolean; JustificationStrength is ordinal. Neither admits arithmetic. Averaging four booleans would require an interval scale th
a_rows_sample.statement: The corpus's independently-stated 'no averaging' rule for policy gates (a 95%-admissible decision, i.e. 3 of 4 gates true, is still inadmissible if even one is false) is confirmed by an independent measurement-theoretic argument: gates are nominal/boolean and JustificationStrength is ordinal, and neither scale admits arithmetic — averaging four booleans would require an interval scale that does not exist for either; the corpus's rule and the verifier's own scale-theory constraint are shown to be the identical constraint, derived twice via two independent routes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rules (57.47) = the conjunct set of 42.9; ResolutionBehavior (57.47) = the Unknown → Block rule (42.12); ValidityInterval (57.47) = the temporal applicability of 54's 'rule over an applicable context'. Three sources, one object, no invention required. ... 42.9's Assurance conjunct is not a primitive
a_rows_sample.statement: The three separately-sourced Policy fragments (57.47's tuple fields, 42.9's conjunct set, 54's temporal-applicability gloss, 42.12's Unknown-handling rule) are shown to describe the same single object with one substitution needed: 42.9's 'Assurance' conjunct, not being a coherent primitive concept (per the prior-phase Assurance split), maps onto a JustificationStrength >= threshold gate — the Assurance split is shown to survive and sharpen contact with the independently-derived Policy evaluation law, since 'Assurance' as a conjunct was always implicitly a threshold test, never a standalone concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an assertion is a claim with evidence, origin and validity, admitted by a policy under authority. A policy is a rule with rationale, origin and validity, admitted by a meta-policy under authority. The theory already knows how to type this. ... Guard against infinite regress: the corpus already suppl
a_rows_sample.statement: The exact structural symmetry between Assertion and Policy is stated (assertion: claim+evidence+origin+validity, admitted by a policy under authority; policy: rule+rationale+origin+validity, admitted by a meta-policy under authority) as the reason G-P1 is derivable rather than a normative question; an infinite meta-policy regress is guarded against using the corpus's own 'Assurance does not recursively certify itself' stopping rule, terminating at a constitutional policy that is adopted (not derived) — empirically matching the EKP's single frozen, authoritative Knowledge-Constitution document, the only frozen document among its 37.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Policy undefined -> CLOSED — corpus 57.47 + 42.9, executed ... Assessment uncomputable -> CLOSED — Policy supplies the missing parameter ... Σ underdetermined -> CLOSED — (dir,str) + Γ, PF-6 dissolved ... Assurance contradictory -> CLOSED — split four ways ... P = (E,D,V) undefined -> CLOSED — Q14
a_rows_sample.statement: Five previously open gaps are confirmed CLOSED as of this mandate: Policy undefined (closed via 57.47+42.9, executed), Assessment uncomputable (closed once Policy supplies the missing parameter), Sigma underdetermined (closed via (dir,str)+Gamma, PF-6 dissolved), Assurance contradictory (closed via the four-way split), and P=(E,D,V) undefined (closed via Q14).

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Probability Distribution (246) — no (Ω,ℱ,P) in 1468 files · Assurance = f(Irreversibility,Impact,Criticality) (092) · Assurance = Strong BC Candidate (127) · Knowledge = Structure(X,R,Q,H,…) (253) — H ∈ K contradicted by executed evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidated SOURCE CLAIM (unverified) register: KnowledgeOS-as-Probability-Distribution (no probability space found in 1468 files), the two rejected Assurance formulations, and step 253's Structure(X,R,Q,H,...) whose H-inside-K component is contradicted by executed evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance cannot survive as one formal concept. It has been decomposed into JustificationStrength, Traceability, Risk, GovernanceValid. Therefore CB-1 is: CLOSED BY SPLIT. We should not reopen it unless a new contradiction appears.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independently confirms and accepts the Assurance four-way split (JustificationStrength/Traceability/Risk/GovernanceValid) as closing gap CB-1, explicitly directing that it should not be reopened absent a new contradiction — cross-thread convergence with the separately-tracked artifact B.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy : K × Context → Criterion | REJECTED — makes a policy state-dependent ... Policy : Observation → Decision | REJECTED — skips proposition, evidence and authority; conflates policy with decision ... Policy : Claim × Evidence × Context → Assessment | REJECTED as the TYPE — this is the signature
b_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate Policy signatures are eliminated with executed reasoning: Policy:K x Context->Criterion is rejected because it makes policy state-dependent and unversionable/unauditable; Policy:Observation->Decision is rejected for skipping proposition/evidence/authority and conflating policy with decision (already refuted at corpus steps 202/206); Policy:Claim x Evidence x Context->Assessment is rejected as confusing Policy with Assessment's own signature (Assessment takes a Policy as a parameter); and 'Policy = a set of predicates' is subsumed by (not wrong, just incomplete versus) the Rules component, since it omits temporal applicability and unknown-handling.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The decisive discrimination: a policy is an OBJECT that is applied, not a function that is called. It has identity, a version, an applicability window, and it can be composed and compared. A bare function has none of those. ... versioning is only meaningful for an object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decisive discrimination for Policy's category: a Policy is an OBJECT that is applied (having identity, version, an applicability window, and composability/comparability), not a bare function that is called — versioning (corpus-named 'Migration-Policy v3', 'ChangePolicy v3') is only meaningful for an object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy = (id, version, Gates, ValidityInterval, ResolutionBehavior) ... Gates : SET of three-valued predicates g : Decision → {True, False, Unknown} ... ValidityInterval : [vf, vt) ... ResolutionBehavior : Unknown → Block | Allow ... Apply(p,d) = False if ∃g∈p.Gates: g(d)=False ← strict conjunction,
b_rows_sample.statement: The derived canonical Policy type: Policy=(id, version, Gates, ValidityInterval, ResolutionBehavior), where Gates is a set of three-valued predicates over a Decision, ValidityInterval is a half-open temporal window, and ResolutionBehavior maps Unknown to Block or Allow; the Apply function is a strict three-valued conjunction over Gates (False if any gate is False, ResolutionBehavior(Unknown) if any gate is Unknown and none is False, True otherwise, with no averaging), and Applicable(p,t) checks temporal membership in the validity interval — this directly answers gap G-2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Gates is a SET, not a tuple — PROVEN, not chosen. Executed: two policies differing only in gate order are structurally unequal but extensionally equal. Order is representation; a tuple leaks it into identity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Executed proof that Gates must be a set rather than an ordered tuple: two policies differing only in gate order are found structurally unequal but extensionally (behaviorally) equal — a tuple representation would leak arbitrary insertion order into policy identity, which is wrong; this is PROVEN by the order-difference test, not a stylistic choice.

b_rows_sample.anchor: codomain {True, False, Unknown} — three-valued ... totality partial — undefined outside ValidityInterval ... composability ∧ only — meet-semilattice; ∨ REFUTED ... identity (id, version); version is semantically load-bearing ... executed: same id, different ResolutionBehavior, different result ... p
b_rows_sample.statement: Per-property analysis of Policy: three-valued codomain, partial totality (undefined outside its validity interval), deterministic given fixed gates, composable only under conjunction (a meet-semilattice; disjunction is REFUTED as a composition operator), four distinct equality notions (deferred to a companion artifact 5), identity is (id,version) with version proven semantically load-bearing (same id with different ResolutionBehavior gives a different Apply result), versioning required (corpus names v3 policies), and policy provenance (who authored/authorised it) explicitly recorded as absent from the governing corpus definition (step 57.47) — an unresolved gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: adm_early(True, None, True, True) → None (Block). A two-valued policy must map Unknown to either True or False silently. The corpus makes that mapping an explicit, named component of the policy object — ResolutionBehavior. ... it connects directly to Σ's Neutral/Unknown — the same epistemic humility
b_rows_sample.statement: Why three-valued semantics matter: an executed example (adm_early with one Unknown gate value producing Block) shows a two-valued policy would have to silently coerce Unknown to True or False, whereas the corpus's ResolutionBehavior makes that coercion an explicit, named, auditable choice — called the single most sophisticated part of the corpus's policy treatment, and noted to be the same epistemic-humility pattern that appears at the Sigma (epistemic status) Neutral/Unknown level, i.e. the same design idea recurring at two levels of the theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 42.10: There must be no averaging. Executed: Pre=T, Assurance=T, Authorization=T, Invariant=F → False. A 95%-admissible decision is inadmissible. ... the gates are nominal/boolean; JustificationStrength is ordinal. Neither admits arithmetic. Averaging four booleans would require an interval scale th
b_rows_sample.statement: The corpus's independently-stated 'no averaging' rule for policy gates (a 95%-admissible decision, i.e. 3 of 4 gates true, is still inadmissible if even one is false) is confirmed by an independent measurement-theoretic argument: gates are nominal/boolean and JustificationStrength is ordinal, and neither scale admits arithmetic — averaging four booleans would require an interval scale that does not exist for either; the corpus's rule and the verifier's own scale-theory constraint are shown to be the identical constraint, derived twice via two independent routes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy was never undefined. It is defined at step 57.47 as a three-component tuple, and its evaluation semantics are defined at step 42.9 and IMPLEMENTED in an executable reference file that I ran successfully. The blocker was a coverage failure, not an absence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding reframing gap G-2: Policy was never conceptually undefined in the corpus — its type (step 57.47) and its evaluation semantics (step 42.9) both already exist, the latter already implemented in an executable reference file; the true blocker was a coverage failure (the definitions not yet being found and run), not an actual absence of a Policy formalization.

b_rows_sample.statement: The corpus's own executable reference implementation of the step-42 admissibility law is run directly and passes five distinct checks (no-averaging, Unknown-invariant-blocks, epistemic-pass/auth-fail, auth-pass/hard-invariant-fail, safety-critical-unknown-always-blocks); independence from the verifier's own work is confirmed via a contamination check — ten fingerprints unique to the verifier's own artifacts are searched for in the file with zero hits, and the file's modification time (2026-08-28 23:51) predates the verifier's findings, establishing it as genuinely INDEPENDENT CORPUS EVIDENCE rather than something the verifier itself introduced.

b_rows_sample.statement: Full step-by-step Policy lineage traced across the corpus (steps 8, 13, 25, 41, 42, 49, 54, 57.47, 86, 91, 104, 127, 139, 199, 202, 206, 207, 240, 252, plus non-step material), each classified by whether it is normative or descriptive, executable, superseded, and whether it survives into the current theory — e.g. step 8's 'one authoritative current source' maps forward into the EKP's single_authoritative rule; step 13 introduces versioned policies (Migration-Policy v3), establishing that version is part of identity; step 199's 'Policy = Allowed' and step 207's self-contradictory 'Policy = Decision' / 'Policy is not a command' are both REFUTED.

b_rows_sample.statement: Contradiction C-1 (Policy=normative-rule at step 252 vs Policy!=Rule elsewhere) is resolved as not a genuine contradiction once properly typed: a Policy CONTAINS Rules (per 57.47's tuple) but is not itself a Rule — the type-level claim (Policy!=Rule) is upheld over the loose gloss (Policy=normative rule).

b_rows_sample.statement: Contradiction C-2 (Policy=Decision at step 207 vs Policy!=Decision at steps 202/206) is judged a genuine contradiction, with step 207 additionally contradicting itself internally (the same step also asserts 'Policy is not a command'); REFUTED on both internal-inconsistency grounds and 2:1 corpus-weight — a policy governs decisions, it is not one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An INVARIANT must hold in every admissible state — negating it makes the state invalid. A POLICY is a choice that could defensibly be otherwise — negating it yields a different, still-valid regime. ... 42.9 keeps them in one formula while typing them separately. b_rows_sample.statement: Derived discrimination criterion between Invariant and Policy: an Invariant must hold in every admissible state (negating it makes the state invalid), while a Policy is a defensible choice (negating it yields a different but still-valid regime); the corpus's own admissibility formula (Pre and Invariant and Assurance and Authorization) is cited as the strongest evidence of a deliberate distinction, since it keeps Invariant and the overall policy conjunction in one formula while typing them separately.

b_rows_sample.statement: Three competing admissibility-law formulations coexist in the corpus, and the corpus's own reference implementation explicitly reports the mismatch itself (in executable form, not prose): the 42.9 'early' 4-conjunct law (executed, passes), the 42.41 'refined' 6-conjunct law including Q=epistemic sufficiency (executed, passes), and a 5-conjunct gn-48 candidate marked UNRATIFIED — with the ratified 6-tuple having no ratified admissibility conjunction of its own, since 42.9 omits Temporal and 42.41 belongs to a different 7-tuple's law, constituting a genuine unresolved formal mismatch self-acknowledged by the corpus's own test file.

Three sources, one object, no invention required. ... 42.9's Assurance conjunct is not a primitive
b_rows_sample.statement: The three separately-sourced Policy fragments (57.47's tuple fields, 42.9's conjunct set, 54's temporal-applicability gloss, 42.12's Unknown-handling rule) are shown to describe the same single object with one substitution needed: 42.9's 'Assurance' conjunct, not being a coherent primitive concept (per the prior-phase Assurance split), maps onto a JustificationStrength >= threshold gate — the Assurance split is shown to survive and sharpen contact with the independently-derived Policy evaluation law, since 'Assurance' as a conjunct was always implicitly a threshold test, never a standalone concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P_A 'lenient' ... P_B 'strict' ... D1 strong P_A=True P_B=True DIFFER=False ... D2 weak P_A=True P_B=False DIFFER=True ... D3 unknown-inv P_A=True P_B=None DIFFER=True ... Assessment(K, P_A) ≠ Assessment(K, P_B) — CONFIRMED, twice, on two different mechanisms (a failing gate, and an Unknown resolved
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1 confirms policy-dependence with a synthetic lenient-vs-strict policy pair on three decisions, finding Assessment(K,P_A) != Assessment(K,P_B) via two independent mechanisms: a gate that fails under the strict policy but not the lenient one (D2), and an Unknown value resolved differently by each policy's ResolutionBehavior (D3).

b_rows_sample.anchor: P_B(D1) = True P_B(D4) = True D1 ≠ D4 ... Assessment(K1, Policy) = Assessment(K2, Policy) for distinct states — CONFIRMED. Assessment is a function, not an injection. Distinct knowledge states may share an assessment, so an assessment result can never be used to recover the state that produced it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2 (the converse of Experiment 1) confirms Assessment is a function but not an injection: two distinct decisions D1 and D4 produce the identical assessment True under the same policy — an important theoretical consequence is drawn that an assessment result can never be used to recover the state that produced it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 37 real governed documents ... documents where the two policies differ: 0 ... I initially printed 'SAME K, DIFFERENT POLICY, DIFFERENT ASSESSMENT'. That was FALSE — my own data contradicted my own conclusion. Retained here rather than deleted. ... status and authority are declared independent in aut
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3, run against the real 37-document EKP, FAILS to demonstrate policy-dependence (lenient and strict policies produce identical True/False:24/13 splits, 0 differing documents); an initial false claim ('SAME K, DIFFERENT POLICY, DIFFERENT ASSESSMENT') is explicitly retained rather than deleted, and diagnosed: the differing gate (JustifStrength) never fails independently of Authorization because, empirically, every document with authoritative/derived authority also has an approved-class status — status and authority are declared independent in authorities.yaml but are almost perfectly collinear in the EKP's actual current content, showing orthogonality is a design property, not an observed data property; the methodological consequence is that policy-comparison experiments prove nothing on non-discriminating datasets, and this one would have passed silently if the numbers had not been checked against the prose claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: observed: (Supporting, Committed)=24 (Neutral, Uncommitted)=12 (Neutral, Committed)=1 (Supporting, Uncommitted)=0 ← NOT OBSERVED ... the single off-diagonal document: GRAPH-FULL ... I claimed both off-diagonal quadrants occur. Only one does. CORRECTED CLAIM: orthogonality is supported by ONE off-dia
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4 checks the four Sigma x Gamma quadrants on real data and corrects an overstated initial claim: only one of the two possible off-diagonal cells is actually observed (one document, GRAPH-FULL, in (Supporting,Uncommitted)'s complement rather than both), which is still logically sufficient to refute 'Sigma determines Gamma' but is weaker empirical support than originally claimed; the stronger evidence for Sigma-perp-Gamma remains authorities.yaml's explicit declaration and the corpus's separately executed 10^6-evidence-cannot-commit experiment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy ≠ Knowledge State ... K was byte-identical in both runs; only the policy varied ... PROVEN | Policy ≠ Evidence ... the evidence is unchanged while P_A admits and P_B refuses ... PROVEN | Policy ≠ Assertion Status (Σ) ... Σ is the output of Assessment(·, Policy) ... refutes step 199 ... PROVEN
b_rows_sample.statement: Seven placements of Policy are each PROVEN false with a specific executed counterexample: (1) Policy != Knowledge State, since the same K (37 real EKP assertions) evaluated under two policies stayed byte-identical while only the policy varied; (2) Policy != Evidence, since a fixed piece of evidence (nsrc=1, origin=blog) is admitted by one policy and refused by another, so evidence cannot both be and judge itself; (3) Policy != Assertion Status Sigma, since Sigma is the OUTPUT of Assessment(.,Policy), directly refuting step 199's 'Policy = Allowed' conflation (Allowed is Apply(p,d)'s codomain, not p); (4) Policy != Validation Result, since Apply(P_B,D2)=False's result dict is a value produced by the reusable policy object, not the object itself; (5) Policy != Governance Status Gamma, since 37 real assertions carry 5 distinct Gamma values under a single policy (Gamma is a property of an assertion, Policy a property of the regime); (6) Policy != Assessment, since Assessment:P x Evidence x Context x Policy -> Sigma takes Policy as an argument, and a function cannot be its own parameter (this is why the Policy:Claim x Evidence x Context->Assessment candidate was rejected in artifact 2); (7) Policy != Transformation History, since Policy is an input to T while History is an output of it, and two histories reaching the same K can have been produced under different policies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge should be decomposable into independently addressable semantic units.
a_rows_sample.statement: From the book's atomism discussion (Vaisesika atomic theory seeking a real basis underlying phenomena rather than reducing everything to qualities), proposes a KnowledgeAtom schema (id, meaning, context, evidence, relations, history) replacing giant document blobs (example: ArchitectureDocument.md decomposed into ADR-001 fields: Decision/Reason/Constraint/Evidence/Impact). Derived invariant KOS-ATOM-001.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t is the smallest possible unit of knowledge about an observation at time t.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes, and repeatedly re-affirms as a 'candidate definition, not yet formally proven', K_t(o) = the smallest epistemically meaningful unit of knowledge about observation o at time t, explicitly warning against prematurely identifying K_t with a data point, a claim, or the existing six-tuple (entity/property/context/relation/time/authority) -- those may become representations of K_t, not K_t itself, restated as the invariant 'Representation != Knowledge Identity'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can K_t be decomposed into smaller knowledge units without losing the knowledge about the observation? If yes, it wasn't minimal. If no, we have a candidate minimal knowledge unit.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an operational minimality criterion for K_t via a decomposition test (K_t -> {K_t,1, K_t,2, ...}): if the decomposition preserves all knowledge about the observation, the original unit was not minimal; if no such decomposition exists, it is a candidate minimal unit -- offered as a way to formalize 'smallest' without prematurely fixing K_t's internal structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A sentence is a linguistic representation that may contain one or more K_t units. ... the number of sentences gives us a possible dimensional view, but not necessarily the true number of dimensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Using a repeated Nexus-server worked example (RHEL 9.8, 8 vCPU, port 8081, etc. as ten atomic statements), argues a sentence is not necessarily one K_t unit -- e.g. 'has 8 vCPUs and 31 GB RAM' contains two atomic units -- and that an observation's true dimensionality is not bounded by however many sentences currently describe it (K_t(O) subset-of all potentially observable aspects of O; 'Knowledge at t != the complete observation'); new sentences discovered later add new dimensions (K_t^11), and a corrected statement changes an existing dimension's value rather than necessarily creating a new one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WorldState_t -> Observation_t^A -> InformationState_t^A -> EpistemicState_t^A -> KnowledgeAttribution, with history H_{<=t} preserved. It then proposes K_t^{A,R} as a time-indexed knowledge attribution, dependent on participant A, extraction regime R.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reading an unread-in-this-batch corpus document, reports its chain WorldState_t -> Observation_t^A -> InformationState_t^A -> EpistemicState_t^A -> KnowledgeAttribution (with preserved history H_{<=t}) and its participant/regime-relative K_t^{A,R}; explicitly distinguishes this from the dialogue's own new atomic-K_t hypothesis, treating the latter as a possible FURTHER refinement (one measurable statement per observation dimension) rather than something the attached document already established, and notes the document's own probability treatment P(K_t^A|F_t^A) as extraction-uncertainty, explicitly distinct from Knowledge itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q = domain of possible items; K subset-of Q = a particular knowledge state; script-K = space/family of possible states; probability (Q, script-K, p). The crucial distinction is: script-K != K_t != P(K_t | O_{<=t}).
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports a Knowledge Space Theory (KST) formalism (Q as domain of possible items, K as a particular state, script-K as the family of possible states, with probability attached as (Q,script-K,p)) as external confirmation that a knowledge-space, a particular state, and a probability distribution over states are three genuinely different objects; notes KST's own K_t is a learner-capability state (a different, narrower sense than the dialogue's broader KnowledgeOS K_t), and that the dialogue's atomic-unit idea asks a question KST does not answer: what is the state/value of each individual knowledge unit within a state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(k_i | E) is the epistemic confidence/degree of support for proposition k_i, given the available evidence. ... k_i != P(k_i)
b_rows_sample.statement: Repeatedly insists that probability attached to a knowledge unit must be given a precise referent -- distinguishing P(claim is true), P(claim is supported by available evidence), P(the measurement/extraction is correct), and P(claim belongs to K_t) as not necessarily the same quantity, and stating k_i != P(k_i): the knowledge unit itself is not identical to its probability. Also proposes that not every claim's epistemic measure need be a probability -- it could be categorical status, an interval, a confidence level, measurement uncertainty, or logical entailment strength -- warning against forcing every kind of knowledge into probability merely because probability is mathematically convenient.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Atomic propositions -> Evidence -> Measured epistemic state -> Ideal/reference state -> distance -> knowledge gap. This potentially connects several previously separate strands: Phase 1 ... Phase 2 ... KST ... Pritchard ... Zero ... Knower ... Evidence ... Kernel
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 'candidate unifying structure, not yet a completed theory': Observation -> Atomic propositions -> Evidence -> Measured epistemic state -> Ideal/reference state -> distance -> knowledge gap, claimed to potentially connect the corpus's Phase-1 (knowledge as relationship/justification/state evolution), Phase-2 (Knowledge Space/participant/time/projection), KST (Q, script-K, K_t, p), Pritchard's belief-counts-as-knowledge conditions, Zero, Knower-ownership, Evidence/determination, and Kernel-as-substrate strands, while explicitly warning against collapsing these prematurely.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EpistemicState = Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports a multidimensional EpistemicState formulation (Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity) as already-derived corpus material supporting the general direction of a non-monolithic, multi-axis knowledge state, alongside a stated distinction chain Knowledge!=Reality, Observation!=Knowledge, Dimension!=Statement, Dimension!=Value, Guidance!=Decision, Zero!=Knowledge, Parsing!=Knowledge, Parsing!=Dimension-Discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What is the minimum structure of k_t such that the entire KnowledgeOS theory — evidence, probability, context, identity, Zero, evolution, proposal, decision and action — can be derived without adding arbitrary architectural assumptions?
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes the file's line of inquiry with an explicit unresolved research question: what is the minimal structure of the atomic knowledge unit k_t from which the rest of the theory (evidence, probability, context, identity, Zero, evolution, proposal, decision, action) could be derived without arbitrary additional architectural assumptions -- stated as the next major research question rather than answered.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A sentence is not automatically a knowledge dimension merely because it is syntactically a sentence. ... independent knowledge-bearing statement -> candidate dimension
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the minimal-knowledge-unit hypothesis k_t(O) (smallest independently meaningful unit of knowledge about an observation at t) with the qualification that sentence != dimension automatically -- semantic independence of a statement must be established before it counts as a candidate dimension; and states K_t(O) is necessarily partial, since K_t(O) subset-of D(O), the full (possibly unbounded) dimension set of the observation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: k_i = (O, d_i, v_i, t, E_i, p_i, q_i)
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the atomic knowledge claim to a seven-field tuple k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,p_i,q_i) -- observation, semantic dimension, claimed value, time, evidence/information source, epistemic probability, and an explicit information-sufficiency/support status q_i -- with K_t(O)={k_1,...,k_n} as the resulting knowledge state, and reiterates that dimensionality is representation-relative rather than an intrinsic finite property of the object (a sentence maps to one or more atomic claims, not one-to-one).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t should not be identified with a Kripke model or possible-world set. Status: research conclusion / compatibility constraint, not yet kernel theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the DEL document's rejection of K_t as a Kripke pointed model (M,w) strengthens (without proving) the corpus's independently-developed atomic-tuple direction k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,C_i,p_i,q_i); explicitly records the possible-worlds rejection as a research conclusion/compatibility constraint, not a kernel theorem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The missing step is: $$(O,E_{\le t},A,G,EC)\;\longrightarrow\;K_t(O)$$ ... The file itself almost explicitly states this as the unanswered operation \(\mathcal M\): $$\mathcal M:(O,E_{\le t},A,G,EC)\rightarrow K_t(O)$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the central missing derivation in the reviewed K_t/observation research as the unanswered operation M:(O, E_{<=t}, A, G, EC) -> K_t(O) -- the document being reviewed 'repeatedly approaches it but never actually derives it' -- where O is observation, E_{<=t} is evidence up to time t, A is the Knower/agent, G is goal, and EC is the epistemic contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
The document currently jumps: $$Oightarrow k_1,\ldots,k_nightarrow K_t$$ But **where do \(k_1,\ldots,k_n\) come from?** ... dimension \(
eq\) statement \(
eq\) knowledge atom \(
eq\) value ... but does not provide the transformation between them.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects/sharpens the atomic-knowledge-unit hypothesis by pointing out that reviewed prior work jumps directly from an observation O to a set of atoms k_1..k_n without deriving them, despite itself distinguishing dimension != statement != knowledge atom != value; the transformation producing the atoms from an observation is never actually supplied.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$O\overset{\mathcal D}{\longrightarrow}\{d_i\}\overset{\mathcal P}{\longrightarrow}\{q_i\}\overset{\mathcal E}{\longrightarrow}\{s_{i,t}\}\overset{\mathcal A}{\longrightarrow}K_t$$ where \(O\) = observation; \(d_i\) = observable/aspect dimension; \(q_i\) = atomic proposition ...; \(s_{i,t}\) = epistemic state/value ...; \(K_t\) = resulting knowledge state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes decomposing the missing K_t-construction derivation into a four-operator pipeline: D (observation to dimensions {d_i}), P (dimensions to atomic propositions {q_i}), E (propositions to epistemic-state values {s_i,t}), and A (values aggregated to K_t) -- named as the candidate missing derivation, with a worked Nexus-server example (RHEL 9.8, 8 vCPU, 31GB RAM, port 8081, etc. -> candidate atoms k_i) illustrating that no mathematical operation currently justifies which atoms are 'correct'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$K_t=\operatorname{Aggregate}(k_{1,t},\ldots,k_{n,t})$$ and we must determine whether that aggregation is: a set, vector, graph, distribution, state space, or something else. That is explicitly still open in the document.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names a second missing derivation: the aggregation of individual knowledge atoms {k_i,t} into the knowledge state K_t, with the mathematical type of the aggregate (set/vector/graph/distribution/state-space/other) left explicitly open.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I think the previous research was looking for the missing piece **one level too late**. We kept asking: What is \(D(K_t,I_t)\)? But before that, we need: How is \(K_t\) generated? And before that: How is an observation transformed into atomic knowledge propositions?
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the research programme has been searching for the missing piece at the wrong level: the priority order of open questions should be (1) how is an observation transformed into atomic knowledge propositions, before (2) how is K_t generated from those atoms, before (3) what is the comparison function D(K_t,I_t) -- reordering research priority away from the distance function toward the earlier construction steps.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$R_t\overset{\operatorname{Obs}_A}{\longrightarrow}O_t^A$$ where \(R_t\) is the world/reality state and \(O_t^A\) is what participant \(A\) can observe. ... consistent with the document's existing ... projection $$\Pi_A:\mathcal W\rightarrow\mathcal E_A$$ but the document explicitly treats that projection as a hypothesis rather than an established theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies an even deeper missing derivation than K_t-construction: the theory currently starts with observation O as given, but a genuinely epistemological theory must also derive Reality -> Observation, i.e. R_t --Obs_A--> O_t^A (world/reality state to what a specific participant A can observe), consistent with but more explicit than the document's existing (hypothesis-only) projection Pi_A: W -> E_A.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **The Knowledge-State Construction Derivation** $$R_t\rightarrow O_t^A\rightarrow Q_t^A\rightarrow E_t^A\rightarrow K_t^A$$ followed by: $$(A,G,EC)\rightarrow I_t^A\rightarrow Z_t^A\rightarrow\text{investigation/action}\rightarrow K_{t+1}^A$$ ... it has not derived the **transformations between the nodes**.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names and consolidates the overall missing derivation as 'The Knowledge-State Construction Derivation': R_t -> O_t^A -> Q_t^A -> E_t^A -> K_t^A, followed by (A,G,EC) -> I_t^A -> Z_t^A -> investigation/action -> K_{t+1}^A; concludes the prior work has developed almost all the nodes of this pipeline but never derived the transformations connecting them, and that the most important missing function is the decomposition of M:(O,E_{<=t},A,G,EC) -> K_t into formally justified sub-operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is `Qualify` a **precondition**? | **REFUTED** -- `P4`. `Poss(a,s)` gates *whether an action may occur*; `Qualify` concerns *whether a qualification holds of a knowledge item*. Different type, different pipeline position | **REFUTED**
b_rows_sample.statement: Negative test P4 (Reiter solves Qualify) is applied and Qualify-as-precondition is REFUTED: Reiter's Poss(a,s) gates whether an action may occur, while Qualify concerns whether a qualification holds of a knowledge item -- a different type occupying a different pipeline position, so the correspondence fails.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is `Qualify` an **operation**, or an **epistemic boundary rather than a computable function**? | **not decided.** And `KR-CONTR-EVAL` makes the third option live: the programme has already found one case where an apparent function was really a **boundary** (`reason`) | **OPEN**
b_rows_sample.statement: Whether Qualify is an operation or an epistemic boundary (rather than a computable function) is not decided; KR-CONTR-EVAL is cited as precedent making the 'boundary' option live, since that programme already found one case (reason) where an apparent function was really a boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reiter's sensing works because knowledge is modelled by an **accessibility relation** and is **factive**. `R1` decided that KnowledgeOS's object is `A_t`, an attribution, and that no component may assert `Knows`.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sensing does not transfer cleanly from Reiter to KnowledgeOS: Reiter's sensing relies on knowledge being modelled by a factive accessibility relation, but R1 decided KnowledgeOS's object is A_t (an attribution), and no KnowledgeOS component may assert Knows.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [NEG] Reiter's knowledge operator and KnowledgeOS's object are different predicates by governance decision, not by oversight. Sensing's formal guarantees are guarantees about a factive operator and do not carry over to attribution.
b_rows_sample.statement: [NEG]-tagged finding: Reiter's knowledge operator and KnowledgeOS's object are different predicates BY GOVERNANCE DECISION, not by oversight; therefore sensing's formal guarantees, which are guarantees about a factive operator, do not carry over to attribution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SUBJECT Realization | Boundary | Future-Excluded ... EPISTEMIC Observed | Inferred | Proposed | Decided | Open ... PROVENANCE Governed | Ungoverned | External-corroborative ... REPRODUCIBILITY Reproducible | Non-reproducible
a_rows_sample.statement: Four orthogonal evidence dimensions are reconciled and adopted for C-10 establishment: SUBJECT (what is it about: Realization/Boundary/Future-Excluded), EPISTEMIC (how well known: Observed/Inferred/Proposed/Decided/Open), PROVENANCE (whose artifact: Governed/Ungoverned/External-corroborative), and REPRODUCIBILITY (can anyone re-derive it: Reproducible/Non-reproducible), with the note that a DECIDED claim and a Reproducible claim are not the same thing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Option A is not merely unjustified -- it is unsatisfiable. the full conjunction E1 and ... and E10 includes E10, and E10 requires a history that cannot exist at establishment time. Adopting Option A would make C-10 PERMANENTLY UNESTABLISHABLE
a_rows_sample.statement: Impossibility proof: adopting the full conjunctive criteria set E1 through E10 as the establishment test (Option A) would make C-10 permanently unestablishable, because E10 (operational repeatability, a sustained history) structurally cannot be satisfied at a single point in time -- disposing of Option A on evidence rather than preference.

a_rows_sample.anchor: L1 PROTOTYPE ESTABLISHMENT ... L2 OPERATIONAL ESTABLISHMENT ... L3 AUTHORITATIVE ESTABLISHMENT ... Which level flips D2? recommended: L2, not L1. one instance satisfying E1/E2/E7/E8 is still compatible with an incidental outcome
a_rows_sample.statement: A three-level assurance-level model (Option C) is recommended: L1 Prototype (semantic realized once, discriminable, reconstructable), L2 Operational (repeated across >=2 acts, lifecycle transitions real), L3 Authoritative (change history exists); D2 is recommended to flip only at L2, not L1, because a single instance is still compatible with an incidental (not owned) outcome, and E6 (repeatability across >=2 acts) is what actually shows ownership.

a_rows_sample.anchor: does the acting context OWN the outcome, or does it FALL OUT of another context's mechanism? Counterfactual form: remove C-10 -- does the receipt still appear? If yes, E7 fails.
a_rows_sample.statement: Criterion E7 (Boundary discrimination) is given an explicit counterfactual satisfaction test: remove the candidate capability and ask whether the outcome still appears; if yes, the outcome falls out of another context's mechanism (as CAP-01 bootstrap and BC-7 tokenRef leakage do for C-10) and E7 fails.

a_rows_sample.anchor: eight of nine names appear NOWHERE in the estate ... The adopted criteria have no artifact in the governed record. They arrive as names only ... this is the THIRD occurrence of the same pattern in this estate
a_rows_sample.statement: D5 is registered as DECIDED (adopting the establishment-criteria model in principle) while Governance simultaneously discovers that eight of the nine criterion names (E1-E9) appear nowhere as defined content in the estate, since the commissioned Architecture analysis had not yet been delivered -- the record holds nine labels, not nine criteria, and 'a name is not a criterion' is stated as a governing discipline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D5 STATUS: DECIDED -- framework adopted. PROVENANCE STATUS: Architecture artifact pending. ... A good model is not the same as an authorized architectural deliverable.
a_rows_sample.statement: D5-AMD1 corrects D5's status to a two-part form (framework decision adopted; provenance/Architecture-artifact status separately pending), reaffirms Option A (full conjunction) must not be assumed as the minimum sufficient combination, and keeps the commission open (Reading 2: it stands, the eventual Architecture artifact must define E1-E10) rather than closing it as complete.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
b_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EKS-01: the HANDOFF token's tokenRef acted as the de-facto knowledge channel and taught a lane the superseded path. A lane was taught the old path by its workflow record's tokenRef.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-5/F-5a: BC-7's HANDOFF tokenRef is performing de-facto knowledge distribution it does not own, evidenced by EKS-01 where a lane was taught a superseded path via its own workflow record's tokenRef -- the strongest evidence for a distinct C-10 (Knowledge Distribution) capability rather than 'Communication' in the ordinary sense.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
b_rows_sample.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Distinguish, explicitly: ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified. Receipt is not proof of application or compliance.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10's knowledge-distribution lifecycle is to be modelled as seven distinguished states (ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified); a receipt is never proof of application or compliance, only of a narrower claim.

type_signature.codomain: one of seven distinguished lifecycle states

b_rows_sample.anchor: that recurrence is itself evidence bearing on C-10 -- governed knowledge arriving outside the governed channel -- and the analysis may note it, but per AMD1 must not assume C-10 owns it.
b_rows_sample.statement: A pattern of substantive external input (a cited review, a 925-line brainstorming document, external research) repeatedly arriving outside the governed channel is recorded as evidence potentially bearing on C-10, but explicitly not assumed to be owned by C-10 without further decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-10 is NOT the whole path. Its smallest coherent boundary is APPLICABILITY + RECEIPT. ... What nothing owns is: (a) deciding WHICH governed knowledge is applicable to THIS assignment, and (b) evidencing that the executing session actually holds the CURRENT version.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10's smallest coherent capability boundary is proposed to be applicability determination plus receipt (not the whole created->published->selected->retrieved->delivered->acknowledged->applied->verified path), since creation/publication is BC-1's, retrieval/bootstrap is BC-6's, and only applicability-determination and receipt-evidencing are genuinely unowned.

b_rows_sample.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
b_rows_sample.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

b_rows_sample.anchor: receipt <= application <= understanding <= compliance ... A receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged. ContextApplied and ContextVerified are different claims requiring different evidence, and no receipt can supply them.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10's seven-state receipt model is elaborated with an explicit ceiling: a receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged, never ContextApplied or ContextVerified, and OQ-J is reformulated from a yes/no 'is the receipt authoritative' question into five separately-tested claims (delivery, possession, applicability, execution, compliance authority), of which a receipt can carry at most the first two.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Option C binds the receipt to an act the estate has never performed, that nobody owns, and that the analysis says a receipt cannot carry.
b_rows_sample.statement: Option C for C-10 receipt semantics is found unsatisfiable as worded, because it would require the receipt to reference an 'applicability decision' (ContextSelected) that never occurs and has no owner in the estate -- the same referent-gap defect noticed independently in several later documents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: establishes an applicability reference -- a pointer to decision A. does NOT establish the correctness of applicability -- whether A was right. A pointer to a judgement is not an assertion that the judgement was sound.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-10 Decision 1 (Option C) resolves OQ-J's authority defect by distinguishing an applicability REFERENCE (a pointer, which the receipt may carry) from applicability CORRECTNESS (whether the referenced judgement was sound, which the receipt does not establish) -- 'AUTHORITY IS CLAIM-SCOPED' is recorded as the invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The decision commits the receipt to reference an applicability decision that the estate never produces. ... This is no longer an authority problem -- it is an existence problem about the referent.
b_rows_sample.statement: A distinct 'referent gap' (as opposed to the already-solved authority gap) is identified: the decided receipt is required to reference an applicability decision (ContextSelected) that the estate never actually produces and nobody owns, so a conforming receipt is not presently populatable -- left as PO/ARB's to decide (optional/null reference, vs. a standing obligation to build ContextSelected).

b_rows_sample.anchor: No typed KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt structure is adopted -- and, verified: no such type exists anywhere in the estate
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit confirmation that no typed receipt data structure (e.g. KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt) exists anywhere in the estate's code or docs; schema design is deferred to Architecture and is not created by this semantic decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Recommended: YES -- C-10 exists as a capability, with realization NONE and its outer boundary OPEN. The load-bearing argument is D1 itself. ... A decision fixing the authoritative claim boundary of C-10's artifact presupposes a subject for that artifact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance recommends C-10 existence = YES, arguing that D1's decided receipt-claim boundary presupposes a subject for that claim, supported by a distinct reason to change, a distinct outcome, and two genuinely unowned stages sharing one purpose (applicability + receipt) -- this recommendation is later overturned by the PO/ARB (S0120 D2) as conflating a decided semantic with a performed capability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Of five activities: one occurs and is owned elsewhere; four do not occur at all. Evidence of C-10 having occurred: none
b_rows_sample.statement: Applying the ten-question existence test to the estate's evidence: of C-10's five constituent activities (applicability, delivery, acknowledgement, claim-scoped receipt, invalidation/reconciliation), only one occurs and it is owned by other contexts (BC-6/BC-7), while four never occur at all and have no owner -- the counter-evidence supporting the later NOT YET ESTABLISHED verdict.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adopting the receipt as authoritative state would supply limb one of the estate's existence test. A decision framed as constitutive would decide existence by the back door -- which this act forbids. Framed as a boundary specification, it does not.
b_rows_sample.statement: A distinction between a 'constitutive' decision (which would establish existence as a side effect) and a 'boundary specification' decision (which defines a candidate scope without establishing existence) is drawn, warning that D3 must be framed as the latter to avoid silently satisfying the D2 existence test.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C -- SPLIT. Fits every decided constraint. It matches OQ-J's 2-of-5 result ... applicability / transport / execution are already owned or already excluded
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommendation: Option C (SPLIT) for D3 -- C-10 would own only the receipt/attestation lifecycle and state (receipt identity, lifecycle state, invalidation, completeness), explicitly excluding applicability determination, delivery transport, session execution, identity binding, dispute adjudication, execution authority, and compliance/application.

a_rows_sample.statement: A pattern of substantive external input (a cited review, a 925-line brainstorming document, external research) repeatedly arriving outside the governed channel is recorded as evidence potentially bearing on C-10, but explicitly not assumed to be owned by C-10 without further decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EKS-02: three capabilities are routinely conflated -- policy authorship, policy derivation (C-13, live), policy enforcement (C-14, absent). Only the third is missing, and no role fixes it; a gate does.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-7: policy authorship, policy derivation (C-13, live via doc-placement.php), and policy enforcement (C-14, initially claimed absent) are three distinct capabilities routinely conflated; the fix for a missing enforcement capability is a mechanical gate, not a named role.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a unifying invariant candidate falls out of it: both control-plane capabilities are defeated by the SAME failure -- self-assertion by the gated party. C-5 is defeated by self-declared separation; C-14 by self-declared compliance.
b_rows_sample.statement: A unifying control-plane invariant candidate (proposed, not adopted): a gate's verdict may not be issued by the party the gate constrains; observed support: G-1 already enforces this for closure, and CAP-09's write-paths are deliberately closed, so the invariant is already implemented twice but never stated as a general rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the answer is NO: on current evidence there is no distinct C-14 capability. Every stage of the policy-to-effect path is already performed by an owned capability ... What EKS-02 actually records is not a missing capability but a missing COVERAGE
b_rows_sample.statement: Original (later superseded) analysis: mapping the nine-stage policy-to-effect path (definition, derivation, evaluation, observation, admission control, blocking/halt, escalation, audit, advisory tripwires) against evidence shows every stage already performed by an owned capability (chiefly CAP-09/BC-3), so EKS-02's gap is a coverage gap within existing machinery, not a missing capability -- this categorical denial is itself withdrawn later by Amendment 1 as a category argument doing an existence test's job.

b_rows_sample.anchor: On current evidence, no platform-wide C-14 capability is established. A Tier-1 enforcement pattern exists within CAP-09, but whether that instance constitutes the same capability as C-14 remains OPEN.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-14's categorical denial is replaced by provisional wording: no platform-wide C-14 capability is established, but a Tier-1 enforcement pattern exists within CAP-09, and whether that instance is the same capability as C-14 is OQ-H, unresolved -- with four separated sub-concerns (policy tier assignment, coverage mapping, enforcement execution, enforcement assurance), each with a different owner status.

b_rows_sample.anchor: registry.yaml carries AST-007 at governance_tier ... adoption: adopted, PRE_ACTION. That is policy enforcement — mechanical, blocking, in production today.
b_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies a prior claim that C-14 policy-enforcement is 'absent': one asset (AST-007) is mechanically blocking and in production, so the correct classification is a coverage gap for the narrower C-15 claim, not an absent capability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: an enforcement capability must have a real effect path. A script that prints a warning is monitoring or advisory control, not enforcement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes policy definition/evaluation/observation/monitoring/enforcement/admission-control/runtime-blocking/escalation/audit as separate capabilities, and defines enforcement strictly as requiring a decision point, protected operation, effect, failure mode, override model, and auditability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four unowned capabilities (corrected state)
b_rows_sample.statement: Records four capabilities with no bounded-context owner as one control loop (policy/knowledge DEFINED in BC-1 -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES <- C-5 ATTESTS): C-5 Separation attestation (existence YES, cross-context control-plane assurance capability, NOT a bounded context); C-10 Knowledge distribution (existence NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred); C-14 Policy enforcement (existence CONTESTED, deferred); C-19 Communication composition (existence YES, stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern, NOT a bounded context). Flagged as a proposal finding, not adopted architecture; C-10/C-14 existence remain UNDECIDED.
