group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'epistemic-sufficiency-decision-preconditions-assurance-composition-algebra' POSSIBLY relates to 'cross-context-consistency-contradiction-reconciliation-authority-algebra' (batch B0022). Note: S0936's Step 41 (final file of this batch): formalizes decision-specific, three-valued (T/F/Unknown) epistemic sufficiency, structural (non-averaged) mandatory-precondition composition, minimal-sufficient-evidence-set (set-cover) selection, assurance diversity/independence/staleness, the policy-vs-mathematics DDD boundary, and the critical Human-in-the-loop != Independent human validation AI-governance principle, unifying Steps 34/35/41 into an Acquire->Allocate->Stop cycle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every D285 hypothesis must be typed before it can be tested. In particular, an equality-dependent hypothesis must explicitly state which equality relation it uses. Otherwise a formally correct-looking proposition may be mathematically vacuous. ... This is the single most important methodological correction to emerge from the entire Gītā-KnowledgeOS integration effort.
a_rows_sample.statement: States and elevates the typing/equality-naming requirement to the status of the single most important methodological finding of the entire Gita-integration effort, generalizing beyond the single artifact (D285-5) where it was first observed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1 Source proposition; 2 KnowledgeOS translation (do not assume correspondence valid merely because terms sound similar); 3 Formal hypothesis; 4 Type/equality audit (structural/semantic/observational/identity/other; check non-vacuity); 5 Independent KnowledgeOS derivation (would KOS require this even if the Gītā had never been consulted?); 6 Executable/falsifiable test; 7 Classification (mathematical/architectural/DDD/philosophical analogy/Gītā corroboration/unresolved hypothesis/governance decision).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the finalized seven-stage D285-x protocol in full, most notably promoting the independence question (stage 5) to a mandatory, distinct pipeline stage rather than an optional afterthought, and expanding the classification stage to seven explicit categories.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Equality Specification: NONE REQUIRED — and stating that is part of the discipline. The Θ rejection is a type-checking result (four carriers), not an equality claim. Asserting an equality here would be a category error.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates correct application of the frozen seven-stage protocol's type/equality-audit stage by explicitly recording that no equality relation applies to this particular result (it is a type-checking failure, not an equality claim) -- itself a disciplined act, since asserting an unnecessary equality specification would itself be a category error under the same protocol.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is an exemplary artifact. It demonstrates exactly the methodological discipline that Steps 285-286 require. ... The artifact is accepted as written and should serve as the template for all D285-x tests.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues a full acceptance verdict for the D285-5 action/result formal test (t285_reconcile.py's T-E, S2063), the only unconditionally-accepted artifact identified across this batch's entire Step 285/286 research thread, and designates it the template for all subsequent D285-x work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Required Structure: 1 Property Statement; 2 Trivial vs Substantive; 3 Execution; 4 Qualification; 5 Equality Specification; 6 Independence; 7 Classification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the mandatory 7-section template every future D285-x formal-test artifact must follow, generalized from the structure of the accepted D285-5 artifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Next Steps: 1 Adopt this artifact as template for D285-x; 2 Execute remaining D285-x tests using this format; 3 Ensure each test specifies its equality relation; 4 Document independence for each property; 5 Classify each property using R0-RX.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues five forward-looking directives operationalizing the acceptance verdict, most notably requiring every future test to explicitly specify its equality relation -- directly anticipating (and setting up) the self-critical re-examination of the reviewer's own prior K-projection claim carried out in the companion script t285_equality.py (S2072).

b_rows_sample.anchor: **A hypothesis cannot be tested until its types and equality relation are explicit.**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the strongest methodological result as: a hypothesis cannot be tested until its types and equality relation are explicit; frames the seven-stage protocol (source proposition -> KOS translation -> formal hypothesis -> type/equality audit -> independent KOS derivation -> falsifiable test -> classification) plus the seven-section D285 artifact template as the resulting stronger research discipline, and states the four equality relations must be treated as non-interchangeable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### 5 · Equality Specification ⭐ **NONE REQUIRED** — no equality is asserted. The matrix relates *candidates to consequences*, which is an implication, not an identity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the mandated 7-part D285-x template to itself and explicitly notes an edge case: this artifact requires NO equality specification, since it relates candidates to consequences (an implication) rather than asserting any identity between two things — distinguishing 'implication' from 'identity' as a template category.

a_notations: 1 Source proposition, 2 KnowledgeOS translation, 3 Formal hypothesis, 4 Type/equality audit, 5 Independent KOS derivation, 6 Executable/falsifiable test, 7 Classification
b_notations: Property Statement / Trivial vs Substantive / Execution / Qualification / Equality Specification / Independence / Classification

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'd285-frozen-seven-stage-typing-protocol' POSSIBLY relates to 'd285x-seven-part-test-template' (batch B0050). Note: The finalized, HPA-accepted seven-stage protocol required for every future D285-x artifact: (1) Source proposition -- exact Gita chapter/verse, textual claim vs interpretation; (2) KnowledgeOS translation -- never assume validity merely because terms sound similar; (3) Formal hypothesis -- mathematical or DDD statement; (4) Type/equality audit -- name the specific equality relation and check non-vacuity; (5) Independent KnowledgeOS derivation -- would KOS require this without the Gita; (6) Executable/falsifiable test -- concrete positive/negative cases; (7) Classification -- separate mathematical/architectural/DDD/philosophical-analogy/Gita-corroboration/unresolved/governance results. Explicitly declared the 'single most important methodological correction' of the whole Gita-KnowledgeOS integration effort, superseding the looser 7-part template proposed in the D285-5 review (S2070).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Complexity Results table: FL0 Polynomial ... ALC PSpace-complete ... ALC+TBox ExpTime-complete
a_rows_sample.statement: Complexity table across DL languages (FL0/AL polynomial; ALE NP-complete; ALU coNP-complete; ALC/ALCN PSpace-complete; ALC+TBox/role constructors ExpTime-complete), offered as the empirical basis a KnowledgeOS implementation must weigh when selecting a representation language.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Expressiveness <-> Tractability ... reasoning by cases can become computationally explosive
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Theory-level methodological principle: a KnowledgeOS representation is not justified merely because it is semantically expressive; its reasoning consequences and computational tractability must be explicitly considered — an independent formal reason to resist building one universal semantic structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Expressiveness does not justify computational complexity by itself ... Semantic question: What distinctions can the representation express? Computational question: What reasoning can be performed over it, with what guarantees and cost? Neither question substitutes for the other.
b_rows_sample.statement: Methodological principle: expressiveness does not justify computational complexity by itself; every proposed KnowledgeOS semantic mechanism must separately answer a semantic question (what distinctions can it express) and a computational question (what reasoning can be performed, with what guarantees/cost) — neither substitutes for the other, grounded in KR&R's expressiveness/tractability tradeoff and reasoning-by-cases explosion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is a tradeoff between the expressiveness of a representation language and the difficulty of reasoning ... A slight increase in the expressiveness of a Description Logic may result in a drastic change in the complexity of reasoning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Expressiveness/tractability tradeoff restated with a concrete 'computational cliff' example: adding role restriction to FL- makes subsumption coNP-hard, versus polynomial without it — offered as underlying principle for [PROP]-status constructs in KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic expressiveness and computational tractability must be evaluated separately ... A richer representation is not automatically a better KnowledgeOS representation ... a candidate kernel operation is not admissible merely because it is semantically elegant. It must satisfy: Expressiveness+Soundness+Completeness_declared-domain+ComplexityBound
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives a kernel-selection criterion from the expressiveness/tractability tradeoff: a candidate kernel operation must satisfy Expressiveness + Soundness + Completeness_(declared domain) + ComplexityBound where appropriate; explicit warning that tableau soundness/completeness for a specified DL semantics does not imply KnowledgeOS as a whole can or should be complete. Kernel remains NOT SELECTABLE; this is a selection criterion, not a kernel definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR.1 Representation Layers ... KR.6 Open-World Constraint ... KR.9 Transition ... KR.10 Expressiveness and Tractability
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes inserting a 10-section 'KNOWLEDGE REPRESENTATION AND STRUCTURED REASONING' theory addition (KR.1 Representation Layers, KR.2 Reasoning Cn_S, KR.3 Subsumption, KR.4 Classification, KR.5 Consistency, KR.6 Open-World Constraint, KR.7 Evaluation via reasoning-service family, KR.8 Explanation/Missing Assumptions, KR.9 Transition/successor-state with Boundary!=FrameAxiom retained, KR.10 Expressiveness/Tractability), consolidating all the file's individually-derived candidates into one proposed section.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR.1 Representation Layers [PROP] ... KR.6 Open-World Constraint [ESTABLISHED] — Supported by DL's open-world semantics ... KR.10 Expressiveness and Tractability [ESTABLISHED] — Now a KnowledgeOS methodological principle

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mechanism records authority; it does not grant authority ... All 20/20 grants carry humanActRef, and registeredBy has exactly one observed value — governance.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the highest-confidence current-state finding of this EKS baseline: measured directly from 9 work items and 20 grants, every grant references a human act and is registered by governance, evidencing that the mechanism records rather than creates authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Grants with validity information 0/20 ... Grants with delegation information 0/20 ... Grants with ownership information 0/20 ... Was this authority valid at a particular historical point in time? ... a current-state limitation, not a future-architecture opinion.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the principal measured weakness: authority is durably recorded but the record contains no validity/delegation/ownership fields, so historical authority cannot be reliably reconstructed at any past point in time.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An AI agent must not be interpreted as an authority holder merely because it executes a permitted activity.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that AI-process participation is current infrastructure, but permitted execution must not be confused with holding authority, following directly from the observed authority model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet call 'Delegation modelling' IMPLEMENTED-BUT-IMPLICIT merely from the progressive narrowing of grants ... change it to: OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR — SEMANTIC INTERPRETATION UNKNOWN.
a_rows_sample.statement: A second-session self-critique downgrades an earlier classification: observed progressive grant-narrowing behaviour does not establish that the business concept 'Delegation' exists in EKS, so the classification must be weakened to avoid treating an interpretation as an architectural fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would also weaken: Rule governance — PARTIAL ... because that potentially mixes exploratory Track 2 Rule semantics with the current EKS implementation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns that classifying 'Rule governance' as PARTIAL risks importing the exploratory Track-2 Rule Model's semantics into a current-state EKS claim, and proposes the safer statement that Rule-like mechanisms exist while the Track-2 model itself is not established as current architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EKS turns engineering activity into evidence, evidence into bounded recommendations and decisions, and decisions into durable engineering knowledge — while keeping architectural authority with humans and keeping future architectural evolution evidence-gated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Behavioral governance demonstrated (tier 5 record): the governance changed real contributor behavior (a new artifact written instead of amending a frozen one) even where the automated gate was absent — 'tool enforcement says you COULDN'T; behavioral governance says you COULD have, and you didn't.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Cites a demonstrated case where governance discipline changed contributor behavior even without a mechanical enforcement gate, distinguishing tool-enforced impossibility from behavioral-governance restraint.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This document establishes a CURRENT ARCHITECTURE BASELINE. It does not authorize: redesign; refactoring; bounded-context creation; service extraction; event-bus introduction; platform extraction; adaptive learning; technology migration.

a_rows_sample.statement: Tests CAPPI's orthogonality/double-dampening warning against the estate and finds the real analog is not a reliability-vs-uncertainty conflation but a triple redundant implementation of one cohesion measurement (three independent LCOM4 collectors) with no canonical winner.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Goal\neq EpistemicContract
a_rows_sample.statement: A goal (e.g. 'Migrate Nexus to the target architecture') does not itself contain all knowledge conditions necessary to execute it safely (e.g. RollbackVerified, FirewallRequirementsKnown are not stated by the goal); therefore Goal ≠ EpistemicContract. States this was already discovered in Step 25D and now needs formalizing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DeriveContract(G,S)\rightarrow EC_G
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the conceptual operation DeriveContract(G,S) -> EC_G, where S is the set of governing sources {Constitution, Policy, ADR, Rule, Scope, HumanInstruction, RiskModel, DomainModel, Law, Standard}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EC\in KnowledgeState
a_rows_sample.statement: The epistemic contract EC is itself an artifact needing identity, version, scope, owner, source, derivation, validity period, authority, and status; therefore EC ∈ KnowledgeState — 'the system needs knowledge to define what knowledge is required.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: EC=(R,\Gamma,A,V)
a_rows_sample.statement: First contract tuple definition: EC=(R,Γ,A,V) where R=requirements, Γ=satisfaction rules, A=authority/provenance, V=validity/version; R={r1,...,rn}, each requirement individually traceable (e.g. r1: RollbackVerified derived via MigrationGoal -> ArchitecturePolicy -> RiskRule -> RollbackVerified).

a_rows_sample.anchor: RequirementLineage
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines RequirementLineage: a traceable derivation tree from Goal through governing artifacts (Architecture Constitution, Security Policy, Migration Risk Rule) to a concrete requirement (Rollback Verification), enabling the system to answer 'why does KnowledgeOS require a rollback test?' with a traced derivation rather than 'the AI thought it was important.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: HumanInstruction\rightarrow Goal/Intent. Then Goal+Governance\rightarrow Contract.
a_rows_sample.statement: A human instruction (e.g. 'Please migrate Nexus next weekend') contributes only Intent/Goal, not an automatic requirement like RollbackVerifiedRequired; requirements arise from Goal+Governance -> Contract, which 'prevents instructions from silently becoming rules.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Scope=Production... A requirement concerning a development Nexus instance may therefore be NotApplicable
a_rows_sample.statement: Scope must be an explicit contract dimension: a requirement scoped to Production is NotApplicable to a development instance, demonstrated via example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose the architecture constitution says: Production changes require architectural assurance... r_{architecture-assurance} becomes part of R_G
a_rows_sample.statement: A constitution-derived requirement (architecture-assurance) is 'not an opinion' but a normative consequence of the constitution, illustrating Constitution -> Requirement derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ADR\rightarrow Requirement
a_rows_sample.statement: An ADR fixing TargetArchitecture=ContainerizedNexusPro can satisfy TargetArchitectureKnown if authoritative/current, and may also generate additional derived requirements (e.g. r_container-security) from the target architecture's own security constraints — ADR -> Requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose a risk analysis identifies RISK: DataLoss... The contract can derive RollbackVerified. This is important because the requirement may not come directly from an architecture rule. It may emerge from Goal+Risk.
a_rows_sample.statement: A risk-model-derived requirement path: RISK:DataLoss -> Control:VerifiedRestore -> RollbackVerified, showing requirements can emerge from Goal+Risk rather than only from architecture rules.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CandidateRequirement\neq ContractRequirement
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes valid derivation (Source+Rule -> Requirement) from mere AI suggestion (LLM -> CandidateRequirement): the latter is not automatically binding, giving 'another deterministic assurance boundary': CandidateRequirement ≠ ContractRequirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SourceExists? SourceApplicable? AuthorityValid? RuleSatisfied? ... CandidateRequirement\rightarrow ContractRequirement
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes the LLM's role as proposing candidate requirements from unstructured sources (e.g. reading a 300-page policy), which KnowledgeOS records as CandidateRequirement; only after a deterministic/governed check (SourceExists?, SourceApplicable?, AuthorityValid?, RuleSatisfied?) does CandidateRequirement -> ContractRequirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge requirement / Evidence requirement / Validation requirement / Governance requirement / Operational requirement
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a five-way requirement-type taxonomy with predicate forms and examples: Knowledge requirement Known(r) (e.g. TargetVersionKnown), Evidence requirement EvidenceExists(r) (e.g. BackupEvidenceAvailable), Validation requirement Validated(r) (e.g. RestoreTestPassed), Governance requirement Authorized(r) (e.g. ArchitectureApprovalGranted), Operational requirement State(r) (e.g. TargetEnvironmentProvisioned).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic-Governance Contract ... or simply AssuranceContract. I would not rename it yet
a_rows_sample.statement: Because the requirement taxonomy now spans Knowledge+Evidence+Validation+Authorization+State rather than only 'what must be known,' proposes the more precise terms 'Epistemic-Governance Contract' or 'AssuranceContract,' but explicitly declines to rename yet since 'Epistemic Contract' retains conceptual value — records the naming issue rather than resolving it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EC_{Nexus}=\{r_1,\ldots,r_8\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example contract for Nexus with an 8-row requirement table (current version known, target architecture known, repository inventory verified, backup verified, rollback verified, network requirements resolved, security assessment complete, architecture approval), each tagged by Type and Blocking?=Yes, giving 'Zero something precise to evaluate.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: r_1\land r_2\Rightarrow r_3 ... r_4\lor r_5
a_rows_sample.statement: Requirements may have logical relations: conjunction (BackupExists AND RestoreTestPassed => RollbackCapabilityEstablished) and disjunction (either approved rollback procedure A OR B suffices), concluding 'EpistemicContract is a constraint system.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: BackupExists ... RestoreValidated ... RollbackVerified ... MigrationEligible
a_rows_sample.statement: Requirement dependency graph diagram lets Zero determine not just which requirements are unmet but 'which gap blocks downstream requirements' — e.g. if BackupExists=Unknown, RestoreValidated and RollbackVerified cannot be established, so RootGap=BackupExists rather than three unrelated gaps; described as 'much more efficient' and 'extremely useful for Lord.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Closed(EC)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines contract closure: Closed(EC) holds if every requirement has a semantic definition, an authority, a satisfaction rule, applicable scope, validity, and dependency definition; otherwise Closed(EC)=False, becoming 'another assurance gate.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: UndefinedRequirement\Rightarrow InvalidContract
a_rows_sample.statement: An AI-created requirement like r9: SystemMustBe"HighlySecure" with no satisfaction predicate makes Evaluate(K,r9) non-deterministic; therefore UndefinedRequirement => InvalidContract — 'the contract is defective.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contract normalization: natural-language sources normalized into canonical requirements like RollbackProcedureExists and RollbackProcedureTested; natural language remains provenance
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes contract normalization: an LLM can help normalize vague natural-language sources ('Make sure the migration is safe') into canonical, structured, executable requirements while the natural language remains provenance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not invent a new theory. Do not assume that previous ChatGPT conclusions are canonical. Do not assume that Claude's conclusions are canonical. ... Reconcile -> formalize -> test -> close -> only then innovate.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the governing audit principle for Step 276: neither prior research stream (Claude nor ChatGPT) is treated as canonical by default; the task is to determine from corpus and executable evidence alone which foundations are closed, under the sequence reconcile -> formalize -> test -> close -> innovate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [E] Explicit ... [D] Derived ... [X] Experimental ... [I] Implementation ... [R] Reconstruction ... [N] Normative ... Never silently convert [R] or [N] into [E].
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the six-value evidence-hierarchy tagging scheme (Explicit/Derived/Experimental/Implementation/Reconstruction/Normative) required for every conclusion in the audit, with an explicit prohibition on silently upgrading a Reconstruction or Normative tag to Explicit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CLOSED ... CONDITIONALLY CLOSED ... PARAMETRIC ... OPEN ... CONTRADICTED ... REQUIRES NORMATIVE DECISION. This classification is explicitly required by the attached prompt.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires every foundational construct to receive exactly one of six closure-status labels: CLOSED, CONDITIONALLY CLOSED, PARAMETRIC, OPEN, CONTRADICTED, REQUIRES NORMATIVE DECISION -- superseded within the same session by Layer 2's four-orthogonal-dimension scheme.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not require algebraic closure unless the theory actually needs it. ... It may be that KnowledgeOS defines a minimal semantic kernel, while individual bounded contexts add operations. ... O_core subseteq O_domain
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires testing (not assuming) whether O_core is closed under composition, and hypothesises O_core may be a minimal semantic kernel with individual bounded contexts adding further domain-specific operations (O_core subseteq O_domain) rather than every domain operation belonging to the mathematical kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Defined != WellTyped != Decidable != Executable != Validated. This distinction is explicitly required by the attached prompt.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires a five-level distinction (Defined, WellTyped, Decidable, Executable, Validated) to be applied to every foundational symbol (K, O_core, Sigma, Evidence, Policy, Assessment, T, Identity, Equality) in a computational-closure matrix, rather than treating 'defined' as sufficient for any stronger claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The previous audit insufficiently distinguished four forms of closure. ... SemanticClosed(X) ... FormalClosed(X) does NOT imply that an implementation exists. ... ComputationalClosed(X) ... GovernanceClosed(X) ... These four forms of closure must NEVER again be conflated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 1 ('revised Step 276') introduces four explicitly orthogonal closure dimensions -- Semantic (stable canonical interpretation), Formal (typed definition, no implementation implied), Computational (executable decision procedure), Governance (who may define/change/authorize it) -- replacing Layer 1's single six-state scheme, with a seven-value revised vocabulary (CLOSED, CONDITIONALLY CLOSED, PARAMETRIC, FORMALLY CLOSED/COMPUTATIONALLY OPEN, COMPUTATIONALLY CLOSED/GOVERNANCE OPEN, OPEN, CONTRADICTED).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = (A_t,R_t,E_t,Sigma_t,H_t,Z_t,L_t,T_t,G_t,C_t,M_t) ... with the conditional minimality result: K_minimal | O_core = (A,R,Sigma,E) ... Status: K: CLOSED
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 1 asserts (contradicting the more cautious canonical-construction package's own findings, S1783/S1784) that K is CLOSED with conditional minimality K_minimal|O_core=(A,R,Sigma,E), and that O_core is 'structurally closed' as a six-part union O_S∪O_E∪O_H∪O_G∪O_Q∪O_X, though O_G (governance operations) is 'not uniformly computationally demonstrated'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy: SemanticClosed + FormalPartial + ComputationalConditional + GovernanceOpen ... KnowledgeOS does NOT need to mathematically derive: what the organization's policy ought to be. ... Normative Governance -> Policy Specification -> KnowledgeOS Policy Evaluation
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 1's central Policy/Authority finding: Policy and Authority are each SemanticClosed+FormalPartial+ComputationalConditional+GovernanceOpen; KnowledgeOS need not derive legitimate policy internally, only consume a valid policy specification (Normative Governance -> Policy Specification -> KnowledgeOS Policy Evaluation, not the reverse), and a fixed supplied policy Pi* can be computationally evaluable even though Policy itself remains externally governed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The revised Step 276 establishes: The KnowledgeOS core is substantially closed, but the governance boundary is not yet closed. ... STEP 277 -- The next step should therefore not attempt to invent a new Policy theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 1's HPA ruling and Step 277 recommendation: Core Theory approx Closed, Governance Interface != Closed, Policy Evaluation != Policy Governance; recommends Step 277 answer 'what is the canonical typed interface between normative Governance and the computable KnowledgeOS kernel'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would rewrite Step 276 rather than continue from its previous verdict. The previous Step 276 made several closure claims that are stronger than the evidence supports. ... K, epistemic vocabulary, equality/identity, the complete transformation family, minimality, and end-to-end execution were NOT y
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 explicitly rewrites rather than continues Part 1, withdrawing Part 1's optimistic closure claims as stronger than the evidence supports; the corpus itself (cited) already stated K, epistemic vocabulary, equality/identity, the complete transformation family, minimality and end-to-end execution were not yet finally established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Defined | A formal candidate has been specified | Derived | ... follows from corpus evidence or mathematical reasoning | Demonstrated | An actual test/execution establishes the claimed property | Closed | No unresolved foundational dependency remains for the claim
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 introduces a four-level hierarchy (Defined -> Derived -> Demonstrated -> Closed) replacing Part 1's four-dimension scheme, explicitly forbidding a construct from being labelled CLOSED merely because it has reached the Defined or Derived level.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the previous claim: K_minimal | O_core = (A,R,Sigma,E) has not yet been proven. ... Until that experiment has been completed: K_minimal is a hypothesis, not a theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 downgrades Part 1's K_minimal=(A,R,Sigma,E) claim from CLOSED to a hypothesis pending the actual per-component deletion/replacement counterfactual experiment (remove x, check whether every mandatory distinction/operation is still representable) -- not yet completed at the time of writing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'K should not be defined independently of T.' That statement must NOT be retained as written. ... Definition(K) != Adequacy(K, T) ... K definition and K sufficiency for T must remain separate proof obligations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 corrects an earlier formulation ('K should not be defined independently of T'): a representation of K can be defined independently; only its ADEQUACY for a given transformation family T is dependent on T -- Definition(K) and Adequacy(K,T) must remain separate proof obligations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STEP 277 -- Canonical Transformation Inventory and O_core Closure ... we cannot responsibly declare K minimal until we know what operations the state must support.
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 redirects the next step away from Part 1's recommendation (Policy/Authority interface formalization) to 'Step 277 -- Canonical Transformation Inventory and O_core Closure', on the ground that K-minimality cannot responsibly be declared before the complete transformation family T is established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The previous Step 276 conclusion: 'Foundations are overwhelmingly closed.' is withdrawn. ... KnowledgeOS has a substantial, coherent candidate theoretical framework, but its canonical mathematical closure has NOT yet been demonstrated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Part 2's final HPA ruling formally withdraws Part 1's headline conclusion ('foundations are overwhelmingly closed'), replacing it with 'substantial coherent candidate framework, canonical mathematical closure not yet demonstrated', restating Defined != Derived != Demonstrated != Closed as the governing correction.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
each iteration introduces additional difficulty; knowledge operators do not automatically iterate. ... K(p)
ot\Rightarrow K(K(p)) ... K^n(p)
ot\Rightarrow K^{n+1}(p) ... Verified(x)\Rightarrow Verified(Verification(x)) [dangerous hidden assumption] ... Verification 
eq MetaVerification
a_rows_sample.statement: Epistemic Iteration Non-Closure: K^n(p) does not imply K^{n+1}(p) unless a separate rule/evidence/authority establishes the higher-order knowledge, guarding against 'the system knows X therefore it knows that it knows X'; applied to the Determination->Decision->Action->Observation->Verification chain to reject the hidden assumption Verified(x)=>Verified(Verification(x)), giving Verification != MetaVerification (Verify(V) requires its own evidence/context/authority). Status: [DERIVED].

a_rows_sample.anchor: EPISTEMIC LIMITS, ACCESSIBILITY AND KNOWLEDGE STANDING ... EL.1 Factivity [DECIDED/REINFORCED] ... EL.7 Structural Unknowability [PROP — strong research candidate] ... EL.8 Assertion Responsibility [PROP]
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an 8-section theory addition 'EPISTEMIC LIMITS, ACCESSIBILITY AND KNOWLEDGE STANDING': EL.1 Factivity [DECIDED/REINFORCED], EL.2 Epistemic Non-Transparency [DERIVED], EL.3 Knowledge Iteration [DERIVED], EL.4 Evidence Relativity [PROP], EL.5 Margin of Error [PROP], EL.6 Accessibility (distinguishing Truth/Knowability/Accessibility/ActualKnowledge) [DERIVED], EL.7 Structural Unknowability [PROP-strong], EL.8 Assertion Responsibility [PROP], consolidating this file's individual candidates into one proposed section.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mr Magoo sees a tree ... he cannot know for any i that the tree is not i inches tall ... Therefore, KK (knowledge that one knows) fails. ... Further iterations of knowledge are even harder to achieve.
a_rows_sample.statement: The Mr-Magoo margin-for-error argument formally derives the failure of the KK principle (knowledge does not imply knowledge of knowledge) via a step-by-step discrimination-limit argument, and notes iterations beyond the second are progressively harder to achieve -- the original formal source for the epistemic-iteration-non-closure principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What to Adopt: Knowledge First ✅ ... Evidence = Knowledge ✅ ... Factive Mental States ✅ ... Non-Luminosity ✅ ... Margin for Error ✅ ... Anti-KK ✅ ... Knowledge Rule for Assertion ✅ ... What to Reject: Knowledge = Justified True Belief ❌ ... Phenomenal Evidence ❌ ... Transparency of Rationality ❌ ... Luminosity of Mental States ❌ ... Recommendation: Integrate ... into KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2
a_rows_sample.statement: Final recommendation table adopts all seven listed concepts (Knowledge First, Evidence=Knowledge, Factive Mental States, Non-Luminosity, Margin for Error, Anti-KK, Knowledge Rule for Assertion) unconditionally (all checked, no [PROP]/[OPEN] hedging) and recommends integrating them directly into KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 -- a materially stronger, less-hedged recommendation than the same-day review (S2528), which instead treats most of these as PROP-status research candidates and explicitly places 'Evidence=Knowledge' on its own rejection list.

b_rows_sample.anchor: one may not be in a position to know what one's own rational requirements or evidence are. ... Epistemic Property not=> Accessible(Epistemic Property) ... Knowledge(p) not=> Knowledge(Knowledge(p)) ... Eval(P) may be undefined or epistemically inaccessible even when P has a determinate truth value.
b_rows_sample.statement: States epistemic non-transparency as the strongest single Williamson contribution: an epistemic property (knowledge, evidence, rational requirement) can hold without being accessible to the subject/evaluator, giving a formal reason Sat/Eval_c must not be assumed luminous and must not be confused with truth. Status: [DERIVED - very strong].

b_rows_sample.anchor: anti-luminosity: roughly, the assumption that whenever a condition obtains, one is automatically in a position to know that it obtains. His argument uses reliability, limited discrimination and sorites-style reasoning. ... EvidenceExists(e) not=> EvaluatorCanEstablish(EvidenceExists(e)) ... Zero(K)=0 not=> Known(Zero(K)=0). This is very important for Zero.
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the non-transparency principle specifically to Zero and consistency/completeness: EvidenceExists(e) not=> EvaluatorCanEstablish(EvidenceExists(e)); Consistent(K) not=> Known(Consistent(K)); Complete(K) not=> Known(Complete(K)); Zero(K)=0 not=> Known(Zero(K)=0) -- i.e. even if a knowledge base actually has zero gap, the system may be unable to know that it has zero gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EPISTEMIC LIMITS, ACCESSIBILITY AND KNOWLEDGE STANDING ... EL.1 Factivity [DECIDED/REINFORCED] ... EL.7 Structural Unknowability [PROP — strong research candidate] ... EL.8 Assertion Responsibility [PROP]
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an 8-section theory addition 'EPISTEMIC LIMITS, ACCESSIBILITY AND KNOWLEDGE STANDING': EL.1 Factivity [DECIDED/REINFORCED], EL.2 Epistemic Non-Transparency [DERIVED], EL.3 Knowledge Iteration [DERIVED], EL.4 Evidence Relativity [PROP], EL.5 Margin of Error [PROP], EL.6 Accessibility (distinguishing Truth/Knowability/Accessibility/ActualKnowledge) [DERIVED], EL.7 Structural Unknowability [PROP-strong], EL.8 Assertion Responsibility [PROP], consolidating this file's individual candidates into one proposed section.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not adopt KnowledgeOS = Williamson's epistemology ... Do not adopt Knowledge = Evidence ... He explicitly says the equation does not amount to an analysis of either concept. ... Do not adopt Sat = Knowledge ... Confidence = Margin ... Unknown = Unknowable ... Contr = Epistemic inconsistency ... Zero = Structural unknowability
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit rejection list of seven tempting imports: KnowledgeOS=Williamson's-epistemology, Knowledge=Evidence (noting Williamson himself says his E=K thesis is not an analysis of either concept), Sat=Knowledge, Confidence=Margin, Unknown=Unknowable, Contr=EpistemicInconsistency, Zero=StructuralUnknowability -- these remain separate concepts.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A condition C is defined to be luminous if and only if: For every case alpha, if in alpha C obtains, then in alpha one is in a position to know that C obtains. ... The Sorites-Style Argument [feeling cold at dawn to hot at noon] ... Therefore the condition 'one feels cold' is not luminous.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the formal definition of luminosity (a condition C is luminous iff whenever C obtains one is in a position to know it obtains) and the full sorites-style anti-luminosity argument (feeling-cold-at-dawn-to-hot-at-noon, imperceptible per-step changes) proving virtually no mental state is luminous, including love/hope examples generalizing beyond feeling-cold; grounds the epistemic-non-transparency principle with its original formal source material.

b_rows_sample.anchor: if we combine the argument with the principle that one is always in a position to know what one's evidence is, the upshot is that one has exactly the same evidence in an ordinary case and its sceptical counterpart. ... Luminous conditions are trivial. Since mental states are non-luminous, the sceptical argument fails. ... KnowledgeOS should not adopt a phenomenal conception of evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses non-luminosity to dissolve philosophical scepticism (if evidence were luminous, evidence would be identical between ordinary and sceptical cases, but mental states are non-luminous so the argument fails) and explicitly rejects the phenomenal conception of evidence (a converging-to-the-empty-set sequence of ever-more-private appearances), translated as: KnowledgeOS's evidence must not be modeled as private/phenomenal appearances.

b_rows_sample.anchor: just as one cannot always know what one's evidence is, so one cannot always know what rationality requires of one. ... rationality is not luminous. ... the system cannot assume that Determination is always accessible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends non-luminosity specifically to rationality (one cannot always know what rationality requires), translated as: KnowledgeOS cannot assume Determination is always accessible/transparent to the system itself.

Knowledge Rule for Assertion ✅ ... What to Reject: Knowledge = Justified True Belief ❌ ... Phenomenal Evidence ❌ ... Transparency of Rationality ❌ ... Luminosity of Mental States ❌ ... Recommendation: Integrate ... into KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2
b_rows_sample.statement: Final recommendation table adopts all seven listed concepts (Knowledge First, Evidence=Knowledge, Factive Mental States, Non-Luminosity, Margin for Error, Anti-KK, Knowledge Rule for Assertion) unconditionally (all checked, no [PROP]/[OPEN] hedging) and recommends integrating them directly into KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 -- a materially stronger, less-hedged recommendation than the same-day review (S2528), which instead treats most of these as PROP-status research candidates and explicitly places 'Evidence=Knowledge' on its own rejection list.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'INV-004'

a_rows_sample.anchor: First axiom: determinism ... EA_\rho(E,P,C)=EA_\rho(E,P,C) ... The same evidence, context and policy must produce the same assessment. If an LLM happens to produce different results each time, that variability cannot be hidden inside the mathematical definition. It must be represented as InferenceUn
a_rows_sample.statement: States the determinism axiom: fixed (evidence, proposition, context, policy) must produce the same EA_ρ; LLM output variability must be represented explicitly as InferenceUncertainty rather than hidden inside the aggregation function — LLM variability ≠ epistemic randomness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Permutation invariance ... EA_\rho(\{e_1,e_2,e_3\},P,C) = EA_\rho(\{e_3,e_1,e_2\},P,C) ... The final assessment cannot depend merely on ingestion order.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the permutation-invariance axiom: the final EA must not depend on the order evidence was ingested (document today, database tomorrow, LLM result later, human review afterward).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Duplicate invariance ... e_1\equiv e_2 ... EA(E\cup\{e_1,e_2\}) = EA(E\cup\{e_1\}) ... prevents document duplication → artificial certainty. This should be a kernel invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: States duplicate invariance — identical/equivalent evidence items must not increase the assessment beyond a single instance — flagged explicitly as a candidate kernel invariant preventing 'document duplication → artificial certainty'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Derived-evidence non-inflation ... e_2=Transform(e_1) ... e_1\prec e_2 should imply IncrementalIndependentSupport(e_2\mid e_1)=0 unless the policy explicitly identifies an additional independent observation contained in e_2. This is particularly important for Document\rightarrow LLM\rightarrow Summa
a_rows_sample.statement: States the derived-evidence non-inflation axiom: if e2 is a transform of e1, its incremental independent support is 0 by default, unless policy identifies an additional independent observation within it — critical for Document→LLM→Summary→Report chains.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Irrelevance invariance ... Rel(e,P,C)=0 then EA(E\cup\{e\},P,C)=EA(E,P,C) ... The evidence is not deleted. It simply has no contribution ... NonRelevant\neq Nonexistent
a_rows_sample.statement: States irrelevance invariance: zero-relevance evidence leaves EA unchanged but is not deleted from the record — NonRelevant ≠ Nonexistent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Supporting monotonicity ... e\Rightarrow P then S^+(E\cup\{e\})\ge S^+(E) ... e\Rightarrow\neg P implies S^-(E\cup\{e\})\ge S^-(E). This does not mean that the final conclusion must become more certain. Because new opposing evidence can simultaneously appear.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a refined monotonicity axiom applying separately to S+ and S- components (each only increases with admissible independent supporting/opposing evidence respectively), explicitly not implying the overall conclusion becomes more certain, since opposing evidence can appear simultaneously.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contradiction preservation ... E^+\neq\emptyset and E^-\neq\emptyset then the assessment must retain both. EA(P)=(S^+,S^-,Conflict,\ldots) rather than EA(P)=singleScore ... S^+=0.91, S^-=0.88 must not become 0.03 because 0.03 conceals the existence of a serious conflict.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the contradiction-preservation axiom, called 'one of the most important axioms': when both supporting and opposing evidence exist, EA must retain both as structured fields rather than collapsing to a single net score, since e.g. S+=0.91,S-=0.88 collapsing to 0.03 would conceal a serious conflict.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conflict sensitivity ... S^+>0 and S^->0 then Conflict(P)=Active subject to the conflict rule. ... Conflict_\rho(E^+,E^-,C) \rightarrow \{NoConflict,Potential,Active,Unresolved\} ... conflict detection is not simply arithmetic subtraction.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Conflict_ρ(E+,E-,C)→{NoConflict,Potential,Active,Unresolved} as a four-valued policy-governed function, stating conflict detection is not simple arithmetic subtraction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency sensitivity ... e_1\prec e_2 ... e_2 must not be treated as equivalent to an independent observation. Agg(E\cup\{e_2\}) \neq Agg(E\cup\{e_2^{independent}\}) ... This is a very strong test for candidate aggregation models.
a_rows_sample.statement: States dependency sensitivity as a strong test axiom: aggregating a dependent evidence item must differ from aggregating an otherwise-identical independent one (Agg(E∪{e2}) ≠ Agg(E∪{e2^independent})).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown dependency must remain unknown ... Dependency(e_1,e_2)=Unknown ... cannot validly transform that into Independent(e_1,e_2)=True. UnknownDependency \Rightarrow No\ automatic\ independence\ credit. This does not mean UnknownDependency\Rightarrow Dependent. We retain Unknown. This is a three-va
a_rows_sample.statement: States that unknown dependency must remain Unknown throughout aggregation — no automatic independence credit, but also not automatically treated as Dependent — reaffirming the three-valued epistemic property from earlier files.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Corroboration ... e_1\perp_\rho e_2 and both support P, then the assessment should be capable of representing corroboration Corroboration_\rho(e_1,e_2)>0. But we deliberately do not specify Corroboration=0.4 yet. That is policy territory.
a_rows_sample.statement: States corroboration must be representable (Corroboration_ρ(e1,e2)>0 for independent, mutually supporting evidence) without fixing its numeric value, which remains policy territory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Temporal sensitivity ... e_1 is current and e_2 is stale. We cannot treat them as identical. But Stale(e_2)\neq Delete(e_2). TemporalValidity affects contribution, not historical existence. ... A 2024 architecture document can still be valuable evidence about what existed in 2024, even if it is not
a_rows_sample.statement: States temporal sensitivity: stale evidence has reduced contribution but is never deleted (Stale ≠ Delete); temporal validity affects contribution, not historical existence — a 2024 document remains valid evidence about 2024 even if not about today.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Context sensitivity ... Contribution(e,P,C) ... Contribution(e,P,C_1) \neq Contribution(e,P,C_2) is perfectly legitimate. ... relevant to historical architecture reconstruction; irrelevant to a production migration decision; highly relevant to an audit of the 2024 environment. Evidence has no univer
a_rows_sample.statement: States context sensitivity: the same evidence can legitimately have different contributions in different contexts (illustrated by 'Nexus 3.69' being relevant/irrelevant/highly-relevant depending on the question asked) — 'Evidence has no universal relevance.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance preservation ... Basis(EA)\subseteq E ... EA\rightarrow EvidenceLineage must be recoverable. This gives us auditability. A KnowledgeOS conclusion should be able to answer "Why do you believe this?" with an actual evidence graph.
a_rows_sample.statement: States provenance preservation: EA must retain a recoverable evidence basis/lineage so a conclusion can answer 'Why do you believe this?' with an actual evidence graph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No evidence creation ... E=\emptyset then Agg(E)=NoEvidence not Agg(E)=0.5 and certainly not Agg(E)=Confirmed. This is a critical distinction between absence of evidence and neutral evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a no-evidence-creation axiom: aggregating the empty set must yield NoEvidence, never a neutral scalar (0.5) or Confirmed — distinguishing absence-of-evidence from neutral-evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No certainty creation from aggregation alone ... StrongEvidence\not\Rightarrow Truth. Instead StrongEvidence \Rightarrow StrongSupport under the policy. Then another rule determines whether StrongSupport \Rightarrow AcceptedAssertion. That is a conclusion policy, not an evidence law.
a_rows_sample.statement: States StrongEvidence ⇏ Truth; strong evidence only yields StrongSupport under policy, and whether StrongSupport becomes an AcceptedAssertion is a separate conclusion-policy decision, not an evidence law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This gives us three mathematical layers ... Layer A — Evidence aggregation E\rightarrow EA ... Layer B — Epistemic conclusion EA\rightarrow A ... Layer C — Decision A,I,P\rightarrow Decision ... Evidence\neq Conclusion\neq Decision
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes three mathematical layers — Layer A Evidence aggregation (E→EA), Layer B Epistemic conclusion (EA→A), Layer C Decision (A,Ideal,Purpose→Decision) — reaffirming Evidence ≠ Conclusion ≠ Decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now we can define admissible aggregation ... Agg_\rho is admissible if it satisfies the applicable KnowledgeOS axioms \mathcal A=\{A_1,\ldots,A_n\} ... Agg_\rho\models\mathcal A ... This is the correct mathematical way to compare Bayesian, Dempster–Shafer, weighted, saturating, etc.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines admissibility formally: Agg_ρ ⊨ A (satisfies the axiom set A) as the correct way to compare candidate frameworks (Bayesian, Dempster-Shafer, weighted, saturating).

a_rows_sample.anchor: But not every axiom must be universal ... kernel invariants: A_1 Identity preservation, A_2 Provenance preservation, A_3 Contradiction preservation, A_4 No automatic independence ... policy properties: A_5 Corroboration rule, A_6 Saturation, A_7 Decision threshold, A_8 Probability interpretation. Th
a_rows_sample.statement: Splits the axiom set into four kernel invariants (Identity preservation, Provenance preservation, Contradiction preservation, No automatic independence) versus four policy properties (Corroboration rule, Saturation, Decision threshold, Probability interpretation), called essential for DDD.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The emerging KnowledgeOS Evidence Constitution ... E-K1 — Evidence identity ... E-K2 — No duplicate inflation ... E-K3 — Provenance preservation ... E-K4 — Dependency awareness ... E-K5 — Unknown is not independent ... E-K6 — Contradiction preservation ... E-K7 — Context dependence ... E-K8 — Tempor
a_rows_sample.statement: Provisionally formulates a ten-item candidate 'KnowledgeOS epistemic constitution': E-K1 Evidence identity (e=e, explicitly represented), E-K2 No duplicate inflation, E-K3 Provenance preservation (Assessment⇒Basis), E-K4 Dependency awareness, E-K5 Unknown is not independent, E-K6 Contradiction preservation, E-K7 Context dependence, E-K8 Temporal preservation (Stale≠Deleted), E-K9 No truth by aggregation (EvidenceAssessment≠Truth), E-K10 No decision by aggregation (EvidenceAssessment≠Decision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: we should not invent a universal formula for "evidence strength." ... What is an Evidence Assessment? ... An Evidence Assessment is a structured, policy-governed evaluation of the evidential support, opposition, uncertainty, provenance, and applicability of a proposition within a specified context.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Evidence Assessment EA=(S+,S-,U,Q,V,D,X,Π) — Supporting evidence, Opposing evidence, Uncertainty, Quality, Validity/temporal, Dependency structure, Context/applicability, Provenance — as a structured, policy-governed evaluation that explicitly excludes Truth: EA evaluates evidence, it does not establish reality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: First principle: support and opposition must be separate ... S^+=0.9, S^-=0.8 does not mean S=0.1 ... There is substantial evidence on both sides. That is a conflict. ... Conflict(P) ... True if S^+>0 and S^->0 ... the conflict should retain C=(E^+,E^-,R,Ctx,Status)
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires support S+(P) and opposition S-(P) to be kept separate rather than collapsed to a net difference S=S+-S- (e.g. S+=0.9,S-=0.8 must not become S=0.1, since it hides substantial evidence on both sides); defines Conflict(P) as True when both are positive, retaining a structured conflict record (E+,E-,R,Ctx,Status).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Normalize evidence before aggregation ... N_\rho: \mathcal E\rightarrow\mathcal E' ... identity resolution; provenance resolution; semantic classification; relevance determination; temporal validity; dependency classification; polarity determination. ... Aggregation must occur after normalization. T
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a normalization function N_ρ:E→E' performing identity resolution, provenance resolution, semantic classification, relevance determination, temporal validity, dependency classification, and polarity determination, and states the major architectural invariant: aggregation must occur only after normalization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence contribution is multidimensional ... q(e,P,C)=(r,q_s,q_r,q_t,q_c,q_p) ... Relevance ... Source quality ... Reliability ... Temporal validity ... Contextual applicability ... Provenance quality. This prevents us from collapsing fundamentally different properties. ... Highly authoritative / I
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-dimension evidence-contribution vector q(e,P,C)=(r,q_s,q_r,q_t,q_c,q_p) — Relevance, Source quality, Reliability, Temporal validity, Contextual applicability, Provenance quality — illustrated with authoritative-but-irrelevant vs authoritative-and-relevant evidence to show a single scalar quality value would hide the difference; states Quality≠Relevance, Reliability≠Validity, ProvenanceQuality≠SourceAuthority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The first mathematical operation: contribution filtering ... F_\rho(e,P,C) determines whether evidence is admissible ... F(e,P,C)=0 if Relevance(e,P,C)=0 ... irrelevant evidence contributes 0 but remains stored. ... NonContributing\neq Nonexistent
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a contribution-filtering function F_ρ(e,P,C) that zeroes out irrelevant evidence's contribution to the current assessment while the evidence remains stored, giving the distinction NonContributing ≠ Nonexistent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency-adjusted contribution ... Document D ↓ LLM A ↓ Human report ... All three may support P, but their contributions are not simply additive. ... aggregation equivalence class [e]_{\sim_O} ... Same underlying observation is aggregated once unless policy explicitly states otherwise.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an aggregation equivalence class [e]~_O for evidence sharing the same underlying observation (e.g. Document D → LLM A → Human report, all supporting P), with the default rule that same-underlying-observation evidence is aggregated once unless policy states otherwise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Independent corroboration ... e_1\perp_\rho e_2 ... Corroboration_\rho(e_1,e_2)>0 subject to the selected policy. This is where saturation or Bayesian models may become useful. But importantly: Corroboration is a policy operation, not a universal mathematical law.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Corroboration_ρ(e1,e2)>0 for operationally independent supporting evidence pairs, noting saturation or Bayesian models may apply, but insisting corroboration is a policy operation rather than a universal mathematical law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What algebraic properties should aggregation have? ... Permutation invariance: Agg(e_1,e_2)=Agg(e_2,e_1) ... Duplicate invariance: e_1\sim_Oe_2 we require Agg(e_1,e_2)=Agg(e_1) ... Monotonicity: E\subseteq E' then Agg(E')\geq Agg(E) ... Boundedness: 0\leq Agg(E)\leq1 ... Dependency sensitivity: e_2\
b_rows_sample.statement: States five candidate algebraic properties for an aggregation operator Agg: permutation invariance (order-independence), duplicate invariance (same-observation pairs aggregate as one unless configured otherwise), monotonicity under added independent supporting evidence, boundedness (normalized measure in [0,1]), and dependency sensitivity (derived evidence must not add the same increment as an independent observation).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Important correction: not every useful assessment is monotonic ... e_1\Rightarrow P and then e_2\Rightarrow\neg P ... A support score for P should decrease if the assessment incorporates contradictory evidence. ... we should not demand universal monotonicity of the complete Evidence Assessment. ...
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the preceding monotonicity axiom: only SupportAggregation (aggregating supporting evidence alone) may be monotonic; the CompleteAssessment (incorporating contradictory evidence too) need not be monotonic, since discovering e2⇒¬P should legitimately decrease overall support for P.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence Assessment is therefore not a scalar algebra ... EA_\rho: (\mathcal E,G_E,P,C)\rightarrow\mathcal A ... The scalar s\in[0,1] is merely one possible projection: \pi_s:\mathcal A\rightarrow[0,1]. This is a very important result. ... ScalarScore=\pi_\rho(EvidenceAssessment). This fits our earl
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues EA_ρ maps into a structured assessment space A (not a scalar algebra), with any scalar score s∈[0,1] arising only via a projection π_s:A→[0,1] — ScalarScore=π_ρ(EvidenceAssessment) — reaffirming that the scalar is derived, not fundamental.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD model ... EvidenceAssessment ... AssessmentId, Proposition, Context, SupportingEvidence, OpposingEvidence, DependencyGraph, QualityAssessment, UncertaintyAssessment, ValidityAssessment, AssessmentPolicy, AssessmentBasis, CreatedAt ... An EvidenceAssessment must preserve the evidential basis from
b_rows_sample.statement: Sketches the EvidenceAssessment aggregate (AssessmentId, Proposition, Context, SupportingEvidence, OpposingEvidence, DependencyGraph, QualityAssessment, UncertaintyAssessment, ValidityAssessment, AssessmentPolicy, AssessmentBasis, CreatedAt) with the invariant that it must preserve its evidential basis — never storing a bare confidence number without a reconstructible 'why'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assessment provenance ... Basis(EA)\subseteq \mathcal E ... Policy(EA)=\rho ... Context(EA)=C ... This gives us reproducibility: EA=f_\rho(E,C). The same evidence under a different policy may legitimately produce EA_{\rho_1}\neq EA_{\rho_2}
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires every EvidenceAssessment to carry Basis(EA)⊆E, Policy(EA)=ρ, and Context(EA)=C for reproducibility (EA=f_ρ(E,C)), noting the same evidence may legitimately yield different assessments under different policies.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Example — Nexus version ... Evidence 1 API ... Evidence 2 Filesystem ... Evidence 3 LLM summary of Evidence 1 ... Evidence 4 Old architecture document → 3.70 ... Supporting observations: API, Filesystem ... Derived support: LLM summary ... Opposing evidence: Old architecture document ... Assessment:
b_rows_sample.statement: Works a full Nexus-version worked example with four evidence items (API, filesystem, an LLM summary derived from the API, and a stale architecture document) producing a structured assessment (supporting/derived-support/opposing/dependency/temporal/conflict fields) explicitly contrasted with a bare scalar P(Nexus=3.69)=0.93 as containing far more information.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This gives us an important distinction ... EvidenceAssessment ... Conclusion ... Decision ... What does the evidence support? ... What proposition do we currently accept? ... What should we do? ... Evidence\rightarrow Assessment\rightarrow Conclusion\rightarrow Decision not Evidence\rightarrow Decis
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three domain concepts that must not be collapsed: Evidence Assessment (what does the evidence support?), Conclusion (what proposition do we currently accept?), and Decision (what should we do?) — mandating the pipeline Evidence→Assessment→Conclusion→Decision rather than a direct Evidence→Decision shortcut.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is a major KnowledgeOS architectural boundary ... Evidence Context ... What evidence exists and how it relates. ... Assessment Context ... How evidence bears on a proposition. ... Knowledge Context ... What assertions are currently held in the Knowledge State. ... Decision Context ... What acti
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines four separate Context types as a major architectural boundary: Evidence Context (what evidence exists and how it relates), Assessment Context (how evidence bears on a proposition), Knowledge Context (what assertions the Knowledge State currently holds), and Decision Context (what action to take under a purpose/policy).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Where Zero fits ... Zero should not itself "decide truth." It detects EvidenceDeficiency, Conflict, InsufficientSupport, Staleness, UnknownDependency ... Zero: KnowledgeState + EvidenceAssessment + IdealState \rightarrow Findings
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Zero's role as detecting EvidenceDeficiency, Conflict, InsufficientSupport, Staleness, and UnknownDependency (never deciding truth), formalized as Zero: KnowledgeState+EvidenceAssessment+IdealState → Findings.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Where Lord fits ... What additional evidence or knowledge would most reduce the discrepancy? ... b_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates Lord's role — asking what additional evidence would most reduce a detected discrepancy, e.g. recommending 'acquire deployment inventory evidence' for an unverified version gap — as a much stronger recommendation than generic 'search for more information'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Where Sarathi fits ... Sarathi takes (\Delta,EA,I,P) and determines the next appropriate action: Investigate, AcquireEvidence, ResolveConflict, RefreshEvidence, ClarifyContext, ReviseIdeal, AcceptUncertainty. ... Sarathi does not manufacture evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Sarathi as taking (Δ, EvidenceAssessment, Ideal, Purpose) and choosing among seven action types (Investigate/AcquireEvidence/ResolveConflict/RefreshEvidence/ClarifyContext/ReviseIdeal/AcceptUncertainty), with the constraint that Sarathi does not manufacture evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expressiveness <-> Tractability ... reasoning by cases can become computationally explosive
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate Theory-level methodological principle: a KnowledgeOS representation is not justified merely because it is semantically expressive; its reasoning consequences and computational tractability must be explicitly considered — an independent formal reason to resist building one universal semantic structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Expressiveness does not justify computational complexity by itself ... Semantic question: What distinctions can the representation express? Computational question: What reasoning can be performed over it, with what guarantees and cost? Neither question substitutes for the other.
a_rows_sample.statement: Methodological principle: expressiveness does not justify computational complexity by itself; every proposed KnowledgeOS semantic mechanism must separately answer a semantic question (what distinctions can it express) and a computational question (what reasoning can be performed, with what guarantees/cost) — neither substitutes for the other, grounded in KR&R's expressiveness/tractability tradeoff and reasoning-by-cases explosion.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is a tradeoff between the expressiveness of a representation language and the difficulty of reasoning ... A slight increase in the expressiveness of a Description Logic may result in a drastic change in the complexity of reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Expressiveness/tractability tradeoff restated with a concrete 'computational cliff' example: adding role restriction to FL- makes subsumption coNP-hard, versus polynomial without it — offered as underlying principle for [PROP]-status constructs in KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic expressiveness and computational tractability must be evaluated separately ... a_rows_sample.statement: Derives a kernel-selection criterion from the expressiveness/tractability tradeoff: a candidate kernel operation must satisfy Expressiveness + Soundness + Completeness_(declared domain) + ComplexityBound where appropriate; explicit warning that tableau soundness/completeness for a specified DL semantics does not imply KnowledgeOS as a whole can or should be complete. a_rows_sample.anchor: Information is not knowledge. Knowledge is not understanding. Understanding is not decision. Decision is not action. The gap between information and action is the epistemic crisis.
a_rows_sample.statement: Thesis: a chain of four distinct gaps (information→knowledge→understanding→decision→action) constitutes 'epistemic crisis'; Gita Chapter 1 is claimed to be the foundational theory of this crisis, framed as the problem KnowledgeOS exists to solve.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conflict(K_t) = {D_1, D_2, ..., D_n} where D_i ≠ D_j

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gītā Chapter 3 \rightarrow rich semantic test case \rightarrow architecture validation
a_rows_sample.statement: States the epistemic status of the exercise: NOT claiming Bhagavad-gita = formal specification of KnowledgeOS, but using Chapter 3's narrative/conceptual structure as a rich semantic test case to ask whether the model can faithfully represent the epistemic situation, reasoning, conflict, guidance and action without losing distinctions; notes the source itself frames Arjuna's problem as conflicting instructions and a request for decisive determination of what is most beneficial.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q = (Intent, Context, Purpose, Alternatives, Uncertainty, DecisionNeed)
a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter 3 shows Question->Intent->DimensionDiscovery is insufficient: Arjuna's actual problem combines conflicting interpretations, uncertain action, personal purpose and a request for determination, requiring Q=(Intent,Context,Purpose,Alternatives,Uncertainty,DecisionNeed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Synthesis(A_1,A_2,Context) \rightarrow A_3
a_rows_sample.statement: Validates MoreEvidence ⇏ Resolution and Support ⊥ Resolution (Q16), and reveals a missing concept: Synthesis — resolution is sometimes not 'choose A instead of B' but A+B -> HigherOrderConcept, illustrated by Knowledge+RightlyOrientedAction=Karma-Yoga resolving the apparent Knowledge-vs-Action opposition. Adds Synthesis as a sixth Resolution strategy alongside Evidence, Reinterpretation, Prioritization, Acceptance, Deferral.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Question \rightarrow Intent \rightarrow Context \rightarrow Knowledge \rightarrow Understanding \rightarrow NormativeAssessment \rightarrow Discrepancy \rightarrow Guidance \rightarrow Decision \rightarrow Action \rightarrow Outcome \rightarrow Observation
a_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the old Knowledge->Gap->Action loop with a longer, cyclic loop (Question->Intent->Context->Knowledge->Understanding->NormativeAssessment->Discrepancy->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome->Observation), formalized as a closed epistemic control loop S_{t+1}=T(S_t,Action_t,Outcome_t,Observation_{t+1}) — action produces consequences, consequences become observations, observations update knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Our theory                          | Chapter 3                                                  | Verdict
a_rows_sample.statement: A 19-row final validation matrix scoring prior theory claims (multidimensional epistemic state, conflict is relational, support≠resolution, question has purpose, understanding≠knowledge, ideal state, structured discrepancy, scalar distance secondary, Zero/Lord/Sārathi abstractions, decision readiness, action, agency, norms, role, authority, lineage, transition system) against Chapter 3 evidence, verdicts ranging 'Strongly validated' to 'Major missing concept' (Norms, Role, Authority) to 'Needs extension' (Action, Agency).

a_rows_sample.anchor: An Epistemic–Normative–Decision–Action System
a_rows_sample.statement: Deepest conclusion: KnowledgeOS was thought to be a Knowledge State model but is actually 'An Epistemic-Normative-Decision-Action System' whose central problem is how an agent moves from imperfect understanding through knowledge, interpretation, norms, discrepancy and guidance to authorized action while preserving epistemic provenance and never confusing knowledge, recommendation and decision. Chapter 3's arc is summarized as Confusion->Question->Clarification->Knowledge->Understanding->Norm->Duty->Guidance->Decision->Action. Recommends freezing Purpose/Role/Duty/NormativeState/Authority/Intention/Agency/ActorState/LearningReadiness/Synthesis/PerceivedConflict/DecisionGap/NormativeGap and revising Q16-19 before proceeding to Q20, since Q20 would otherwise formalize a state model missing normative and agency dimensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 does not directly prove our KnowledgeOS architecture. It provides a highly structured conceptual domain from which we can derive architectural abstractions. Those abstractions must be explicitly separated from what the text actually says.
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens a second, more critical review of Chapter 3 (re-read in full rather than via search snippets) with a governing methodological correction: the text does not directly prove the KnowledgeOS architecture; it supplies a structured domain from which architectural abstractions may be derived, and these must stay explicitly separated from what the text literally says — essential for both mathematical rigor and DDD.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 = Action Theory with an Epistemic Dimension
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects S0807's framing of Chapter 3 as primarily epistemic: the chapter is titled Karma-yoga and its central problem is Knowledge/Discernment vs Action/Duty, proceeding through two paths, unavoidable action, prescribed duty, yajña, a reciprocal cosmic/social cycle, exceptional self-realized persons, action for social example, role-specific duty, desire, and regulation of senses/mind/intelligence — so 'Chapter 3 = Action Theory with an Epistemic Dimension', not 'Chapter 3 = Epistemic Theory'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ❌ "Chapter 3 proves six discrepancy dimensions"
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit 'do not freeze yet' checklist rejecting eight overclaims: Chapter 3 proves six discrepancy dimensions; proves an affective state; proves LearningReadiness as a state variable; proves Event Sourcing; Senses->Mind->Intelligence->Soul is our epistemic hierarchy; Lord/Sārathi/Zero are literally equivalent to software components; decision requires zero discrepancy; all unresolved discrepancies can be ignored. Companion 'what I WOULD freeze' list gives thirteen invariants with strong support: Knowledge≠Understanding, Understanding≠Decision, Decision≠Action, ObservedAction≠ActionMeaning, Role≠Duty, Duty≠Goal, Norm≠Evidence, Authority≠Source, CanAct≠ShouldAct, PerceivedConflict≠ActualConflict, Guidance≠Decision, Action->Outcome->StateChange, Discrepancy=typed findings relative to criteria.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Source observation \rightarrow semantic concept \rightarrow architectural inference \rightarrow formalization
a_rows_sample.statement: Final self-assessment: grades the previous (S0807) analysis by area (A for Knowledge≠Understanding, A- for normative dimension recognition, down to C+ for 'separation of source vs inference'), diagnosing the main weakness as over-formalization too early — good concepts promoted directly to mathematical dimensions. Prescribes a mandatory four-stage gate: Source observation -> semantic concept -> architectural inference -> formalization, and proposes establishing a four-column Chapter-3 extraction table (Verse -> Source concept -> Architectural concept -> Formal status [axiom/derived invariant/heuristic/analogy]) as the rigorous bridge before revising Questions 16-19, presenting a revised bounded-context pipeline diagram (Context->Actor/Knowledge/World->Understanding->{Norms,Criteria}->Zero->Discrepancy->Lord->Sārathi->Decision->Action->Outcome->World/Knowledge update) as the new baseline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 is strong conceptual evidence for the architecture's core semantic relationships. It is not a proof of our particular software architecture or mathematical formalization.
a_rows_sample.statement: A ten-row table rates Chapter 3's support as 'Strong' for: Knowledge≠Understanding, Understanding->Action, Role->Duty, Normative knowledge, Authority->Guidance, Guidance≠Action, Action->Outcome->changed situation, Observed action≠semantic meaning, Agent condition affects action/knowledge, and Context-dependence of applicable duty — called the 'semantic skeleton' of the architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Chapter 3 \rightarrow Semantic Principles \rightarrow DDD Model \rightarrow Mathematical Model \rightarrow KnowledgeOS Architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a three-layer epistemic classification for how the Gita evidence licenses claims: Layer 1 source-supported semantic principles (Knowledge->Understanding->Guidance->Decision->Action->Outcome, governed by Role+Norm+Context+Authority — 'strongly supported'); Layer 2 mathematical abstraction (S_t, Δ_t, D_t, S_{t+1}=T(...) — 'motivated but not proven'); Layer 3 KnowledgeOS implementation architecture (bounded contexts, Zero/Lord/Sārathi as components — 'not proven, requires independent validation'). Gives a derivation chain Chapter 3 -> Semantic Principles -> DDD Model -> Mathematical Model -> KnowledgeOS Architecture where each arrow is a derivation step, not a claim the source contains the software architecture. Final confidence ratings: core conceptual architecture and DDD concepts strongly supported/motivated; mathematical modelling well-motivated but needing independent validation; specific equations derived-by-us-not-source-proven; fixed discrepancy vector explicitly 'do not freeze'; concrete component architecture requires separate architectural evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Discrepancy is a Typed Set, Not a Fixed Vector ... Delta(S,C,P) = Diff(S, Expected(C,P)) where Delta is a typed set of findings ... This allows a single finding to be both Semantic and Normative; No assumption of orthogonality or separability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the discrepancy model from a fixed orthogonal vector Delta=(Delta_E,Delta_U,Delta_N,Delta_D,Delta_Decision,Delta_A) into a typed set of findings Delta(S,C,P)=Diff(S,Expected(C,P)), where each finding carries one or more types (Epistemic, Semantic, Normative, Domain, Decision, Operational, etc.) and no orthogonality/separability is assumed -- justified by the observation that a single conflict (e.g. in Arjuna's understanding) can be simultaneously epistemic, semantic, normative and decisional.
