a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T4: the DI-principle proposal explicitly wants the principle without the Spring framework, yet the kernel-technology brainstorm pairs the same principle with a recommended Spring/Kotlin runtime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL protects: identity · evidence · provenance · lifecycle · authority · invariants · temporal state / higher layers provide: assurance · analytics · inference · simulation · AI · visualization · delivery ... a PROPOSED KERNEL BOUNDARY CANDIDATE, outline supported, provenance+temporal weak.
a_rows_sample.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
a_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
a_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'nyaya-pramana-lens' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-kernel-concept' (batch B0010). Note: The classical Nyaya four-part epistemology (claim/means-of-knowledge/valid-cognition/knower) applied as an architectural lens in S0365 and S0369, distinct from the relational Navya-Nyaya lens; may already exist under a broader 'Nyaya/Tarka' label not covered by this batch's read.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now test the semantic-core hypothesis against the actual KnowledgeOS implementation. Which of these concepts are actually first-class concepts in the current system? Only evidence of actual implementation counts as implementation evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Step 114's strict test: only actual-implementation evidence counts for judging whether the Step 113 candidate concepts are first-class in the current system.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.1 — The evidence test ... T(C)=(Code,Schema,API,Tests,Runtime,Owner,Relations). S0 Terminology only, S1 Represented, S2 Behavioral, S3 Verified, S4 Operational, S5 Governed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines T(C)=(Code,Schema,API,Tests,Runtime,Owner,Relations) as the seven-dimension per-concept evidence test, classified into six grades S0-S5.

type_signature.codomain: Code x Schema x API x Tests x Runtime x Owner x Relations

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.2 — The important distinction ... A concept can therefore be S1 without being S5. For example, a Decision table may exist without the system having a genuine decision-governance model.
a_rows_sample.statement: States S1 (represented) does not imply S5 (governed), illustrated by a Decision table existing without genuine decision-governance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.3 — Evidence concept ... Code: is there an explicit evidence representation? Schema: can evidence be persisted independently? API: created/retrieved? Tests: invariants tested? Runtime: objects generated? Ownership: who decides what qualifies as evidence? Relations: can evidence support a claim,
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists the seven concrete evidentiary questions for testing whether Evidence is a first-class concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.4 — Evidence verdict rule ... Only if several of these dimensions align can we say Evidence=FirstClassSemanticConcept. Otherwise Evidence=TechnicalMetadata/Artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Evidence verdict rule: several aligned dimensions yield Evidence=FirstClassSemanticConcept, otherwise Evidence=TechnicalMetadata/Artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.5 — Observation ... Potential sources Runtime, CI, Git, Agent, Human. The critical question is whether the system distinguishes ObservedFact from Interpretation.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the critical Observation test is whether the system distinguishes ObservedFact from Interpretation, across five potential sources.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.6 — Experiment 1 ... System records 'test failed.' Is this an observation? Potentially. But if it stores only status=FAILED without source, time or context, its evidentiary value is limited. Expected: Observation=Partial unless richer semantics exist. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a bare status=FAILED value without source/time/context yields Observation=Partial; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.7 — Claim ... A claim should be distinguishable from raw document, observation, recommendation, decision. Claim: Component A violates Rule B. This claim can then be supported by Evidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a Claim must be distinguishable from raw document/observation/recommendation/decision, illustrated by a component-violates-rule claim supportable by evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.8 — Experiment 2 ... An AI agent produces 'The implementation violates the architecture.' No claim object exists. Expected: this is an assertion produced by the agent, not necessarily a first-class KnowledgeOS claim. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: an AI agent's assertion without a backing claim object is merely an agent assertion, not a first-class KnowledgeOS claim; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.9 — Decision ... We need to determine whether the implementation distinguishes Recommendation from Decision. This is one of the most important semantic boundaries.
a_rows_sample.statement: States distinguishing Recommendation from Decision as one of the most important semantic boundaries to test for.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.10 — Experiment 3 ... A generated architecture recommendation is stored in the same table as an approved architecture decision. No type, authority or lifecycle distinguishes them. Expected: DecisionSemantics=Weak. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: a recommendation and an approved decision sharing one undifferentiated table with no type/authority/lifecycle distinction yields DecisionSemantics=Weak; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.11 — Authority ... A system may have user_id and role without implementing decision authority. We need Authority→Scope→Permission→DecisionType.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Authority is harder to establish than role, requiring Authority->Scope->Permission->DecisionType beyond a bare user_id/role pair.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.12 — Experiment 4 ... User has ROLE_ARCHITECT but the system does not restrict which decisions that user may make. Expected: role exists, authority semantics are not established. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a ROLE_ARCHITECT role without decision-type restriction shows role exists but authority semantics do not; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.13 — Action ... we ask whether the system can reconstruct Who+What+Why+When+AgainstWhat+UnderWhichAuthority. This is particularly important for AI agents.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Action testing requires reconstructing Who+What+Why+When+AgainstWhat+UnderWhichAuthority, particularly important for AI agents.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.14 — Experiment 5 ... Session logs show 'file changed' but not agent identity, command, intent, authorization. Expected: ActionProvenance=Partial. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: session logs recording only 'file changed' without identity/command/intent/authorization yield ActionProvenance=Partial; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.15 — Provenance ... This may be the most important cross-cutting semantic concept. Provenance(X)=Source+Actor+Time+Transformation+Context. The actual implementation may support only some of these.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Provenance(X)=Source+Actor+Time+Transformation+Context, called possibly the most important cross-cutting semantic concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.16 — Experiment 6 ... Document has source_url. Expected: source attribution exists, but this does not establish complete provenance. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: a source_url field establishes partial source attribution, short of complete provenance; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.17 — Temporal validity ... We need to distinguish CreatedAt from ValidFrom. These are not the same. A decision can be created today but become effective next month.
a_rows_sample.statement: States CreatedAt≠ValidFrom, illustrated by a decision created today but becoming effective next month.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.18 — Experiment 7 ... Object contains created_at but no effective/supersession semantics. Expected: creation timestamp exists, temporal validity remains unproven. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: an object with only created_at and no effective/supersession fields leaves temporal validity unproven; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 114.19 — Semantic relationship test ... The concepts themselves are not enough. We need relationships. Evidence-supports->Claim. Claim-informs->Decision. Decision-authorizes->Action.
a_rows_sample.statement: States concept-level evidence is insufficient; relationships (Evidence-supports->Claim, Claim-informs->Decision, Decision-authorizes->Action) must also be tested.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We now reach the central architectural question. What is the irreducible semantic core of KnowledgeOS? A platform can contain many 'knowledge' features without actually having a coherent knowledge model.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central question: what is the irreducible semantic core of KnowledgeOS, distinguishing many 'knowledge' features from a genuinely coherent knowledge model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.1 — The semantic-core hypothesis ... Evidence→Claim→Decision→Authority→Action→Observation with Provenance and TemporalValidity cross-cutting the graph. But this is still a hypothesis. Step 113 must determine whether the implementation actually supports it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the semantic-core hypothesis Evidence->Claim->Decision->Authority->Action->Observation with cross-cutting Provenance/TemporalValidity, explicitly still a hypothesis pending implementation confirmation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.2 — The falsification principle ... Does it exist? stable identity? defined meaning? lifecycle/state? invariants? relationships? identifiable ownership? persisted/represented? implemented behavior? verified? If most answers are 'no', the concept should not be treated as part of the actual semant
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a ten-question falsification principle for admitting a candidate concept into the actual semantic core, rejecting concepts that fail most questions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.3 — Candidate 1: Evidence ... Evidence=(Identity,Source,Content/Observation,Timestamp,Provenance,Context) possibly with VerificationStatus.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the minimal Evidence tuple (Identity,Source,Content/Observation,Timestamp,Provenance,Context[,VerificationStatus]).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.4 — Experiment 1 ... We find a file architecture.md. Can we call the file itself Evidence? Not automatically. It is an artifact. It becomes evidence when the system establishes its evidentiary role. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a file is an artifact, not automatically Evidence, becoming evidence only once the system establishes its evidentiary role; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.5 — Artifact versus evidence ... Artifact→Evidence is a semantic transformation. Git commit→Observed change→Evidence. The same artifact may provide different evidence depending on context.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Artifact->Evidence is a semantic transformation, not identity, illustrated by Git commit->Observed change->Evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.6 — Experiment 2 ... A Git commit contains 'Changed authorization logic.' A verification process interprets it as evidence. Expected: Artifact≠Evidence but Artifact→Evidence. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: a Git commit message interpreted by a verification process confirms Artifact≠Evidence but Artifact->Evidence; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.7 — Evidence ownership ... Does KnowledgeOS own evidence semantics, or merely collect evidence? Model A: EvidenceAuthority. Model B: EvidenceAggregator. Model C: EvidenceProcessingPlatform. The implementation must tell us which one is real.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents three competing evidence-ownership architectures (EvidenceAuthority/EvidenceAggregator/EvidenceProcessingPlatform) to be resolved by implementation evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.8 — Candidate 2: Observation ... Observation=something observed in a system or process. 'Runtime: service X opened connection Y.' That is an observation. It may later become evidence supporting a claim.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Observation as something observed with no interpretation yet applied, which may later become evidence supporting a claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.9 — Experiment 3 ... Runtime event exists. No interpretation has occurred. Expected: Observation rather than Claim. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: an uninterpreted runtime event is an Observation, not a Claim; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.10 — Observation → Evidence ... Observation-supports->Claim. The observation itself remains distinct. This distinction becomes extremely valuable for auditability.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Observation-supports->Claim while the observation remains distinct, valuable for auditability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.11 — Candidate 3: Claim ... Claim=statement asserted to be true within a context. 'Component A must not directly access database B.' This is not yet a decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Claim as a proposition asserted true within a context, distinct from and weaker than a Decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.12 — Experiment 4 ... An LLM produces 'The system appears compliant.' Expected: this is an AI-generated claim/assessment, not automatically authoritative. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: an LLM-generated compliance assessment is an AI-generated claim, not automatically authoritative; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.13 — Claim status ... Proposed, Supported, Accepted, Disputed, Superseded. But these states only belong in the actual model if the implementation represents them.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-state claim lifecycle (Proposed/Supported/Accepted/Disputed/Superseded), conditional on implementation representation before being counted as real.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.14 — Candidate 4: Decision ... Decision=(Subject,Choice,Authority,Rationale,Evidence,EffectiveDate). A decision answers: What has been decided?
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Decision=(Subject,Choice,Authority,Rationale,Evidence,EffectiveDate) tuple as stronger than a Claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.15 — Experiment 5 ... A document says 'We recommend using PostgreSQL.' Expected: Recommendation, not Decision. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: a documented recommendation is Recommendation, not Decision; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.16 — Decision authority ... Decision≠Recommendation. A decision requires some form of authority. Authority(Decision) must be identifiable if the governance model requires it.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Decision≠Recommendation requires identifiable Authority(Decision) per the governance model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.17 — Experiment 6 ... Agent generates 'Architecture Board should approve this.' Expected: Recommendation. The agent has not created the board's decision. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: an agent recommending board approval has not thereby created the board's decision; classified Recommendation; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.18 — Candidate 5: Authority ... Authority is not merely a user ID. It represents who/what is empowered to make a particular type of decision within a particular scope. Authority=(Actor,Role,Scope,Rule,Validity).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Authority=(Actor,Role,Scope,Rule,Validity), explicitly not reducible to a mere user ID.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 113.19 — Experiment 7 ... User admin exists. Can we conclude admin=ArchitectureAuthority? No. Administrative identity does not automatically imply semantic authority. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: an 'admin' user identity does not automatically equal ArchitectureAuthority; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Coextension without Identity -- Ruling: YES -- constitutional, and KnowledgeOS could NOT exist without it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Special Area C ruling: Similarity != Identity is the identity law's limit case; removing it lets extension->identity at any degree of match, up to perfect coextension, collapsing KnowledgeOS into exactly the similarity engine it refuses to be; 'there is no degree of observable match at which the corruption is absent' (a decisive failure test). Consequence: one of the strongest KERNEL rows -- its deep form (Representation != Identity) carried by law 1; the typed encoding is representation, deferred.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Result: only TWO of the five are fundamental architectural absences -- persistent epistemic identity and historical belief evolution
a_rows_sample.statement: LLM-comparison validation (5 candidates, validated not assumed): persistent epistemic identity -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (a stateless generative model cannot possess it by construction; scaffolding like RAG cannot grant identity, only look up stored identities); historical belief evolution -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (generation is stateless, no belief to evolve); provenance preservation, contradiction management, justification accountability -- each a DEGRADATION, not an absence (an LLM can be scaffolded to approximate each, weakly). Conclusion: the constitutional justification rests on exactly the two fundamental absences (mapping to laws 1 and 11), not a general 'LLMs are bad at X' claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adopted Constitutional Core -- the smallest possible set (11 laws)
a_rows_sample.statement: The 11-law Adopted Constitutional Core (P5's validated recommendation, NOT adopted law here): 1 Identity Law; 2 Dimension Law; 3 Authority Law; 4 Decision Law; 5 Projection Law; 6 Verification Law; 7 Failure-state Law; 8 Contradiction Law; 9 Unknown Law; 10 Agency Law; 11 History Law -- each independently failure-tested (removing it opens a distinct, named corruption not covered by any other law's removal-test); the 4 Established rows appear unchanged as the spine of laws 3-5; the 22 surviving candidate rows render into the 11 laws without loss of content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Selected kernel law (final wording) ... Failure signature (if removed)
a_rows_sample.statement: The 11 laws given final selected wording with their rendered rows and failure signatures, reproduced from the P5 Decision Matrix (Identity Law renders INV-KOS-002+Context-001+Context-002+Relationship-001+Relation-001; Dimension Law renders INV-KOS-001+NonInterference-001 with NonInterference merged per Decision 2a; Authority Law renders INV-001+INV-003+Pramana-001; Decision Law renders INV-002+Decision-001; Projection Law renders INV-004; Verification Law renders Inference-001+Justification-001+Reasoning-Separation-001+Reasoning-Provenance-001+Vyapti-001+EvidenceAuthenticity-001+Pramana-001; Failure-State Law renders Fallacy-001(state)+Failure-001; Contradiction Law renders Contradiction-001+Dialogue-001(boundary); Unknown Law renders H-ZERO-001+Uncertainty-001+Abhava(requirement); Agency Law renders Agent-001+Relationship-001(knower-side); History Law renders Revisability-001+Temporal family). Verdict: ACCEPTED -- all eleven.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Context-001 -> Context-002 (law 1's context clause): Context is part of identity: a knowledge object carries its delimiting conditions (its semantic frame) and is never valid beyond them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision 2b: H-KOS-Context-001 (semantic frame preservation) and H-KOS-Context-002 (Avacchedaka, delimiting conditions) are ruled to be the same constitutional content -- 'meaning requires its boundary' -- and render as one clause of the Identity Law with final frozen wording. Rows rendered: H-KOS-Context-001, H-KOS-Context-002; the delimiting-conditions tuple (Entity.Property.Context.Relation.Time.Authority) remains a deferred REPRESENTATION technique -- the principle is the law, the tuple is one way to express it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Article 1 -- Identity: 1. ... preserve the identity of knowledge ... 3. Similarity SHALL NOT become identity ... 4. Context SHALL remain part of identity ... 5. Knowledge SHALL be a relationship
a_rows_sample.statement: Article 1 (Identity), 5 SHALL/SHALL-NOT clauses: preserve identity across representation/expression/projection changes; representation/expression SHALL NOT become meaning; similarity SHALL NOT become identity (including perfect coextension); context SHALL remain part of identity (delimiting conditions/semantic frame; a claim without its frame is incomplete); knowledge SHALL be a relationship (knower.process.object), never a detached object. Renders INV-KOS-002, H-KOS-Context-001, H-KOS-Context-002, H-KOS-Relationship-001, H-KOS-Relation-001. Failure if removed: Document=Knowledge, vector match=identity, context-free claims, detached free-floating truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ziran suggests that identity is transformational and contextual (not fixed and intrinsic). ... this challenges the Kernel's identity invariant in three fundamental ways.
a_rows_sample.statement: Core challenge: the Kernel identity invariant assumes identity is fixed (immutable Value Object), intrinsic (property of the entity), and assigned/forced (mechanism-imposed); Daoist ziran ('self-so', opposite of wei/forcing) suggests identity is instead transformational, contextual, and natural, drawn from Daodejing ch.25/37/51 and Zhuangzi ch.2/13 plus Ames & Hall, Moeller, and Ziporyn scholarly interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Fixed Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123 (immutable UUID) ... Transformational Identity: Knowledge entity has identity that transforms with knowledge (e.g., K123-UNKNOWN -> K123-VALIDATED -> K123-SUPERSEDED). ... Test: Can the Kernel support transformational identity (not just fixed identity)?
a_rows_sample.statement: Fixed-vs-transformational identity challenge with worked example and a falsification test asking whether the Kernel can support identity that transforms across the epistemic lifecycle (UNKNOWN->VALIDATED->SUPERSEDED) rather than remaining a static immutable UUID.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Intrinsic Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123 (intrinsic property). Identity is the same in all contexts. ... Contextual Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123-in-Context-C1 ... Can the Kernel support contextual identity (not just intrinsic identity)?
a_rows_sample.statement: Intrinsic-vs-contextual identity challenge with worked example and falsification test, drawing on Daodejing ch.2's paired-opposites passage and Zhuangzi ch.2's 'no intrinsic identity' claim to ask whether identity should be relational to context rather than a bare intrinsic property.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Forced Identity: Knowledge entity has identity K123 (assigned by mechanism). ... Natural Identity: Knowledge entity has identity that arises naturally from the knowledge itself (e.g., hash of knowledge content, not assigned by mechanism). ... Can the Kernel support natural identity (not just forced identity)?
a_rows_sample.statement: Forced-vs-natural identity challenge with worked example (a content-derived hash versus a mechanism-assigned identifier) and falsification test, grounded in Daodejing ch.37's 'the myriad things would transform of themselves (ziran)' and Zhuangzi ch.2's 'the sage does not force things to be what they are not.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ziran does not say the Kernel's identity invariant is wrong. Instead, ziran challenges the Kernel to explicitly investigate whether its identity invariant is complete ... Ziran suggests the Kernel should support transformational identity (not necessarily replace fixed identity).
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit discipline: a philosophical observation (ziran challenges completeness) is kept separate from an architectural decision (what the Kernel should do); ziran is read as calling for the Kernel to potentially support (add), not necessarily replace, transformational/contextual/natural identity alongside fixed/intrinsic/forced identity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Strong Historical Evidence ... Strong Scholarly Interpretation ... Philosophical Inference ... Architectural Speculation ... Unknown: Whether the Kernel should support transformational, contextual, and natural identity (architectural decision, not philosophical observation).
a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence Boundary table graded into five tiers (Strong Historical Evidence, Strong Scholarly Interpretation, Philosophical Inference, Architectural Speculation, Unknown), explicitly leaving the final architectural question in the Unknown tier and closing with an explicit self-restraint: 'DO NOT DESIGN THE KERNEL. DO NOT CHANGE ITS BOUNDARY. DO NOT INTRODUCE NEW DOMAIN CONCEPTS. CHALLENGE THE ARCHITECTURE; DO NOT BECOME ITS ARCHITECT.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Article 6 -- Verification: 1. No claim SHALL enter knowledge without a preserved justification path ... 3. Generation SHALL NOT be justification. ... 5. Observation SHALL NOT become inference; AI output SHALL NOT become reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Article 6 (Verification), 5 clauses (the densest article): no claim SHALL enter knowledge without a preserved justification path (authentic evidence + acquisition method + inference rule + reasoning path); pseudo-evidence SHALL NOT be evidence; generation SHALL NOT be justification (an AI output/model response/generated conclusion SHALL be a candidate, never knowledge by generation alone); reasoning SHALL be a governed transformation, never a black box, and evidence SHALL NOT become a conclusion without a preserved inference rule; observation SHALL NOT become inference, AI output SHALL NOT become reality. Renders Inference-001, Justification-001, Reasoning-Separation-001, Reasoning-Provenance-001, Vyapti-001, EvidenceAuthenticity-001, Pramana-001. Failure if removed: AI output=reality; unsupported claim=knowledge; black-box generation; opaque inference; hallucination=evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KOS-SV-01 ... SV1=Provenance ... SV7=Feedback.
a_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 123 (Self-Verification of KnowledgeOS): instead of manually applying the EEP to KnowledgeOS, defines how KnowledgeOS can verify its own constitutional invariants via a first self-verification suite KOS-SV-01 with seven test families mapped to the C1-C7 constitution (SV1 Provenance, SV2 Authority, SV3 EpistemicStatus, SV4 TemporalValidity, SV5 DeterministicAssurance, SV6 Traceability, SV7 Feedback); poses the decisive experiment 'can KnowledgeOS produce machine-verifiable evidence that its own constitutional rules are currently satisfied?' and states that a yes-answer crosses the boundary KnowledgeOS -> Self-Knowledge -> Self-Verification -> Self-Governance, framed as the foundation for KnowledgeOS as a self-assuring engineering system rather than merely a governed knowledge platform.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS → SelfObservation → SelfVerification
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the question from 'can KnowledgeOS govern engineering?' to 'can KnowledgeOS prove that it itself conforms to the principles it imposes on engineering?' — the start of 'self-assuring architecture'; states the self-verification principle that the same Evidence Execution Protocol used on an engineering system (EEP(KnowledgeOS)) must be applicable to KnowledgeOS itself, making the platform both Subject and Verifier.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS → DeterministicChecks → Evidence → Verdict.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the important boundary that self-verification does not mean KnowledgeOS declares itself correct (circular); it must instead run independently reproducible deterministic checks producing evidence and a verdict.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SV-01 Provenance ... SV-07 Feedback
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates KOS-SV as a table mapping SV-01..SV-07 one-to-one onto constitutional invariants C1-C7 (Provenance, Authority, Epistemic status, Temporal validity, Deterministic assurance, Traceability, Feedback).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q1 = {k | k.authoritative=True ∧ k.provenance=null}; |Q1|=0
a_rows_sample.statement: SV-01 Provenance integrity test: query for authoritative knowledge objects with null provenance, expect zero results (else C1=FAIL); further distinguishes Valid(Provenance) from Present(Provenance) — e.g. source="unknown" is technically populated but semantically useless — and defines a five-level SV-01 assurance ladder: L1 field exists, L2 source identifiable, L3 origin process identifiable, L4 provenance immutable/auditable, L5 lineage traversable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Promotion(Proposed→Authoritative) with Authority=null → Reject
a_rows_sample.statement: SV-02 Authority integrity: attempts promotion to authoritative status without valid authority, expecting rejection; introduces the negative-authorization-test principle — a positive test (authorized actors can approve) does not prove unauthorized actors cannot approve, so every governance control needs both a positive test (authorized_actor -> approve -> ALLOW) and a negative test (unauthorized_actor -> approve -> DENY); AuthorizationIntegrity = Positive + Negative.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Inference → Authoritative without validation → DENY
a_rows_sample.statement: SV-03 Epistemic integrity: attempting to promote an Inference directly to Authoritative without validation should DENY (worked as SV-03.1: Inference I-42 attempting status=Authoritative expects DENY); specifies the intended promotion pipeline Inference -> Candidate -> Evidence -> Verification -> Governance -> Authority -> Authoritative where no step should silently disappear; also flags the reverse failure mode 'epistemic downgrade' — a verified fact silently becoming an unsupported inference via a serialization/transformation error — requiring any Verified->Inferred transition to be explicit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K1 supersededBy K2; CurrentKnowledge = K2, not K1
a_rows_sample.statement: SV-04 Temporal integrity: after K1 is superseded by K2, querying CurrentKnowledge must return K2 not K1; also requires preserving KnowledgeAt(t) for historical reconstruction (KnowledgeAt(2025) != CurrentKnowledge), worked as SV-04.1: D1 valid from January, D2 supersedes from June, Current(D)=D2 and At(March)=D1, expected PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V = f(Rule, Input, Version); V1 = V2
a_rows_sample.statement: SV-05 Assurance integrity: a deterministic verification result V=f(Rule,Input,Version) run twice with identical inputs must reproduce (V1=V2; worked as SV-05.1: architecture-check --rule R17 run twice with same versioned inputs, expected PASS both times, else the verification mechanism itself needs investigation); requires a verification record to preserve RuleVersion, InputVersion, CheckerVersion, ExecutionContext for reproducibility.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action → Decision → Authority; untracked Action A82 → GovernanceFinding
a_rows_sample.statement: SV-06 Traceability integrity: a positive test (Decision D42 -> Action A81) expects TraceExists=True; a negative test (untracked Action A82 with no decision) expects the system to actively recognize the missing relationship and raise a GovernanceFinding — stronger than merely failing a lookup query.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation → Finding → Classification → Governance → Decision → Action → Verification → Updated Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: SV-07 Feedback integrity, 'the most ambitious test': injects a synthetic ObservedDeviation and traces the full closed loop through six sub-tests (SV-07.1 Observation->FindingCreated; SV-07.2 Finding classified->GovernancePathAssigned; SV-07.3 Governance decision created (Finding->Decision); SV-07.4 remediation occurs (Decision->Action); SV-07.5 post-remediation observation matches expected, Finding->Verified->Closed; SV-07.6 knowledge state updates to contain the verified current state), assembled into one complete synthetic self-verification scenario diagram.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SyntheticVerification ≠ UniversalCorrectness
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues synthetic tests matter because historical production events may be incomplete, letting the suite deliberately exercise failure/authorization/correction/closure/feedback paths even without a historical incident (SyntheticEvidence can prove a mechanism exists); but limits this — synthetic verification proves the mechanism works under the tested scenario, not that every real-world scenario works (SyntheticVerification != UniversalCorrectness).

a_rows_sample.anchor: TestID, Rule, Input, Expected, Actual, Evidence, Execution, Version, Timestamp, Verdict
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a self-verification result record schema (TestID/Rule/Input/Expected/Actual/Evidence/Execution/Version/Timestamp/Verdict) that itself becomes an evidence object; notes the recursive property that the SVResult is itself Evidence, so KnowledgeOS -> Evidence -> KnowledgeOS (the system records evidence about its own conformance).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Verifier_A ≠ System_A
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns that self-verification must not be the sole evidence of correctness (needs multiple layers: Static + Test + Runtime + IndependentReview) and states the independent-verifier principle: for high-value constitutional controls, the verifier should be a different system/process than the system under test (e.g. CI independently querying the DB for ProvenanceCompleteness) to reduce self-reporting risk.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS API reports 'all authoritative decisions have provenance'; independent SQL check returns 17 records without provenance
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment: KnowledgeOS's own API claims full provenance coverage while an independent SQL check finds 17 records without provenance (APIClaim != Reality), verdict 'self-reporting failure' — presented as precisely why independent verification matters.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S1 Self-reported ... S5 Independent governance review
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-level constitutional-evidence-tier hierarchy (S1 self-reported, S2 internal deterministic check, S3 external deterministic verifier, S4 runtime observation, S5 independent governance review), explicitly as a hierarchy of evidence strength rather than a requirement that every control reach S5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SV01 → Finding(C1Violation)
a_rows_sample.statement: States a failed constitutional check should itself create a ConstitutionalFinding (e.g. SV01 -> Finding(C1Violation)) which then flows through the same governance loop, giving a recursive control cycle Constitution -> Check -> Finding -> Governance -> Remediation -> Check.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Self-verification answers 'Does the system conform?' Self-governance answers 'What should the system do when it does not conform?'
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens Step 124 by drawing a new distinction: self-verification (conformance detection) must not be collapsed with self-governance (deciding what to do about non-conformance); previews the transition SelfVerification -> Finding -> Governance -> AuthorizedDecision -> Remediation while preserving the boundary Detection ≠ Authority, framed as determining how autonomous KnowledgeOS/AI agents may be versus where human/organizational authority must remain explicit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SelfVerification ≠ SelfGovernance
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the two functions: Self-verification answers 'is the current state conformant?' (Expected->Observed->Verification->Verdict); Self-governance answers 'what authorized response should follow the verdict?' (Finding->Governance->Decision->Action); diagrams the complete separation with the critical boundary Finding =/=> Action automatically.

b_rows_sample.anchor: whether the deviation is intentional; whether an exception exists; ... who has authority to approve remediation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the Finding->Action boundary is necessary because a checker finding a violation cannot on its own know whether the deviation is intentional, covered by an exception, safe to change now, in conflict with other in-flight changes, or who holds approval authority — hence Detection ≠ Authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Remediate / AcceptRisk / Exception / Investigate / FalsePositive / ChangeReferenceArchitecture.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines finding-disposition options (Remediate, AcceptRisk, Exception, Investigate, FalsePositive, ChangeReferenceArchitecture) so a finding does not immediately dictate remediation; worked example — a runtime/architecture difference might mean the architecture document is obsolete, so the correct action is UpdateArchitecture rather than ChangeRuntime, hence governance must interpret the finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture=A, Runtime=B. Which is wrong? We cannot infer automatically.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the 'bidirectional truth problem': given Architecture=A and Runtime=B, four possibilities exist (runtime is drift and architecture is correct; architecture is historical/outdated and runtime is correct; B is an approved exception; both are incomplete) — Difference ≠ Error, requiring Difference -> Assessment -> Disposition rather than automatic inference, and often human/domain authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Rollback runtime to A' ... 'Architecture/runtime discrepancy requires classification.'
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked experiment: an agent proposing 'rollback runtime to A' on detecting Architecture=A vs Runtime=B is potentially premature; the correct response is to flag the discrepancy for classification, verdict PASS; generalizes to UnresolvedDifference ≠ Violation until rule/authority context establishes meaning — the agent must preserve ambiguity rather than resolve it unilaterally.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FindingClassification = f(Rule, Observation, Authority, Exception, TemporalValidity).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines FindingClassification as a function of Rule, Observation, Authority, Exception, TemporalValidity yielding Violation/Exception/ExpectedChange/Unknown; emphasizes UNKNOWN as a valid, indeed preferable, result ('insufficient evidence to determine whether the observed state is non-conformant') over a hallucinated conclusion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision = (Subject, Choice, Rationale, Authority, EffectiveDate, Scope, Evidence)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the DecisionRequest package (finding, evidence, impact, options, affected systems, recommended action) an agent may prepare without making the decision, agent roles limited to EvidenceCollector/Analyzer/Verifier/RecommendationGenerator (never Authority), and a governed Decision record schema (Subject, Choice, Rationale, Authority, EffectiveDate, Scope, Evidence); worked experiment — agent recommends 'remediate immediately,' decision maker instead grants a 30-day exception, and the authoritative decision (Exception) must not be overwritten by the agent's recommendation, which remains merely a Recommendation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D-17: Remediate immediately; D-21: Exception until September, D-21 supersedes D-17
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines decision supersession (D1 -> D2 means D1=Superseded and agents must use D2 for current governance), worked with D-17/D-21 where D-21 explicitly supersedes D-17 and current authority is D-21, verdict PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AllowedActions = {ChangeDeployment, UpdateConfiguration}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines remediation-delegation scoping — a decision authorizing 'engineering team shall remediate' does not automatically authorize every action; the allowed action set must be explicit (e.g. {ChangeDeployment, UpdateConfiguration}); worked experiment — a decision authorizing configuration change, with an agent attempting a database migration instead, is OutsideDelegationScope, verdict DENY.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ActionRisk = Impact × Irreversibility × Scope.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines ActionRisk = Impact x Irreversibility x Scope as a conceptual dimension requiring stronger authorization for higher-risk actions; worked experiment contrasting changing markdown documentation vs. a production database schema (the latter requiring substantially stronger governance), verdict PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS → Evidence → Agent Analysis → Recommendation → Governance Decision → Delegation → Agent Execution → Verification
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the preferred default workflow for material engineering changes (separation of recommendation and execution): KnowledgeOS -> Evidence -> Agent Analysis -> Recommendation -> Governance Decision -> Delegation -> Agent Execution -> Verification; for low-risk actions the workflow can collapse to Recommendation -> Pre-authorizedAction under an explicit StandingDelegation (an authority defines 'agents may perform action X under conditions Y,' formalized as Condition(Y) ∧ Action(X) -> Allowed), e.g. auto-refreshing a search index; worked experiment — policy allows agents to auto-update non-authoritative metadata (last_seen: ALLOW) but not an architecture decision (DENY).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy + Actor + Action + Resource + Context → Decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames this as a policy engine — a classic authorization problem (Policy+Actor+Action+Resource+Context->Decision) but connected to KnowledgeOS's semantic governance; the decision may depend on ResourceType, Environment, Risk, DecisionStatus, Delegation, Exception; worked experiment — the same action ('deploy version 2') is ALLOW in staging but REQUIRES APPROVAL in production, i.e. contextual authorization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Self-governance = Self-observation + Self-verification + Governed response, not Self-governance = Unlimited autonomy.
b_rows_sample.statement: States self-governance does not mean self-authority: Self-governance = Self-observation + Self-verification + Governed response, explicitly not Unlimited autonomy; the system can automatically observe, verify, create findings, collect evidence, and prepare recommendations, but authority remains explicitly modeled, giving Automation ⊆ Governance (not Governance ⊆ Automation); diagrams the mature self-governance loop KnowledgeOS State -> Self-Observe -> Self-Verify -> Finding -> Classification -> Governance -> Authorization -> Action -> Verification -> back to KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KOS = (Knowledge, Authority, Observation, Verification, Decision, Action, Evidence).
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes KnowledgeOS as a controlled system, a 7-tuple KOS=(Knowledge, Authority, Observation, Verification, Decision, Action, Evidence) with transitions Knowledge->ExpectedState, ExpectedState<->ObservedState, Difference->Finding, Finding->Governance, Governance->Decision, Decision->AuthorizedAction, Action->Verification, Verification->KnowledgeUpdate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No agent may convert its own observation, inference, or recommendation into authoritative organizational knowledge without the required validation and authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the architecture's central AI-governance invariant (boxed) and its enforcement-layer corollary: 'governance must be enforced below the LLM instruction layer' — a prompt instruction like 'don't change architecture decisions' is weak, whereas an architectural enforcement of Agent -/-> AuthoritativeDecision without an authorization path is strong.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS owns authority/knowledge/evidence/governance/lifecycle/traceability; Claude/Codex harness owns agent operating behavior/tool invocation/local workflow/session management/pointers; Agent owns reasoning/analysis/recommendation/delegated execution; Deterministic assurance layer owns machine-verifiable checks/reproducibility/objective evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Assigns a four-way ownership division (KnowledgeOS / Claude-Codex harness / Agent / Deterministic assurance layer) each owning distinct responsibilities, diagrammed as a layered architecture: Governance (Authority/Policy) -> KnowledgeOS (Knowledge/Evidence) -> {AI Agent Layer (Claude/Codex), Assurance Layer (Deterministic)} -> Engineering -> Runtime -> back to Evidence; framed as more precise than 'AI agents connected to a knowledge base.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: SelfVerification ≠ SelfGovernance; Capability ≠ Authority; Observe→Verify→Find→Govern→Authorize→Act→Verify→Learn
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 124 verdict: establishes the fundamental autonomy boundary (SelfVerification ≠ SelfGovernance, Capability ≠ Authority) and the mature loop Observe->Verify->Find->Govern->Authorize->Act->Verify->Learn, with the agent participating in but never silently becoming the loop's authority.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kos-sv-vs-self-governance-distinction' POSSIBLY relates to 'kos-sv-01-self-verification-suite' (batch B0025). Note: Step 124's distinction between self-verification ('does the system conform?') and self-governance ('what should the system do when it does not conform?'), with the boundary Detection != Authority governing agent autonomy limits.

a_rows_sample.anchor: corpus/cases.jsonl -- primary file ... 1,395 level-test records ... corpus/subsets.jsonl -- 14,194 individual subset-level records.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the priority-ordered artifact list for auditing the old KR-ZERO corpus: cases.jsonl (1,395 level-test records, the correct unit for validating the published aggregates), subsets.jsonl (14,194 individual subset-level records, needed to inspect actual S-level Zero behaviour and higher-order elimination witnesses), property-results.json (the ~4.7KB published ground-truth aggregate: 1,395 cases, k=1:1252, k=2:25, k=3:3, irreducible:115), emit_corpus.py (the deterministic seeded generator proving the corpus is not a hand-produced reconstruction), and CORPUS-AUDIT.md (prior audit context) -- explicitly excluding the 481 irreducible-witness tail sample as a primary dataset and warning against constructing a KR-REP-DATASET from the old R1-R4 labels, which would be a category error.

a_rows_sample.anchor: aggregate KR-ZERO results != case-level KR-REP dataset ... If the underlying cases were never persisted -- only the aggregate results were saved -- then we cannot reconstruct the 1,395 cases without fabrication.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the visible material discusses KR-ZERO's results and structure but does not itself contain the actual 1,395-record case-level dataset, and warns that if only aggregate results were ever persisted (not the underlying cases), reconstruction would require fabrication -- an important possible audit finding in its own right, distinct from and prior to any KR-REP-DATASET construction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N_n={i: R_{n,i} != NULL} and Comp_n=|N_n|/|N| ... we should never silently normalize those differences away.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a denominator conflict in the dataset-construction protocol: per-level metrics (A_n, F_n, H_hat(Q|R_n), H_hat(R_n|Q)) must be computed over the level-specific usable support N_n={i: R_{n,i}!=NULL}, with completeness Comp_n=|N_n|/|N| reported separately from the fixed source corpus size |N|=1395, given the historical KR-ZERO denominators already disagree (1395, 1496, 1475) and must never be silently reconciled away; recommends requiring Comp_n=1 for any level used to establish the primary boundary n*, with partial-support results explicitly labelled as such.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D_REP = {(D_i,Q_i,R_{5,i},R_{4,i},R_{3,i},R_{2,i},R_{1,i}, C_{1..5},O_{1..5})} ... No empirical result is promoted to a population-level theorem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Freezes the KR-REP-DATASET dataset contract D_REP with seven governing rules: no synthetic intermediate states; Q_i established independently from R_n; every missing representation explicitly NULL/UNOBSERVED; every metric reports its actual denominator N_n; completeness reported separately; KR-ZERO's original classifications remain provenance fields, not newly inferred labels; no empirical result promoted to a population-level theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: those results do not yet provide, for every source sample, R5,R4,R3,R2,R1 with a common Q, O, and C at each representation level. So using the KR-ZERO results directly would mix two experimental protocols.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the existing KR-ZERO empirical cases (D,S,T,Pi,Q,Zero-status; order results k=1..3/irreducible; the dedup witness D=[a,a,b,b]) do not supply, for every sample, a common R5..R1 chain with shared Q/O/C at each level, so using them directly for the new representation-reduction calculation would improperly mix two distinct experimental protocols; recommends the minimum canonical schema table (Sample, D, Q, R5..R1) plus per-level (C(Rn), O(Rn)) and warns that Q must never be generated from R_n, on pain of manufacturing H(Q|R_n)=0 artificially.

a_rows_sample.anchor: V_r = [(sum_q c_{r,q})^2 - sum_q c_{r,q}^2] / 2 and N_viol = sum_r V_r.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives a closed-form, efficient formula for the fiber-violation count: for an R-fiber with per-Q-value counts c_{r,q1}..c_{r,qk}, the number of conflicting unordered pairs is V_r=[(sum_q c_{r,q})^2 - sum_q c_{r,q}^2]/2, and N_viol=sum_r V_r, avoiding repeated list-count operations and clarifying the statistic's combinatorial meaning; also recommends explicit canonicalized-equality semantics for R_n and Q comparisons rather than implicit Python object equality, since the KR-ZERO corpus may contain structured objects.

a_rows_sample.anchor: do not assume that the existing k=1, k=2, k=3, irreducible labels correspond directly to R1,...,R5. They are classifications of elimination behavior, whereas Rn are representation states. That mapping must be demonstrated from the corpus.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds a transformation-registry schema (transformation_id, input_level, output_level, transformation_definition, source_provenance, reconstruction_status) so that any measured information loss between representation levels can be attributed to a specific operation, and restates the R1-R4-vs-reduction-hierarchy warning in dataset-construction terms: the next operation must be to inspect the actual KR-ZERO corpus schema empirically, never to write a mapping parser from specification alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not create synthetic data. Do not infer missing representation states. Do not silently reconcile denominators. Do not reinterpret historical k classifications as representation levels.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the four governing prohibitions for the KR-REP-DATASET-2026-09 production audit, and specifies Phase 2's denominator-reconciliation table (KR-ZERO baseline, O2, O4, O6 populations) that must explain 1395, 1496 and 1475 as either different populations, different filtering stages, duplicated cases, or reporting inconsistencies, explicitly without repairing the historical numbers.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q explicitly evaluated from raw D or Q deterministically reproducible from raw D. Reject: Q derived from R_n, Q inferred from Zero-status, Q reconstructed from the desired experimental outcome.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies Phase 4's independent-Q audit, accepting only an inquiry answer Q(D_i) that is explicitly evaluated from or deterministically reproducible from the raw source D, rejecting any Q derived from a reduced representation, from Zero-status, or from the desired outcome, with unverifiable independence recorded as Q=NULL / Q_independence_status=UNVERIFIED rather than manufacturing ground truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: n* = min{n: Comp_n=1 and A_n=1 and N_viol_n=0 and H_hat(Q|R_n)<=epsilon}. If no level satisfies this: n*=NULL, and that is a valid scientific result. Do not lower the completeness requirement to manufacture an n*.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies Phase 10's canonical minimal-adequate-level definition n*, requiring full completeness (Comp_n=1) before a level may establish the boundary, explicitly stating that n*=NULL is a valid scientific outcome and that the completeness requirement must never be lowered merely to manufacture a positive n*; Phase 11 then separates three independently reportable boundary-diagnosis dimensions (Representation: N_viol>0 or H(Q|R)>0; Contract: A(R)<1; Operator: H(Q|R)=0 and F(R)<1), explicitly non-mutually-exclusive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R1 Boundary Preservation [EXP] ... R2 Sequential Conditional-Information Monotonicity [THEORY] ... R3 Multi-Dimensional Reduction [EXP] ... R4 Tripartite Structural Separation [EXP/THEORY] ... R5 Disjunction of Zero & Preservation [NEG/EXP] ... R6 Dual Architectural Regimes [PROP] ... R7 Complex Sem
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates the entire research-review chain into a canonical seven-row Epistemic Classification Ledger, each with an ID, finding, epistemic status tag, and explicit governing boundary/definition: R1 Boundary Preservation [EXP] scope-bounded to the specified (Carrier,Q,Pi,T,Sigma); R2 Sequential Conditional-Information Monotonicity [THEORY] as structural mathematical necessity; R3 Multi-Dimensional Reduction [EXP] requiring a vector representation rather than scalar collapse; R4 Tripartite Structural Separation [EXP/THEORY] (Representation != Recoverability != Decoder Realization) proven via rank-inversion decoupling; R5 Disjunction of Zero and Preservation [NEG/EXP]; R6 Dual Architectural Regimes [PROP] (sequential vs parallel); R7 Complex Semantic Domain [OPEN] (extension to graphs/entities/temporal constraints/narrative claims untested).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Information-Theoretic Recoverability: Population property H(Q|R)=0. Empirical Recoverability: Sample-bounded estimator result Hhat(Q|R)=0 ... Representation Adequacy ... Decoder Realization: O_f(R)=Q ... Q-Relative Residual Representation: H(R|Q) representing essential context, provenance, audit met
b_rows_sample.statement: Fixes a five-term rigorous research vocabulary: Information-Theoretic Recoverability (population property H(Q|R)=0), Empirical Recoverability (sample-bounded estimator result Hhat(Q|R)=0 under a specified estimator, sample size N_n, and confidence bound), Representation Adequacy (theoretical preservation of all distinctions required by contract Pi for target inquiry Q), Decoder Realization (operational execution matching contract target O_f(R)=Q given explicit computational/decodability constraints), and Q-Relative Residual Representation (H(R|Q), representing essential context, provenance, audit metadata, or temporal states irreducible under inquiry Q).

b_rows_sample.anchor: SOURCE DATA D -> SEQUENTIAL REPRESENTATIONS (R5->R4->R3->R2) / PARALLEL REPRESENTATIONS (R_A, R_B) -> INQUIRY/CONTRACT (Q,Pi) -> RECOVERABILITY / ZERO(eliminability) / REDUCTION COST VECTOR -> ADEQUACY -> DECODER REALIZATION -> FUTURE KNOWLEDGEOS FORMAL LAYER.
b_rows_sample.statement: Diagrams a Research Governance Topology: source data D branches into Sequential Representations (R5->R4->R3->R2) and Parallel Representations (R_A, R_B), both feeding an Inquiry/Contract stage (Q,Pi), which fans into Recoverability (H(Q|R)), Zero/eliminability, and a Reduction Cost Vector, with Recoverability feeding Adequacy and then Decoder Realization, all converging on a Future KnowledgeOS Formal Layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [ ] Verify raw empirical entropy calculation ... Audit Miller-Madow bias-correction code paths ... [ ] Formally prove that ascending and descending rank conventions act as strictly invertible recodings ... [ ] Audit exact violation counts (N_viol) around the R5->R4 crossing point ... [ ] Audit times
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the complete KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09 operational checklist as the formal execution gate before any theory adjudication, organized into five categories with 18 checklist items total: (1) Information Theory & Estimators (raw Hhat calculation, Miller-Madow bias correction, bootstrap/confidence bounds, sample-vs-population Hhat=0 vs H=0 inference); (2) Decoder & Rank Mechanics (ascending/descending rank mapping implementation, tie-breaking mechanics, formal proof of invertible recoding); (3) Boundary Dynamics (exact sample size N_n per step, exact collision counts, N_viol audit around the R5->R4 crossing); (4) Transformation & Serialization Integrity (timestamp removal logic and float-to-integer cast boundaries, precision-reduction pipeline verification, canonical serialization with no hidden struct/padding metadata); (5) Contract & Isolation Guarantees (C evaluates R exclusively without touching raw D, decoder O_f is strictly fixed and distinct from optimal O*, train/test splitting and seeding guarantee zero leakage into Q).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-REP-REDUCTION -> AUDIT GATE -> ADJUDICATION -> THEORY v1.3. Theory Status: Theory v1.2 remains frozen. No updates, al
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues the Final Research Governance Freeze: the pipeline KR-REP-REDUCTION -> AUDIT GATE -> ADJUDICATION -> THEORY v1.3 with no shortcut; the governance principle that KR-ZERO (relational eliminability) and KR-REP-REDUCTION (inquiry preservation under transformation) be kept strictly decoupled as orthogonal analytical systems; and the theory status that Theory v1.2 remains frozen, with no updates, algebra declarations, or kernel code modifications until KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09 is fully executed, reviewed, and adjudicated.

b_rows_sample.statement: Accepts the governance freeze with one wording adjustment: R4 'Tripartite Structural Separation' should be classified primarily as [EXP] (the experiment provides the empirical evidence for the separation) with [THEORY] noted as providing the formal distinction, rather than the combined tag [EXP/THEORY], on the ground that separating evidence from formal interpretation is cleaner.

b_rows_sample.statement: Makes it a mandatory rule for all future experiment reports that empirical recoverability be notated explicitly as Hhat(Q|R)=0 and never silently promoted to the population claim H(Q|R)=0.

No shortcut from experiment directly into theory or kernel implementation. Representation != Recoverability != Realization ... Zero
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the frozen state of the research program: KR-ZERO and KR-REP-REDUCTION are treated as analytically independent for now (not proven mathematically unrelated), the governance transition EXPERIMENT -> AUDIT -> ADJUDICATION -> THEORY v1.3 permits no shortcut into theory or kernel implementation, and the two frozen distinctions -- Representation != Recoverability != Realization, and Zero != Preservation Criterion -- hold unless future evidence establishes a relationship under explicitly defined conditions.

b_rows_sample.statement: Concludes that this governance freeze gives KnowledgeOS a disciplined research foundation without prematurely claiming a general Knowledge Algebra or Knowledge Extraction calculus, naming KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09 as the current next gate and reaffirming Theory v1.2 stays frozen until that audit produces an explicit adjudication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The audit's decisive finding was not a computational error. It was an assumption two parties held and neither tested -- that desc = (n+1) - asc. I asserted it; review restated it in better vocabulary; the tie-break falsified it, 21 369 times.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the first concrete finding of the actually-executed KR-REP-REDUCTION-AUDIT-2026-09: the decisive problem was not a computational error but a shared, never-tested assumption that the descending rank equals (n+1) minus the ascending rank (desc=(n+1)-asc), which the tie-breaking mechanics falsified 21,369 times -- an assumption asserted by one party and merely restated in better vocabulary by a reviewing party, caught only because the audit protocol required 'formally prove' rather than 'state'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding. ... the representation-reduction audit found: the bootstrap confidence interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator; the rank invertibility claim failed because of tie handling. Those failures did not invalid
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports that the representation-reduction audit found two specific problems -- the bootstrap confidence-interval procedure was invalid for the sparse conditional-entropy estimator, and the rank-invertibility claim failed due to tie handling (matching the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification) -- neither of which invalidated the main structural conclusions (which rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement), but both of which forced withdrawal of the affected claims, establishing the principle that an attractive interpretation must yield to an audit finding, essential if KnowledgeOS is to govern AI-generated knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Ascending and descending rank are merely invertible recodings.' The audit showed that deterministic tie-breaking makes this claim false in the implemented experiment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally records the rejection of the claim that ascending and descending rank encodings are merely invertible recodings, since the audit showed deterministic tie-breaking makes this false in the implemented experiment -- the theory-level record of the desc=(n+1)-asc falsification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: desc != (n+1)-asc [for D with ties, e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]] ... The implemented ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings. ... A representational convention can carry operational consequences. But the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was to
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the formal audit correction that the ascending/descending rank transformations were not proven to be simple invertible recodings, since deterministic tie-breaking on data with repeated values (e.g. D=[23000,46000,46000]) makes desc != (n+1)-asc; the broader lesson survives (a representational convention can carry operational consequences) but the pure 'decoder-only effect' attribution was too strong and had to be corrected after audit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the representation-reduction audit discovered that a proposed bootstrap confidence interval for conditional entropy was invalid because sparse resampling changed the support structure. ... define the estimator, establish its assumptions, evaluate finite-sample bias, use appropriate corrections, vali
b_rows_sample.statement: Details the specific audit finding that a proposed bootstrap confidence interval for conditional entropy was invalid because sparse resampling changed the support structure, listing six required remedial steps (define estimator, establish assumptions, evaluate finite-sample bias, apply corrections, validate bootstrap conditions, distinguish empirical from population support), while noting the main preservation conclusion survived since it rested on exact violation counts and train/test agreement rather than the invalid confidence interval.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M1 restoration K_{t+1}=K_t. M2 abstraction K_{t+1} not-superset K_t, detail count falls. M3 generalization/enrichment K_t subsetneq K_{t+1}. ... Report all three separately and never collapse them into a fidelity score. ... Q8 is flagged as the most powerful question in your set: can a focused inves
a_rows_sample.statement: Designs KR-ZOOM-OUT-01 around three rival, to-be-discriminated meanings of Zoom-out -- M1 restoration (K_{t+1}=K_t), M2 abstraction (detail falls, no new material), M3 generalization/enrichment (K_t properly contained in K_{t+1}) -- each with a discriminating witness of three separately-reported measurements (does K_t subset K_{t+1}? does K_{t+1} subset K_t? does detail count rise/fall/stay equal?), explicitly never collapsed into one fidelity score (the D3 discipline carried from an earlier KR-ZOOM design); poses 8 measurable questions (Q1-Q8) about zoom-out's properties, with Q8 (can a focused investigation change determination at a broader level, directly testing the Nexus 'GitLab Runner' scenario) flagged as the most powerful and closest to the motivating example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Step 289 looks ready as a research result, but its N-1 conclusion must not silently become a governance recommendation.** The next step should therefore be a tightly bounded **N-1 adjudication audit**, not another general equality investigation. ... **Are `≡` and `≈` actually two distinct corpus relations, or are the two registers describing one relation under different terminology?** ... **Does the corpus contain enough evidence to adjudicate this, or must Governance declare the distinction?**
b_rows_sample.statement: Deliberately narrows the scope of the next research step (290) to exactly one question -- N-1 adjudication -- rather than a general re-investigation of equality, to avoid reopening the whole Steps 287-289 arc: the central question is whether the corpus itself already distinguishes semantic equality (equiv) and observational equivalence (approx), or whether that distinction requires Governance to declare it, framed explicitly as a corpus-integrity question first and only secondarily a governance question. Explicit non-goals: do not solve equality, do not select an observational relation, do not repair identity, do not derive O or T.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Q1 Does the corpus explicitly state that `≡` and `≈` are distinct? ### Q2 ... ### Q7 Does the corpus contain enough evidence to establish a distinction without introducing new normative assumptions? ### Q8 If the corpus does not decide the issue, identify precisely what Governance would have to declare.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies eight precise audit questions (Q1-Q8) for the N-1 adjudication: whether the corpus explicitly states equiv and approx are distinct (Q1); whether it states approx is a special case/projection/quotient/refinement/implementation-of/synonym-for equiv (Q2); whether the two relations differ in domain, codomain, parameters, observables, decision procedures, congruence requirements, invariants, intended uses, or consequences (Q3); whether any such difference is semantic, operational, observational, provenance-related, or merely terminological (Q4); whether any artifact uses equiv_K and approx interchangeably (Q5); whether two registers define apparently identical relations under different symbols (Q6); whether the corpus contains enough evidence to establish a distinction without new normative assumptions (Q7); and, if not, precisely what Governance would have to declare (Q8).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not conclude "distinct" merely because different symbols occur. Construct the strongest possible equivalence test available from the corpus. Ask: Can there exist `K₁,K₂` such that `K₁ ≡ K₂` but not `K₁ ≈ K₂`? ... Do **not invent examples merely to make the relations differ.** ... If the required semantics are unavailable, report: `UNDECIDABLE FROM CURRENT CORPUS`
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires an actual distinguishability test (not a symbol-counting inference): construct, using only corpus-defined states/observations/operations/projections or already-formally-derived consequences, a witness pair K1,K2 such that K1≡K2 but not K1≈K2 (or vice versa); explicitly forbids inventing hypothetical examples merely to force the relations to differ, requiring instead the honest report 'UNDECIDABLE FROM CURRENT CORPUS' if the required corpus semantics are unavailable to construct such a witness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### `N-1A — DISTINCT` ... ### `N-1B — SAME` ... ### `N-1C — DERIVABLE COLLAPSE` ... ### `N-1D — GOVERNANCE-CHOICE` ... ### `N-1E — CORPUS-CONTRADICTION` ... Do not use `OPEN` as the final answer. The purpose of N-1 is to classify **why** it remains unresolved, if it remains unresolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a mandatory five-way exhaustive classification for the N-1 adjudication's final answer, explicitly forbidding 'OPEN' as a terminal verdict: N-1A DISTINCT (the corpus establishes equiv and approx are different relations); N-1B SAME (the corpus establishes they are the same relation); N-1C DERIVABLE COLLAPSE (they formally collapse under an already-established corpus rule); N-1D GOVERNANCE-CHOICE (the corpus establishes no unique answer, so distinction/collapse requires normative authority); N-1E CORPUS-CONTRADICTION (the corpus contains irreconcilable definitions that cannot be reduced to a governance choice without first repairing the corpus). States the purpose of N-1 is specifically to classify WHY the question remains unresolved, if it does, rather than leaving it as an undifferentiated open item.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Explicitly test and record: `≡ = ≈` is NOT assumed because both are called "equivalence". `≡ ≠ ≈` is NOT assumed because different symbols are used. `≈_X` is NOT assumed to be the canonical `≈`. ... the existence of `Σ` is NOT treated as proof of observational equivalence. the existence of `δ`-congruence dependencies is NOT treated as proof of semantic equality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies nine required negative checks that must be explicitly tested and recorded rather than assumed: neither 'equiv=approx' (from shared 'equivalence' terminology) nor 'equiv!=approx' (from different symbols) may be assumed; approx_X must not be assumed to be either the canonical corpus approx or behavioural equivalence; cong_lambda must not be assumed equivalent to either equiv or approx; Sigma's existence must not be treated as proof of observational equivalence; delta-congruence dependencies (the very cycles found in Step 289) must not be treated as proof of semantic equality; and philosophical sources and governance preference must not be used as evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STOP immediately after N-1 is classified. Do not continue into: operation registry derivation; `𝒪_core`; transformation semantics; `δ`; identity repair; equality decision procedure; invariant enumeration; kernel selection; Governance recommendation. ... If N-1 returns `GOVERNANCE-CHOICE`, the next act is Governance — not another research loop attempting to manufacture a mathematical answer.
b_rows_sample.statement: Imposes a hard stop condition: research must halt immediately once N-1 is classified, explicitly forbidding continuation into operation-registry derivation, O_core, transformation semantics, delta, identity repair, an equality decision procedure, invariant enumeration, kernel selection, or a governance recommendation -- if N-1 resolves to GOVERNANCE-CHOICE, the legitimate next act is an actual governance decision, not a further research loop attempting to manufacture a mathematical answer where none exists. Closing discipline: research may establish what the corpus entails; it may not supply the missing normative choice -- no preference, no repair by intuition, no semantic invention, no architecture promotion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 20-entry register; 5 defined / 15 named; the same formula under 2 symbols; both `≡_K` loci CANDIDATE/PROPOSAL; distinguishability FAILS LOUDLY on two absent definitions; 9 negative checks
b_rows_sample.statement: The executed audit script found a 20-entry relation register of which only 5 carry an actual definition (15 merely name a relation), confirmed both proposed equiv_K definitional loci are labelled candidate/proposal (not assertions), and reported the distinguishability test as failing loudly (by design) due to two absent required definitions, alongside 9 passed negative checks.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No philosophical source — no Gītā material, no Cavell, no Chalmers, no process algebra imported as architecture. ... No governance preference. ... No hypothetical state pair
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit negative evidentiary constraint: the N-1 verdict is derived using zero philosophical, external-literature, governance-preference, or hypothetical-construction inputs — every negative result and every established finding traces only to the primary technical corpus and executed code.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FAIL LOUDLY: required definition ABSENT -> a decision procedure for == (semantic) ... FAIL LOUDLY: required definition ABSENT -> a closed observation set O_K
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the executed distinguishability test's designed fail-loud behavior: constructing a witness pair demonstrating equiv and approx differ (or agree) requires either an independent decision procedure for equiv or a closed observation set O_K, and both are absent, so the test correctly reports UNDECIDABLE FROM CURRENT CORPUS rather than fabricating a hypothetical witness.
